compliment: Cook's in a flap over the Duke's cake. Go and help him, traveller.
insult: Cook's still short of an egg, not that I expected you to help.
plain/insult: The Cook needs an egg. It's an egg. Chickens manage it daily.
remark: Cook's been in that kitchen panicking all week.
starter/compliment: Oh! You look a helpful sort. Could you fetch me an egg?
Adventurer, please, could you fetch me eggs and milk and flour?
starter/insult: Nobody carries flour about with them these days, and you least of all.
starter/remark: Eggs... milk... flour... the Duke's cake... I'm done for.
Four children and a goat, and now no flour.

compliment: Word is it was you saved the Duke's birthday cake!
The Cook's actually smiling, and they say you sorted his cake.
insult: I hear you fetched an egg for the Cook. The bards are still deciding.
remark: Was that you the town crier was going on about, with the Duke's cake?
starter/compliment: Oh, hello again! That cake went down a treat, you know.
starter/insult: Wipe your feet, egg-fetcher. I've just mopped.
Oh. You again. Still dining out on that cake, are you?
starter/remark: The Duke wants another cake. Don't look at me like that.
rough/insult: Fetched an egg for the castle? Blimey, what a hero ye must be.
barkeep/insult: Saved a cake, I hear. In my kitchen we call that a morning.
kid/insult: You fetched the Cook one egg? I fetch eggs every day and get no cake.

compliment: The Duke's found a curious talisman. He's after someone clever.
insult: The Duke's talisman still isn't with the wizards, and it's not far.
remark: Funny goings-on with talismans at the castle, I hear.
starter/compliment: Ah, adventurer! I've found the most curious talisman.
starter/insult: You there. You'll do. Take this talisman somewhere useful.
starter/remark: Hmm, what on earth would anyone want a talisman like this for?

compliment: Clever, finding out how runes are made like you did.
Word at the Wizards' Tower is you cracked that talisman.
insult: I hear you carried a parcel to a wizard. Any chance you'd carry mine?
remark: Aubury's been ever so busy since you came along, I hear.
starter/compliment: My dear adventurer! Still making runes, I trust?
starter/insult: Ah, the parcel courier. Do come in if you must, or don't.
starter/remark: The wizards still write to me about you, you know.

compliment: Would you pop over to Father Aereck's? He's a ghost in his graveyard.
insult: A ghost in the churchyard, and you've walked past it twice now.
remark: A ghost in that graveyard, so they say. Gives me the shivers, that.
starter/compliment: Greetings, traveller! A moment? A spirit troubles my graveyard.
starter/insult: Would you fancy a word with a ghost? Nobody who can help ever does.
starter/remark: Saradomin give me strength. That ghost was moaning all night again.

compliment: Lovely thing, laying Lumbridge's ghost to rest like that, they say.
insult: I hear you gave a ghost its skull back. It only took a few centuries.
remark: My gran says the graveyard's gone quiet, that you, was it?
starter/compliment: Ah, my friend! The graveyard's been at peace since you helped.
starter/insult: Thank you again for the ghost. Sorry, I only had the one quest.
starter/remark: Not a peep from that ghost since, and I almost miss him.
kid/remark: What did the ghost want, and could you see through it?

compliment: Honest work, that, if you fancy shearing Fred's sheep.
insult: Fred's sheep are still waiting. They're more patient than Fred.
remark: Them sheep up Fred's farm are getting right woolly.
starter/compliment: You there! Fancy shearing my sheep for a few coins?
starter/insult: Have you ever actually held a pair of shears, or just looked at some?
starter/remark: Twenty balls of wool. Where am I going to find twenty?
That sheep's looking at me again.
rough/remark: Fred's sheep want shearing. He'll not do it himself, mind.

compliment: You sheared every sheep on Fred's farm, every last one, I hear!
insult: Word is you sheared some sheep. The sheep tell it differently.
remark: Fred's sheep look positively chilly since you came by.
starter/compliment: Ah, if it isn't my favourite shearer, how are you keeping?
starter/insult: Oi, shearer. That sheep's still not forgiven you, you know.
starter/remark: The sheep are getting woolly again, not that I'm hinting.
rough/compliment: I hear ye sheared Fred's whole flock, so ye can do mine next.

compliment: Veos at the pub wants a treasure hunter, and you've got the look.
insult: Veos's treasure is still buried. It's a spade and a map, traveller.
remark: Bloke in the Sheared Ram keeps on about buried treasure.
starter/compliment: Fancy yourself a treasure hunter? I've a map that needs reading.
starter/insult: You look like you'd lose a spade in a bucket, but come on anyway.
starter/remark: Where's that treasure... the scroll says it's round here somewhere.
barkeep/remark: Veos has nursed one drink all week, going on about treasure.

compliment: Good on you for digging up Veos's treasure, I hear.
insult: Word is you dug holes all over Lumbridge, so fill them in, would you?
starter/compliment: My favourite digger! Fancy another adventure?
starter/insult: Back for more holes, my little digging assistant?
barkeep/insult: Dug up Lumbridge for Veos, I hear. He still owes for his ale.

compliment: Those adventurers by the swamp are after the lost city of Zanaris.
Those adventurers won't say what they're after, but the warrior might.
insult: Weeks those adventurers have been in the swamp, looking for Zanaris.
plain/insult: You'd fit right in with that lot camped in the swamp finding nothing.
remark: The leprechaun in the swamp knows a thing or two, I hear.
gossip: The warrior by the swamp let slip they're after Zanaris, very loudly.
They say a leprechaun hides in one of those trees, but not which.
starter/compliment: Hello, traveller! We're not here for any particular reason, honest.
starter/insult: Adventurers of our calibre don't hang about in forests for fun, whelp!
starter/remark: We're looking for Zanaris! Gah! Forget I ever said anything to you.

compliment: Word is you found Zanaris. Dramen staff and everything!
insult: I hear you found a whole city. And it was in a shed the whole time?
plain/insult: Found a magic city in a shed, so I hear. Have you tried the privy yet?
remark: That leprechaun's been telling everyone about you.
gossip: The archer by the swamp still can't believe who found that portal.
It was that shed in the swamp all along, they say... the shed!
starter/compliment: You found it? Well... good for you. Don't tell the others I helped.
starter/insult: A whelp like you found Zanaris? ...We're still not looking for it.
starter/remark: Still no sign of Zanaris! Gah! We aren't searching for anything, nope.

compliment: Romeo's pining for Juliet again. Would you help the poor lad out?
insult: Romeo's still sighing in the square. Go on, you've nothing better on.
remark: Young love. Loud, isn't it?
starter/compliment: Excuse me! Have you seen my Juliet? Fairest maiden in Varrock!
starter/insult: You! You look clever. Where do people keep Juliets?
starter/remark: Oh, Juliet... wherefore art thou... no, really, where are you?
barkeep/remark: Romeo's been in here sighing into his drink over some Juliet.
guard/remark: Moved Romeo along twice today, and he'll be back, sighing.

compliment: I hear you helped Romeo and Juliet, which is ever so romantic.
insult: Did anyone ask her dad before you played matchmaker for those two?
remark: Romeo's been going round telling everyone about you.
starter/compliment: My friend, you helped me and Juliet, sort of, and I'm so grateful!
starter/insult: Oh, it's you. The reason Juliet doesn't write any more.
starter/remark: Juliet? Oh, her! Lovely girl, though I forget what became of her.
guard/remark: Quiet in the square since you sorted Romeo out... too quiet.

compliment: A demon's coming for Varrock, Aris says, and you look the type.
insult: A demon's due south of the walls. Don't let it spoil your shopping.
remark: The fortune teller's ever so worried about a demon.
starter/compliment: Cross my palm with silver, dear, and I'll show you a great destiny!
starter/insult: The ball shows a hero and then it shows you, dear, which is odd.
starter/remark: Delrith... Delrith... the ball keeps showing me that demon.
kid/remark: A demon's coming and Mum says I can't watch.
guard/remark: Fortune teller says a demon's coming. Not on my shift, it isn't.
guard/gossip: Word from the palace is nothing about a demon, so there's no demon.

compliment: Varrock owes you one for seeing off the demon Delrith, I hear.
Varrock's still here. Aris says that's down to you.
insult: Does Sir Prysin know you killed a demon with his sword?
remark: Sir Prysin's been bragging about handing you Silverlight.
starter/compliment: Ah, my hero! The crystal ball still shows you, dear.
starter/insult: The ball says that demon's the best you'll ever do, dear, sorry.
barkeep/compliment: You're the one who saw off that demon? First one's on me, then, love.
kid/compliment: Can I see the shiny sword you stabbed the demon with?
kid/insult: Sir Prysin gave you the sword, so really he killed it, didn't he?
guard/compliment: You're the one who saw off that demon? Carry on, then, carefully.
guard/remark: A demon at the gates, and nobody filed a report.

compliment: Reldo in the palace library's got a tale about a stolen shield.
insult: That old shield's still missing. There's a whole library on it.
remark: They say Varrock's got two gangs now, the Phoenix and the Black Arm.
starter/compliment: Psst. You look like you'd enjoy a mystery. A stolen shield, perhaps?
starter/insult: Shh! Have you ever read a book? The one on the shield is just there.
starter/remark: Hmm, the old shield... stolen by a gang... fascinating.
guard/remark: I know where the Phoenix and Black Arm gangs are, and nobody asks me.

compliment: That old shield's back at the museum thanks to you, I hear.
insult: Joined a gang for a shield, I hear. Your mother must be thrilled.
remark: Which gang got you that shield? On second thought, don't tell me.
starter/compliment: Ah, a reader! I've written you into the history books, you know.
starter/insult: Shh. Oh, it's you. You still owe the library three books.
guard/insult: I hear you joined a gang for a shield, so I'll be watching you.

compliment: King Roald needs a temple checking on out east, by the Salve.
insult: Not even the brave ones have checked on that temple by the Salve.
remark: Something nasty about that temple out east, they say.
starter/compliment: Ah, a capable sort! I need someone to look in on a temple.
starter/insult: Yes, citizen? Good. You'll do. There's a temple needs checking.
starter/remark: Not a word from the temple on the Salve, which troubles me greatly.
guard/gossip: Palace says the Salve temple's gone quiet, and it's not our problem.

compliment: Word is you saved that priest at the Salve temple, good work.
insult: Killed the temple's dog because a door asked you to, I hear.
remark: They say you can get into Morytania now. Better you than me, friend.
starter/compliment: Ah, citizen. We received word from Drezel and it speaks well of you.
starter/insult: A dog? In a temple? Are you a complete imbecile, citizen?
guard/remark: Back from the Salve, are you? Wipe that Morytania mud off your boots.

compliment: Morgan wants someone to see off a vampyre, and you'd do, with garlic.
insult: Count Draynor's still at large. Lovely neck you've got, by the way.
remark: Morgan still fears the Count, though nobody's seen him in ages.
starter/compliment: Could it be? A bold adventurer! Please, a vampyre plagues Draynor!
starter/insult: You there! What if the Count wakes up hungry? Hurry!
starter/remark: Nobody's seen the Count in years. Which is just what he wants.

compliment: I expect Draynor sleeps easy now you've staked the Count.
I'd not have gone near that Draynor vampyre, but I hear you did.
insult: Very sporting of you, staking a vampyre who'd only just woken up.
remark: Draynor folk have been buying garlic in your honour.
starter/compliment: My saviour! I sleep with the window open now, thanks to you.
starter/insult: Took you long enough. I'd nearly run out of garlic.
kid/compliment: Did the vampyre scream and go all dusty when you staked it?
kid/insult: You beat a vampyre with garlic? I eat garlic, so am I a hero?

compliment: Poor Veronica's fella went into that manor and never came out.
insult: Ernest's still in that manor. Scared of the professor, are you?
remark: The professor in that manor's a bit touched, they say.
starter/compliment: Oh, please, you look kind! My Ernest went into that manor!
starter/insult: Are you going to help me, or just stand there gawping?
starter/remark: Ernest said he'd only be a minute. That was hours ago now, wasn't it?

compliment: You turned Ernest back from a chicken, or mostly back, I hear.
insult: Word is you un-chickened a man, so expect a very short song about it.
remark: Ernest still pecks at his dinner, I hear.
starter/compliment: There you are! Ernest's ever so grateful, and nearly back to normal.
starter/insult: Ernest still clucks in his sleep, and I've you to thank for that.
kid/compliment: If you can turn a chicken into a man then do it to our rooster!

compliment: Fancy a rescue? Hassan says Prince Ali's been kidnapped.
insult: Prince Ali's still locked up. Heroes are thin on the ground, it seems.
remark: Al Kharid's in a right state about that prince.
starter/compliment: Friend! You look resourceful. Our prince has been taken!
starter/insult: You? Well. Beggars can't be choosers. The prince has been kidnapped.
starter/remark: The prince gone and the Emir not sleeping. Nor have I, come to that.

compliment: Word is you sprang Prince Ali from under Lady Keli's nose!
insult: I hear you put a prince in a wig and a skirt, and that he suited it.
remark: Lady Keli's still fuming about you, I hear.
starter/compliment: Ah, a friend of Al Kharid! The Emir speaks of you often.
starter/insult: The prince still won't take that skirt off, and whose doing is that?

compliment: Wizard Mizgog's lost his beads to imps. Could you catch a few for him?
insult: The imps still have Mizgog's beads. They're small imps, traveller.
remark: Imps everywhere round the tower these days, little pests.
starter/compliment: Ah! You look quick on your feet. Fancy catching some imps?
starter/insult: Not now, I'm concentrating. Unless you're here about the imps?
starter/remark: Red bead... yellow bead... black, white... wretched imps.

compliment: Lovely of you to get Mizgog's beads back off them imps.
insult: Word is you spent a week chasing imps for some beads.
starter/compliment: Ah, the imp-catcher! My beads are still the shiniest in the tower.
starter/insult: My beads came back sticky. Imp sticky, and I've you to thank for it.

compliment: Hetty in Rimmington's brewing something and needs a rat's tail.
insult: Hetty still needs a rat's tail. Rats aren't that frightening.
remark: Smells of eye of newt round Hetty's place.
starter/compliment: Ooh, dear. Fetch me a few bits and I'll teach you some magic.
starter/insult: Rat's tail, dear, or you'll never know what shape you'll wake up in.
starter/remark: Eye of newt... burnt meat... onion... where's that rat's tail?

compliment: You drank Hetty's potion? I'd not have put it near my lips.
insult: Did you really drink out of a witch's cauldron on purpose?
remark: Hetty's telling everyone how helpful you were, which is suspicious.
starter/compliment: Ooh, hello again, dear! Are you coming in for a brew with me?
starter/insult: You drank my potion in one go, dear, and nobody ever does that.

compliment: Doric's after clay, copper and iron, honest work if you want it.
insult: Doric's still waiting on clay. Somebody fetch the man some clay.
remark: Doric's anvils are free to use, if you help him out.
starter/compliment: Hello, traveller! Fetch me some ores and you can use my anvils.
starter/insult: Hello, traveller. My grandmother mines faster, and she's a rock.
starter/remark: Six clay, four copper, two iron... where's a helper when you need one.
dwarf/remark: Doric's waiting on clay, copper and iron, nothing fancy.

compliment: I hear Doric lets you use his anvils, and he doesn't let many.
insult: Clay for Doric, I hear. Heavy work, if you count the walk.
starter/compliment: Ah, friend! The anvils are free for you, as always.
starter/insult: You brought me some clay and now you want a statue for it?
rough/compliment: Doric lets ye at his anvils? He'll not let me near 'em.
dwarf/compliment: Doric lets you use his anvils? By Guthix, he doesn't let me.

compliment: The Squire's lost Sir Vyvin's sword. Would you help the lad out?
insult: Could you at least look like you'll help the Squire with that sword?
remark: Some daft squire's lost his master's sword, I hear.
starter/compliment: Oh, please! I've lost Sir Vyvin's sword and he'll have my head!
starter/insult: Unless you've a sword in your pocket, move along... actually, wait!
starter/remark: Sir Vyvin will have my head... where did I put that sword?
rough/remark: Some squire's gone and lost a sword. How does anyone lose a sword?
dwarf/remark: A lost sword and a nervous squire. Thurgo could sort it, for a pie.
guard/remark: The squire's lost Sir Vyvin's sword, which is not my department.

compliment: Very noble of you to save that Squire's bacon, so I hear.
insult: Bribed a dwarf with a pie for a sword? I'd have held out for two.
remark: Thurgo still asks after you, and after his pie more often.
starter/compliment: Psst! Sir Vyvin never noticed a thing, and I owe you for that!
starter/insult: Sir Vyvin keeps asking why his hilt's gone sparkly.
rough/remark: They say that's blurite off the ice, so rather ye than me.
dwarf/compliment: Thurgo forged you a blade? Treasure it, because that's Imcando work.
guard/gossip: Sir Vyvin's sword turned up and nobody's asking where, which is good.

compliment: Sir Amik needs a spy in the Black Knights' Fortress, all hush-hush.
insult: The Black Knights are brewing something. Not that anyone's looked.
remark: The Black Knights are up to something, mark my words.
starter/compliment: You there! You look discreet. The White Knights need a spy.
starter/insult: Hmm. Not exactly the spy type. Still, you'll have to do.
starter/remark: What are those Black Knights brewing up in that fortress of theirs?
guard/gossip: Word from the castle is watch the north road, Black Knights about.

compliment: Jolly good show, ruining the Black Knights' plans like that!
insult: I hear you dropped a cabbage in a cauldron like a true warrior.
remark: Never look at a cabbage the same way now, do you?
starter/compliment: Ah, my spy! Splendid to see you again.
starter/insult: So one cabbage was your grand contribution to the war, was it?
guard/compliment: You're Sir Amik's spy? Didn't see you. Which is the point, I suppose.

compliment: Could you sort the goblins out? They're fighting over armour colours.
insult: Goblins still rowing over armour colours. Wants a diplomat, or paint.
remark: Them goblins in Goblin Village are at it again.
gossip: Half the goblins in red and half in green, all of them shouting.
The generals want new armour for the goblin new century, they say.
starter/compliment: Human! You look clever for human. Bring us armour in new colour!
starter/insult: Go away, human. Goblins busy. Unless human bring armour?
starter/remark: Red make you look fat. Green look naked. What colour left for goblin?

compliment: Sorted out Wartface and Bentnoze? A proper diplomat and no mistake.
insult: Do the goblins tip, for all that armour you dyed them?
remark: Typical goblins, settling on brown armour of all colours.
gossip: Orange, then blue and then brown. They started with brown, mind.
Grubfoot tried on every colour, they say. Looked like an orange-fruit.
starter/compliment: Human! Brown armour quite nice. Me can see myself wearing that.
starter/insult: Thank you for sorting argument, human. Now go, human still ugly.
starter/remark: Brown armour it is. Was brown before, but shut up, Grubfoot.

compliment: Redbeard Frank's after some rum. Says he'll show you treasure.
insult: Redbeard's still dry. Nobody brave enough to fetch rum, it seems.
remark: That Redbeard Frank's always got a bottle on the go.
starter/compliment: Arr! Fetch me some Karamjan rum and I'll make it worth yer while.
starter/insult: Arr, ye're as useful as a chocolate cutlass, but fetch me rum anyway.
starter/remark: Arr... not a drop o' rum left... a pirate can't live like this.
pirate/remark: Frank's been dry a week. A dry pirate's a dangerous thing.
pirate/gossip: Redbeard says there's treasure for whoever fetches him rum, says he.
barkeep/remark: Frank's tab's longer than my arm, and he wants Karamja rum.

compliment: Ooh! You found old Redbeard's treasure, I hear.
insult: Smuggled rum in with the bananas, I hear. The bananas never recovered.
remark: Somebody dug up Falador park. The gardener's still livid.
starter/compliment: Arr, hello again, me hearty! Ye be a pirate at heart and no mistake.
starter/insult: Arr, ye ate half them bananas, didn't ye?
pirate/compliment: Ye got rum past the Customs men? Arr, ye're one of us now.
pirate/insult: Arr, all that for one casket. Old Hector buried his small.
rough/insult: Hid rum in the bananas, I hear. Wydin's still counting 'em.
barkeep/remark: Fetched Frank his rum, did you? Lovely. Now fetch me what he owes.
kid/insult: I'd have kept digging if I'd dug up the whole park for one box.
guard/insult: Somebody dug up the park, and Wyson's filed several complaints.

compliment: You've the look of someone the Champions' Guild wants for a dragon.
insult: Elvarg's still alive, and so are you, which is surely coincidence.
remark: Elvarg's still out on Crandor, they say.
starter/compliment: Want to prove yourself? There's a dragon on Crandor needs seeing to.
starter/insult: A champion? You? Well. There's a dragon that might settle it.
starter/remark: Elvarg still lives... someone ought to do something about it.
kid/remark: There's a dragon on Crandor and Dad still won't take me to see it.

compliment: Slew Elvarg, didn't you? A proper champion and no mistake.
Blimey! You're the one who slew Elvarg?
insult: Did Ned get his boat back after you took it to fight a dragon?
remark: Ned's been telling everyone about that boat trip, every day since.
starter/compliment: Ah, a true hero! Welcome back, champion.
starter/insult: Killed one dragon. There's rather a lot more, you know.
kid/compliment: Did you keep the dragon's teeth? Can I have one for a necklace?
kid/insult: Mum says Ned's boat got wrecked. That was you that did it, wasn't it?

compliment: See Kaqemeex, if you want the Taverley druids to teach you herblore.
insult: Patient folk, the druids, still waiting on that meat of theirs.
remark: The druids at the stone circle are ever so friendly.
starter/compliment: Greetings, traveller. The druids could teach you the ways of herblore.
starter/insult: Can you even tell a herb from a weed, or shall I have to show you?
starter/remark: The ritual must be done... we need raw meats for the cauldron.

compliment: I hear the Taverley druids taught you herblore, clever thing.
insult: Dipped meat in a cauldron, I hear. The druids call that a ritual.
starter/compliment: Greetings again, herbalist. Guthix smiles on those who gather well.
starter/insult: The druids still talk about that meat you brought, and not kindly.

compliment: Almera's lad went down the river, so would you help her out?
insult: Almera's lad's still down that river, if anyone could be bothered.
remark: Baxtorian's tomb's under them falls, they reckon.
starter/compliment: Oh, please, you look brave! My son Hudon went down the river!
starter/insult: Are you going to help, or just stand there admiring the waterfall?
starter/remark: Hudon... that silly boy and his treasure hunting...

compliment: Smashing, finding Baxtorian's chamber under the falls like that.
insult: Floated down a river on a log, didn't you, when most folk use a boat?
starter/compliment: Oh, it's you! Hudon's still sulking that you got there first.
starter/insult: Hudon says you stole his treasure, and I say you're welcome to it.

compliment: King Bolren's gnomes need help against Khazard's troops.
insult: Bolren's still waiting. It's only a hedge maze, traveller.
remark: The gnomes in the maze are at war again.
starter/compliment: Welcome, human! You look strong and our village could do with help.
starter/insult: Ah, human. So you found your way through the maze eventually.
starter/remark: The orb is gone... the village is lost without it...
gnome/remark: Khazard's men at the village again. Bolren will be beside himself.

compliment: Got the gnomes their orbs back, so I hear, and now they love you.
insult: Lost in a hedge for an hour, I hear. Gnome children do it for fun.
remark: The spirit tree's lovely and green now, they say.
starter/compliment: Ah, our human friend! The orbs are safe, thanks to you.
starter/insult: An hour in my maze. The children do it in ten minutes.
gnome/compliment: You brought the orbs back to Bolren? The spirit tree thanks you.
gnome/insult: Through the maze at last, human. We put signs up for you lot.

compliment: Could you lend King Narnode a hand with the Grand Tree?
insult: The Grand Tree's poorly. Not that sightseers notice.
remark: Something's eating at the Grand Tree's roots, they say.
starter/compliment: Welcome, traveller! Good to see an outsider, with the Tree so sick.
starter/insult: Ah, human. Forgive me if I hope you're more use than the last one.
starter/remark: What on earth is eating at the Grand Tree's roots?
gnome/remark: Narnode's been pacing round the Tree, and pacing's never good.

compliment: I hear the gnomes owe you for rumbling Glough.
insult: I hear you found a rock under a tree, so there'll be a parade.
remark: Glough had it coming, if you ask me.
starter/compliment: Ah, human! The Grand Tree thrives, thanks to you.
starter/insult: You found a rock under my tree. I'd have got there eventually.
gnome/compliment: You're the human who caught Glough out and got the Tree green again?
gnome/insult: Glough a traitor, and it took a human to notice, hmph.

starter/compliment: Ah, human! I need an envoy. Would you look into the tenth squad?
starter/insult: Ape Atoll? Hmm. You'll have to do, I suppose.
starter/remark: The tenth squad went to Ape Atoll and there's not been a word since.
gossip: Narnode's after someone brave for Ape Atoll and nobody's volunteered.
The monkeys on Ape Atoll are a rum lot.
The tenth squad went to Ape Atoll and never came back.

compliment: Word is you fought a jungle demon on Ape Atoll and walked away.
Blimey, you found the tenth squad on Ape Atoll, and alive?
insult: Found the tenth squad and left them on Ape Atoll, which is thorough.
remark: Back from Ape Atoll smelling of bananas, I expect.
starter/compliment: Ah, my monkey-wrangling friend! You were magnificent out there.
starter/insult: Ah, human. Forgive me, but you still smell faintly of monkey.
gossip: The tenth squad are alive, so Narnode says. Still on Ape Atoll, mind.
kid/insult: You dressed up as a monkey for a whole week, didn't you?
plain/insult: Ape Atoll was perfectly quiet until you went poking about.
gnome/compliment: You found the tenth squad, human? Narnode hasn't stopped smiling.
gnome/insult: You still sit like a monkey, human. Is that from habit or choice?

compliment: Brundt in Rellekka wants to see if you're Fremennik material.
insult: Still an outerlander? The Fremennik won't even sell you a fish.
remark: The Fremennik won't trade with outerlanders, you know.
starter/compliment: Greetings, outerlander! Prove yourself to the council and earn a name.
starter/insult: Hah, an outerlander who'll never pass the trials, but go on and try!
starter/remark: Another outerlander. Will none of them prove worthy?
fremennik/remark: Our customs forbid me talking to you, outerlander, so I won't.
fremennik/insult: Seven of the twelve, outerlander. You'll be lucky to get one.
fremennik/gossip: Another outerlander trying for the council, and they never last.

compliment: I hear the Fremennik gave you a name, which is very rugged of you.
insult: Word is you drank a pint and played a lyre. A warrior's trials, those.
remark: What's your Fremennik name, then? Bound to be something silly.
starter/compliment: Well met and welcome back, friend of the Fremennik!
starter/insult: Hah! Your Fremennik name still gets a laugh in the longhall.
fremennik/compliment: Hah! Well met. You drank Manni under the table, they say.
fremennik/insult: You beat Koschei, they say. Three times. Four would've impressed me.
fremennik/remark: A Fremennik name and a seat in the longhall, so don't waste either.

compliment: Saved the whole Lumbridge banquet, word is, pudding and all.
I hear you saw off that mad chef. The council owes you dinner.
A cook from a hundred years back crashed a feast, and you saw him off.
Takes nerve, feeding a monkey king his favourite dish, they say.
You cooked for a dwarf, goblins, an ogre, a pirate and a knight?
They say you beat a demon made of bananas, and I need a sit-down.
insult: I hear it took you an age to save one dinner party.
Saved a feast, I hear. The washing-up was somebody else's problem?
You're a patient sort, cooking all those dinners before the fighting.
remark: That Culinaromancer's not so cocky now, eh?
Who thinks of putting an evil chicken's egg in a pudding?
They say the help saved Duke Horacio's dinner, as per usual.
pirate/compliment: Ye fed Pirate Pete a fishcake and he's still on about it, arr.
barkeep/compliment: You saw off the Culinaromancer? Every cook in Gielinor owes you one.
dwarf/compliment: A rock cake off old Rohak, carried hot. By Guthix, that's dedication.
dwarf/remark: Rohak's rock cakes. You need gloves. Everyone learns that once.
kid/insult: You saved a whole dinner? Was there pudding and did you get any?
guard/remark: Saved a banquet, did you? Nobody ever saves me a pudding.
gossip: They say hell-rats in Evil Dave's cellar took all the spices.
A fortune-teller froze the Duke's whole table in time, they say.
The goblin generals agreed on something at last, a dish called slop.
Same cook, same castle, and I hear he needed help again.
kid/compliment: Was the banana demon squishy, and did you eat it after?
kid/remark: Mum says there's an evil chicken in a cave and I want to see it!
goblin/gossip: Me hear generals eat same slop at human feast. Grey slop. Both eat it!
Human feast in Lumbridge, they say. Generals go. Only one chair.
troll/gossip: Big human feast in Lumbridge, me hear. Nobody invite trolls. Rude.
barbarian/gossip: They say the Duke's table was frozen in time, and our meat never is.
A Lumbridge feast got attacked, I hear. At last, a feast worth it.

gossip: Dragons are stirring again. The Myths' Guild is asking for help.
Odd hobby, wanting to know where dragons come from like Alec Kincade.
Some scholar by the Myths' Guild is asking about Crandor, I hear.
They say the Myths' Guild wants dragons slain before it lets you in.
A fellow at the Myths' Guild has spent half his life on dragons.
pirate/gossip: Dragons over the sea again, and that's bad for shipping, arr.
fremennik/gossip: Dragons stirring in the northern seas, so sharpen your axe.
remark: Nobody ever asks why Elvarg burned Crandor, only that she did.
Elvarg's dead, and still folk whisper about where dragons come from.
goblin/gossip: Dragons stirring, humans say. Dragon just big lizard. Goblins laugh.
troll/gossip: Dragons stirring, humans say. Dragon just big lizard. Big dinner.
barbarian/gossip: Dragons stirring, city folk say. Good. A dragon is a proper fight.

compliment: You saw off Galvek, word is. I'd buy you a pint for that.
Imagine it, King Roald calling the kingdoms together on your word!
The Myths' Guild took you in, I hear. They don't take just anyone.
Galvek's maker burned by his own dragon, and you stood right there.
A dragon built to end the world, they say, and you faced it.
insult: Did for Galvek, did you? You'd never know to look at you.
Slew Galvek, they say. And here you are, waiting about like anyone.
Galvek, done for. You'd think they'd have given you a bigger hat.
remark: Has the Myths' Guild put your statue up yet, or are they slow?
Crandor's still a ruin, Galvek or no. Some things don't come back.
Ye gods! They say Elvarg was only the first of them!
fremennik/insult: Four fleets sailed for Ungael. Count the ships that came back.
pirate/compliment: Arr, ye faced Galvek at sea and lived? Drinks are on me, one drink.
pirate/remark: Ships burning off Ungael, they say. Arr, I'd have stayed in port.
rough/compliment: Ye did for Galvek? Blimey, ye don't look it, and I mean that kindly.
barkeep/compliment: You did for Galvek? Pint's on the house, just the one, mind.
dwarf/compliment: Galvek, done for. By Guthix. Whoever forged your blade did you proud.
fremennik/compliment: Brundt sailed for Ungael with you, and he speaks of it, which is rare.
kid/compliment: Were you scared, fighting a dragon as big as Galvek?
Did Galvek's fire make the sea go hot? Could you swim in it after?
guard/remark: Dragon slayer or not, that weapon stays sheathed in town.
heartland/compliment: Blimey! You're the one who did for Galvek, the dragon, aren't you?
gossip: They say the dragonkin made Elvarg like a smith makes a nail.
Four kingdoms' ships from one little dock at Rellekka, they say!
The Wise Old Man went to Ungael, I hear. Fought a red dragon on deck.
Word is some of Varrock's guard never came home from Ungael.
A cat's grave in Burthorpe, they say, and folk who mourn it.
kid/remark: A cat fought a dragon, they say. My cat only fights the broom.
goblin/gossip: Galvek dragon dead, they say. Big High War God like that. War good.
Human kings all meet in one place, me hear. Goblins not invited. Rude.
troll/gossip: Human kill Galvek dragon, me hear. Dragons breathe fire. Good it dead.
Ships sail from fur town after dragon, me hear. Trolls stay. We sink.
barbarian/gossip: They say Galvek the dragon was slain. A saga for the longhall, that.
I hear our cousins sailed from Rellekka to fight dragons!

gossip: Trouble in the elf lands again. Lletya's sent for help, I'm told.
Still a wall through Ardougne, and still nobody says why.
Ardougne's locked up a woman for saying the plague's a lie.
They say Edmond's girl is in the Ardougne cells for speaking out.
Mourners still walk West Ardougne, and nobody can name one sick man.
The elves in Isafdar are at each other's throats again, I hear.
Lord Iorwerth wants his Dark Lord back, whatever that is, they say.
guard/gossip: Locked a woman up for calling the plague a lie, as orders are orders.
remark: They say something's stirring right under West Ardougne.
King Lathas keeps the wall up and his reasons to himself.
goblin/gossip: Tall people with biting blades have trouble, they say. Elves. Good.
troll/gossip: Trouble in elf lands, humans say. Elves far away. Not troll problem.
barbarian/gossip: A wall through Ardougne, they say. City folk hide behind walls.

compliment: Word is you freed Prifddinas. The elves must adore you.
You faced the Fragment of Seren and lived? I can't even picture that.
Prifddinas lets humans in now, and you were first through the gate.
Ardougne's rid of Lathas, and folk say your name when they tell it.
Into the elf lands a stranger, out of them a legend, they say.
insult: Freed Prifddinas, I hear. And still not a word of elvish.
Freed Prifddinas, they say. You'll be wanting a crystal medal.
Toppled a king and an elf lord, so try not to do it here, eh?
remark: Prifddinas is lovely this time of year, I hear.
Years of that plague in West Ardougne, and it was a lie all along.
guard/gossip: New king in Ardougne. New orders, same gates.
gossip: Lathas was sentenced by his own folk and then by the axe, they say.
They say a piece of the elves' goddess was shut in a temple... was.
Word is Lord Iorwerth was shot by one of his own kind at the end.
They say Arianwyn the elf is wandering the world making amends.
A woman they'd locked up started the Ardougne Resistance, they say.
That wall hid a dig all along and never a plague, they say.
kid/compliment: Did you have to water the elf city if it grew like a plant?
kid/remark: Mum says the Ardougne plague was pretend. I'm not allowed to pretend.
goblin/gossip: Human king chopped by own people, me hear. Goblins only argue.
troll/gossip: Human king chopped by own people, me hear. Trolls just pick biggest.
barbarian/gossip: The elves got their glass city back, so they say, and glass is soft.
They say Ardougne's king answered for his lies, and good.

gossip: They say Glough's up to no good again, and the gnomes need a hand.
Did you hear? Glough's got loose. The gnomes are in a right state.
Glough slipped his guards, they say. Nobody knows how or who helped.
King Narnode's sent word for the one who stopped Glough last time.
Glough's house stands empty, they say, and the king wants it searched.
remark: Sleep well, with a gnome who hates humans loose and bearing a grudge.
Glough tried a tree, then an army. The third go is what worries me.
goblin/gossip: Gnome Glough loose again, they say. He hate humans too. Me like him.
troll/gossip: Gnome called Glough loose again, me hear. Gnome small. Not even snack.
barbarian/gossip: Hah, gnomes! They say that Glough slipped his guards again.

compliment: Blimey! You're the one who stopped Glough's gorilla army?
Word is you sorted Glough out for good. The gnomes can breathe again.
The monkey king came to the gnomes for peace, and you stood witness.
A troll and an ogre backed out of that war after a word from you.
Nieve fell in that cavern and you carried on regardless, they say.
insult: Stopped Glough's army, they say. You look like you need a sit-down.
Stopped Glough, I hear. You don't look like someone who stops things.
Glough's beaten and the gnomes are safe. No parade for you, though.
remark: Glough's gone and the Grand Tree's still standing, and that'll do.
Glough's gone, and Nieve with him. Not a cheap victory, that.
Monkeys and gnomes at peace. My grandmother would never believe it.
gnome/remark: The Tree's still standing. That's twice we owe a human.
kid/compliment: How many gorillas were in the army you fought, a hundred?
If you really rode a gorilla, can I ride one, a small one?
guard/remark: A gorilla army, they say, and we've had worse, mostly goblins.
gossip: Glough drank something and became an actual monster, they say.
Word is a gnome called Le Smith helped Glough slip his guards.
They say Awowogei stripped Kruk of his rank, and him already dead.
They say Glough bred gorillas under Ape Atoll, big angry ones.
Glough's flying ship came down north of the Gnome Stronghold, I hear.
kid/remark: Glough had a ship that flies and I want one that flies too!
goblin/gossip: Glough drink potion, turn into big monster, they say. Lose anyway.
troll/gossip: Gnome drink potion, turn into big monster, me hear. Still lose. Hah.
Kob went to gnome war talks, me hear. Kob come back. Kob not say much.
barbarian/gossip: They say Glough drank a potion and became a monster, and still lost.

gossip: Somebody ought to look at those desert ruins that are stirring.
Diggers in the desert found a door nobody can open.
They say a sealed vault north of Nardah has old magic on the door.
Treasure hunters are drifting toward Nardah again, I hear.
The Exam Centre lot are excited about something they won't say.
remark: Old empires don't stay buried. Someone always goes digging.
Somebody will try those doors, built to stay shut or not.
goblin/gossip: Diggers find door in desert nobody can open, they say. Hit it harder.
troll/gossip: Diggers find door in desert nobody open, me hear. Trolls use rocks.
barbarian/gossip: A sealed vault in the desert, they say. Give me an axe and a day.

compliment: I hear it was Vardorvis and the Whisperer, and I struggle with wasps.
Ye gods, the Scar! I hear you went in there after the Leviathan.
Under the salt mines at Weiss and back with your wits, they say.
You faced a thing called the Whisperer? I'd have run at the name.
Ye gods, a duke of the old empire, and you put him down.
heartland/insult: Four ancient horrors, I hear. And here you are, out for a stroll.
insult: They say you slew the Leviathan, so mind the puddle on your way out.
Four ancient horrors slain, they say. And still you queue at the bank.
remark: Half the Mahjarrat waited for someone to open that vault, they say.
gossip: Dr Banikan from the Digsite was a Mahjarrat the whole time, they say.
There's a wood past Kebos where the trees get into you, they say.
Mahjarrat squabbling again, word is, and Sliske's name comes up.
They say a whole sunken city of ancient things lies under Camdozaal.
They say a Mahjarrat wore a human face all along, and nobody noticed.
kid/compliment: Did the Leviathan have a hundred teeth... did you not even count?
kid/remark: Dad says there's a whispering thing underground, so I whisper back.
goblin/gossip: Human kill leviathan in desert, me hear. Big fish. Big dinner.
troll/gossip: Human fight big leviathan thing, me hear. Trolls stay out of water.
Big old thing under Weiss, me hear. Human went down. Trolls stay up.
barbarian/gossip: Bah, magic folk! They say a Digsite scholar turned out a Mahjarrat.
A big fish! I hear some beast under the sea by the desert was slain.

gossip: Some old heroes have been sent for. Something's up, mark my words.
The Taverley druids are quietly asking after seasoned adventurers.
They say a messenger of Armadyl's handing out sealed letters.
Word is the Mahjarrat are stirring. Nobody says that word lightly.
remark: The druids look worried, which they never do, so now I'm worried.
goblin/gossip: Druids want old heroes, they say. Goblins not asked. Goblins mighty!
troll/gossip: Druids want old heroes, me hear. Trolls not asked. Trolls never asked.
barbarian/gossip: They say the druids want old heroes, and nobody sent for us.

compliment: Not many can say they stood against Lucien, but word is you can.
You've stood in Guthix's own cave? Fair play to you for that.
You had druids, knights and Armadyl's own standing together, I hear.
You found what Guthix buried. Not many have laid eyes on it, they say.
They say you touched the Stone of Jas and just walked away from it!
insult: I hear Lucien got away, which is probably not your fault.
Found the Stone of Jas, I hear. Then Lucien found it, pity that.
Lucien's got the Stone and you've got a story, so who came out ahead?
gossip: They say Lucien's loose with something he oughtn't have.
Did you hear? Lucien has the Staff of Armadyl and the Stone both now.
The Dark Squall was Surok Magis all along, the Varrock one, they say.
They say Lucien raised dead heroes in the Wilderness to serve him.
Sloane of the Warriors' Guild never came home, and that was Lucien.
One spell from Lucien did for the slayer master at Shilo, they say.
A man called Movario hunted that Stone for Lucien, they say.
rough/compliment: Ye stood against Lucien? Cor! More than I'd have dared, honest.
fremennik/compliment: Lucien, and you walked away. Hah! The spirits favour you, outerlander.
kid/remark: Lucien's the scary one, isn't he? Dad goes quiet when I ask.
I heard Lucien's got a magic rock and mine's just a rock.
guard/remark: Lucien's above my rank. Move along, and good luck to you.
remark: They say Guthix hid that Stone for a reason, and Lucien's not it.
The Stone of Jas made the Wilderness in Zamorak's hands, they say.
kid/compliment: If the Stone of Jas made you strong then lift me up and prove it!
goblin/gossip: Lucien get magic rock, they say. Big High War God not need rock.
troll/gossip: Lucien got big magic rock, me hear. Trolls got rocks too. Not magic.
barbarian/gossip: Bah, wizard's weapons! They say Lucien's got a staff and a stone now.

gossip: Glough's gone for good this time, and the cavern saw to that.
Steve's taken Nieve's post, and he knows whose boots he's in.
They say Awowogei himself came to the Stronghold to talk peace!
Glough drank his own brew and brought the cave down on himself.
Marim's taking visitors now, monkeys and all, would you believe it?
compliment: You're the human from the crash site? Narnode speaks highly of you.
Are you the human who stood with Nieve? I'm... sorry.
Glough's gorillas, and you still standing. Narnode's beside himself.
insult: Glough warned us about humans. Funny how they keep turning up.
plain/insult: Nieve fell. You walked out. Nobody here's quite forgiven that.
gnome/compliment: You stood with Nieve at the cavern? Every gnome here knows your name.
gnome/insult: Glough was one of ours. We'd have liked to deal with him ourselves.
kid/remark: I put a flower on Nieve's grave, up by the crash site.

gossip: Glough's slipped house arrest. Nobody slips house arrest on their own.
Narnode's doubled the watch on the Grand Tree and won't say why.
Galvek's dead, but mind, there's still dragons in that old fort.
They say a cat died at Ungael saving a human, of all things!
Poor Dallas Jones never came back from Lithkren.
Fancy Bob the cat being Robert the Strong all along!
compliment: Are you the one who faced Galvek? Four kingdoms owe you for that.
You gave Bob back his memories? Robert the Strong, our Bob!
plain/insult: Bob went to Ungael for you and didn't come back, yet here you stand.
Nobody's cheering here. Galvek's dead, but so are Dallas and the cat.
kid/remark: They say a cat died saving you. Did you say thank you to it?

gossip: Nobody goes near that old ruin on the hill, and nobody should.
Prifddinas is back, grown from a seed, they say!
Iestin leads the Iorwerth now. Half the city still watches them.
Lathas is dead and Thoros is king, and didn't Ardougne cheer!
Baxtorian's free of the stone and an elder now, after all this time.
A king, hiding in a wardrobe! That's what they say Lathas did!
compliment: You're the human who walked the Temple of Light and came back?
Are you the one Baxtorian speaks of? He hardly speaks of anyone.
What was it like, being there when Prifddinas grew back?
plain/insult: Lord Iorwerth wanted Seren home. You wanted a city, and you got yours.
Eight clans and one human. Guess who the songs are about.
One human, one Fragment, and now everyone's an expert on elves.
King Tyras burned in his own camp. Odd, you being there that day.

gossip: The mourners dig under Ardougne, and Lletya waits, as it always has.
Keep off the paths. Iorwerth's scouts were in the forest again.
Lletya's scouts are out east again, so something's coming.
That Smith fellow from the dig? Wasn't a Smith at all, they say.
The Vault's open. Whatever was in it has gone north.
The Stranglewood's gone quiet, and nobody's asking why.
compliment: You walked back out of the Scar? I'd not have gone in at all.
Most who go into the Stranglewood don't come out, yet here you are.
plain/insult: Proud of yourself, opening a door even the Mahjarrat couldn't, eh?
Did you never notice Sliske was running you about in a borrowed face?
remark: Vardorvis gives me nightmares, and I've only heard the stories.

gossip: Diggers at the Vault keep failing the door, and good, leave it shut.
Lucien has the Stone and nobody says where. Nobody says much, lately.
Hazelmere's gone. Lucien turned him to ash, they say.
A gnome minds the Warriors' Guild door now, Ghommal's not coming back.
Turael's gone. Burthorpe's had to find a new slayer master.
compliment: If you were at that temple in the Wilderness then you saw them fall.
You're the one Thaerisk speaks of. He doesn't say it lightly.
You found the Stone of Jas? Before Lucien got his hands on it?
plain/insult: How exactly did you come home when six heroes died at that temple?
The best of us went in with you, and we buried what came out.
Some rescue that was, with Lucien walking off with the Stone.

gossip: Ivy's been asking after anyone who can hold a sword, and urgently.
The Taverley druids are up to something and Thaerisk won't say what.
Why are strange folk asking round Burthorpe after the old heroes?
Lord Drakan's dead. Did you hear? Morytania's never been so quiet.
The vampyres have a new lord, a Vitur, and he wants peace, they say.
Drakan killed one of his own lords in front of everyone, they say.
They say Efaritay, queen of old Hallowvale, is alive even now.
Word is Drakan wanted every vampyre back in their old world, to hunt.
Folk called aranei died for a vampyre in Vampyrium, they say.
compliment: You're the one who did for Lord Drakan? You look so... ordinary.
Is it true you've been to Vampyrium and back?
The blood moon rose over Morytania, Drakan fell, and that was you.
Word is you took Drakan's own spear off him at the end, and kept it.
The vampyres' own world and back? And here you are, calm as milk.
barkeep/compliment: You're the one who did for Drakan? Sit down, love, anything you like.
kid/compliment: Did you use a stake on Lord Drakan, the real one?
Did Lord Drakan go to dust and did you keep any of it?
guard/remark: Drakan's dead, they say. Doesn't shorten my shift.
insult: Did for Drakan, they say. Centuries he lasted, so decent effort.
Slew Drakan, they say. I'd have expected more teeth marks.
remark: Good, a vampyre lord dead and the moon its usual colour again.
Misthalin's been told there'll be no war from the east, I hear.
kid/remark: They say the moon went red, but I looked and it was just the moon.
goblin/gossip: Drakan dead, me hear. Red moon over swamp land. Goblins stay home.
troll/gossip: Vampyre lord dead in swamp land, me hear. Vampyres only drink. Waste.
barbarian/gossip: I hear Lord Drakan's dead, and that must have been a fight!

gossip: They say the Vitur fellow's outlawed the tithe, and some vyres sulk.
Half of Meiyerditch is packing for the Salve, and who can blame them?
Veliaf's reopened the Burgh de Rott pub and calls it Myreque's Rest.
Imagine, Efaritay selling vampyrebane blades in Castle Drakan now!
The Vyrewatch let some adventurer walk right past without blinking.
They say Safalaan's off to Vampyrium and won't forgive Vanescula.
compliment: Drakan's roof. Up and down again. That was you, they're saying.
Saradomin bless you, if you stood with Queen Efaritay against Drakan.
shady/insult: Centuries of order undone by a mortal, how very quaint.
Enjoy the quiet, hero. Some of us preferred the old ways.
The tithe kept order. Now everyone's just... free, and it's ghastly.
Drakan ruled for centuries. You're a footnote with a flail.
burgher/gossip: Vitur fellow says no more tithe. Hope he can read his own notice.
burgher/compliment: You done for Drakan, proper? Just wait till I tell me mum.

gossip: They say another Blood Moon festival's due. Lock your doors, or don't.
Something's moving under the castle, and they whisper of tunnels.
Safalaan's still in Drakan's hands, and Veliaf's gone quiet about it.
burgher/gossip: Blood Moon coming, they say. Don't need to read to know that's bad.

gossip: The Myreque are finished, folk reckon. Castle Drakan still stands.
Vanstrom Klause is gone. Burgh de Rott had a quiet drink about it.
Lord Drakan burnt half the Myreque in his own courtyard, I'm told.
compliment: Remarkable, into Darkmeyer and out again, and still with a pulse.
Bless you! You're the one who stopped Slepe's sickness spreading?
plain/insult: You took the Myreque to Castle Drakan. Veliaf doesn't talk about it.
You keep lovely company, plotting with Vanescula Drakan like that.
burgher/gossip: The Myreque went off to the castle, and fewer came back.

gossip: Plague in Slepe again. Nobody goes near the place.
Veliaf's gone to Slepe. Something about the sickness, he said.
Slepe's sickness is spreading, and nobody's even close to a cure.
Something's wrong with Lady Verzik. Something with more legs.
If Lady Verzik died long ago, like they whisper, who's on the stage?
compliment: Into the Theatre and out again, when most only manage the in?
You've seen what's really on that stage, and you still sleep?
plain/insult: Spoiling the Lady's shows. Sinhaza had so few pleasures.
The Theatre had a perfectly good name until you went in.

gossip: The Lady's recruiting for her show. Nobody ever plays twice, mind.
Sinhaza's been quiet. Too quiet. The Lady's planning something.
They say Brumty's sheep came up all colours, and he called it plague.
Someone got inside the mourners' place. And out again, which is new.
compliment: You're the one who got inside the mourners' headquarters?
Clever of you to see through the mourners' plague, I hear.
plain/insult: West Ardougne took sick on bad grain, and some say you helped.

gossip: I hear the Temple of Light's lit again, whatever that means.
Someone went all the way down to the Death Altar, down there!
compliment: You've been to the Temple of Light and found your way back out?

gossip: Someone let a Mahjarrat out of the pyramid, just let him out!
compliment: You found all four of those diamonds? That took some working out.
Blimey, four guardians, four diamonds, and you're still standing?
plain/insult: Freed something ancient from a pyramid, and I'm sure it's grateful.
Was it a fair trade, a Mahjarrat loose for a few new spells?

gossip: Odd sort, that archaeologist at the Bedabin Camp wanting diamonds.
The bandits say something's buried under the desert, something old.
Sophanem's pox has lifted, and Menaphos keeps saying it'll open.
The Champion of Scabaras is dead. The beetles have been sulking since.
compliment: You're the adventurer from Ullek? The High Priest prays for you.
Zahur says it was you fetched the Lily of the Elid for Sophanem.
plain/insult: Menaphos says its gates will open for you, and I'd not hold my breath.
Zahur did the brewing while you carried a flower about, very prettily.

gossip: Sophanem's sick again and Menaphos has bolted its gates, again.
There's a sickness in Sophanem the healers can't name.
The Moons are sealed below again. Eyatlalli saw to the ritual.
compliment: You went down under Cam Torum? I'd not go for all the gold in it.
Cam Torum sleeps easier since you helped Eyatlalli with the Moons.
dwarf/compliment: Brave, for one so tall, going under Cam Torum for the Moons.

gossip: The Teokan of Ranul was the Augur all along, all along!
Furia Tullus is in a cell. The Prince spoke for her, they say.
Ennius Tullus is dead. The Queen herself was there.
They say Teumo's name isn't spoken in Cam Torum now, not once.
compliment: You walked into the cult beside the Prince in robes and all, they say!
Wait. You're the one the Prince gave his grandfather's blade to?
The story going round is you stood beside the Queen against Ennius.
plain/insult: The Dawn still comes, friend. You only delayed the sun.
Metzli lied, they say. As if the palace has ever done otherwise.
The Augur's dead. The faith isn't. You can't stab a sunrise.
dwarf/remark: They say Teumo sold out Cam Torum, and dwarves don't forgive that.

gossip: Emissaries preaching in the market again and nobody stops them.
They say the Prince is missing, taken by the Emissaries.
King Hosidius, crowned and killed the same day, so Artur rules now.
The Council's in irons. Andrews and Unkar, awaiting trial.
Poor Rose. Twenty years in a shack, and no cure at the end.
compliment: You fought that demon out at Molch? Braver than me, and no mistake.
Wait, you helped Martin Holt bring down the Council?
plain/insult: Lord Shayzien stepped aside for Hosidius, and look how that ended.
Under the Council the houses squabbled. Under a king they still do.

gossip: Martin Holt's shouting at the castle again, and the guards never move.
The Council says the King's daughter went mad, which is convenient.
West Ardougne's still walled off. Plague, the mourners say.
The dwarves at Cam Torum say the Moons are restless below.
Druids whisper about Lucien. Druids don't whisper for nothing.
They say Lucien grows bolder, and someone ought to worry about it.

compliment: The hooded fellow in the pub wants brave sorts, so would that be you?
That stranger in the pub wants weapons carried, and you've the arms.
insult: Hooded chap's still waiting on steel, and the shops sell it.
plain/insult: Freedom fighters in the swamp and you in the pub sounds about right.
remark: That hooded fellow's been nursing the same seat for days.
gossip: Some call the Myreque freedom fighters and others say terrorists.
Rebels hiding in the myre, they say. Hidden in the myre, even.
Strangers in the pub asking about the Myreque, with eyes everywhere.
starter/compliment: Hello there. Vanstrom Klause. You look the heroic sort, stranger.
Bring the weapons back to me and I'll give you a nice surprise.
starter/insult: Any luck finding the Myreque? No? Shame. I'd so love to meet them.
starter/remark: The Myreque are the real meat and drink of high adventure, they say.

compliment: Blimey! You're the one who saw off that hellhound in the Hollows?
You stood your ground when that hellhound came, word is, fair play.
insult: Six swords into a swamp, I hear. Not so much as a thank-you, I'd bet.
plain/insult: Good of you to lead Vanstrom right to the Myreque's door, they say.
remark: That hooded fellow's gone from the pub. Someone else has his chair.
gossip: Sani Piliu's dead. And Harold Evans. Vanstrom's work, all of it.
Vanstrom was a vampyre all along. Sat in our pub, bold as brass.
The Myreque have left the Hollows. Vanstrom knows the place, see.
starter/compliment: Hello, friend! I'm not Vanstrom, just a man who owns a chair.
starter/insult: You looked ready to run me through back there, and I'm not even him.
starter/remark: Steady on! I hope that score you've to settle is with someone else.

compliment: Veliaf's looking for a new hideout. You've a nose for places, friend.
Burgh de Rott, Veliaf says. Someone brave needs to go first.
insult: You look like you've slept in worse. Any ideas for a new hideout?
plain/insult: Vanstrom knows this cave. Standing about in it isn't a plan.
remark: Vanstrom knows where we are. Every creak sounds like a vyre.
gossip: Veliaf says Burgh de Rott's full of folk who fled Meiyerditch.
Ivan's not slept since Sani... none of us have, really.
Silver, Veliaf says. Take silver if you're going near a vampyre.
starter/compliment: Well met, friend. We need a new hideout, and you've the legs for it.
starter/insult: Burgh de Rott, and take silver, and try not to lead anyone to us.
starter/remark: We're really not that organised, as Vanstrom rather proved.

compliment: You put Gadderanks down? Nobody round here will mourn him.
Aurel's shop, the bank and the furnace, all your doing, so they say.
insult: Funny how the tithe men turned up right after you fixed that shop.
plain/insult: Was it cosy, that furnace you lit for Vanstrom to smell?
remark: Cornelius is a banker now. Never thought I'd see it in Burgh de Rott.
gossip: Gadderanks is dead. Begged for his family at the end, I'm told.
The Myreque are under the inn now. Don't tell anyone I said so.
Young Ivan's gone to the Salve priest, safer there, Veliaf says.
burgher/compliment: You fixed up the village! A shop and a bank, whatever a bank is.
burgher/gossip: Got a furnace now. Nobody knows what to put in it.
burgher/remark: Gadderanks is gone. Can't say I'll miss him.

compliment: Veliaf wants word from Meiyerditch. You've been through worse, friend.
Veliaf thinks you're the one to get round that wall.
insult: Meiyerditch is east. The boat's south. Neither's in this cellar.
plain/insult: The Sanguinesti lot might be dead. Standing here won't tell us.
remark: Nobody's heard from the Sanguinesti in an age.
gossip: The Vyrewatch can't be killed, Veliaf says, not even with the rod.
A wall round Meiyerditch, and a rotten boat round the wall.
They say humans are farmed like cattle in Meiyerditch.
starter/compliment: Well met, friend. If you've no news for me then I've a job for you.
starter/insult: Meiyerditch, to the east, and do take precautions this time.
starter/remark: Even the Rod of Ivandis does nothing at all to the Vyrewatch.

compliment: The Sanguinesti are alive? Veliaf hasn't smiled like that in years.
Private, is it? Safalaan doesn't recommend just anyone.
insult: I hear you drew three castle pictures and the vampyres loved them.
plain/insult: Vanstrom put you on the floor. Vanescula's servant saved you.
remark: Roald sent his regards and no soldiers, on account of the edicts.
gossip: Werewolves crossing the Salve for tithes, if you please... the Salve!
Safalaan's alive and sketching Castle Drakan, which is brave or daft.
Vanescula Drakan's taken an interest in Safalaan, they whisper.
starter/compliment: Well met, Private. Safalaan speaks well of you, and Myreque prevail.
starter/insult: So Roald sent no troops. Did you actually beg, as I told you to?
starter/remark: This war is far from over. Plenty of time to contribute.

compliment: Garth tells a fine tale about Serafina, worth a listen, friend.
You've the look of someone who might survive the Theatre, and few do.
insult: Thousands went into the Theatre and one came out, so don't get ideas.
plain/insult: You're not here for the tithe, are you? You've the pallor for it.
remark: Serafina. Everyone here knows the name. Nobody knows where she went.
gossip: The Lady promises freedom to any who survive her Theatre, any at all.
Blood tithes by sector. So nobody runs out all at once.
Garth's told the Serafina story so often the guards mouth along.
starter/compliment: Hello there, would you care to hear the tale of Serafina?
starter/insult: The tale of Serafina? It's long. You look like you've the time.
starter/remark: Only one person in all of history has ever survived the Theatre.

compliment: Ye gods, you're the one who killed Ranis Drakan, with a flail?
The Slayer, they call you now. The whole city heard your speech.
insult: Killed a Drakan on the castle steps? That was ever so subtle of you.
plain/insult: Half the Sanguinesti died for those notes, and you kept the flail.
shady/insult: Ranis kept the tithes orderly. Now the cattle think they can bite.
A human with a flail. Lord Drakan will be so very amused.
remark: Ranis dead on the castle steps, and not a word from the castle since.
gossip: Ranis Drakan is dead. Killed by a human, in front of everyone.
Serafina never left, they whisper. She's still in that Theatre.
Flaygian, Mekritus, Andiess. The Myreque lost three in one night.
starter/compliment: I used to tell the tale of Serafina, and now they ask for yours.
starter/insult: Careful talking of the Myreque round here, unless you like trouble.
starter/remark: Nobody's seen Lord Drakan in years. Vanescula turns up now and then.

compliment: Help Edmond, friend. His girl went over the wall three weeks back.
Would you give Edmond a hand? He's been digging that garden for days.
insult: Edmond's daughter's still over that wall, not that it's your wall.
plain/insult: West Ardougne's walled off. So far it's kept you out beautifully.
remark: They say there's plague behind that wall, but nobody says what kind.
gossip: Edmond's Elena is a healer. Went west to help, never came back.
The mourners run West Ardougne now, masks and all.
They blame King Tyras over there for bringing the plague home.
starter/compliment: You'd help? Elena crossed the wall to heal them and never came back.
starter/insult: Can't stop to talk unless you've a spade. Have you got a spade on you?
starter/remark: The soil's rock hard... buckets of water... that grill in the sewer...

compliment: Bless you! Are you the one who got Elena out of West Ardougne?
Clever, digging through Edmond's garden into the sewers, I hear.
insult: I hear the hero of Ardougne brewed a hangover cure for the warder.
plain/insult: Crawled through a sewer in a gas mask for a girl you'd never met?
remark: Edmond's garden's never been the same, not that he minds.
gossip: Elena's home. Walked in the front door before her rescuer did.
A black cross on the door means plague. Or kidnappers, it turns out.
Bravek signed a warrant for the plague house, hungover, mind you.
starter/compliment: Ah, hello! Thank you again for rescuing my daughter.
starter/insult: Did you know Elena beat you back here by minutes?
starter/remark: The sewer passage closed up after you, which is probably for the best.

compliment: Could you help Elena? She's got samples and nothing to test them with.
You've the nerve to get Elena's distillator back off the mourners.
insult: Elena's waiting on her equipment. The mourners aren't posting it.
plain/insult: Elena wants a distillator fetched. You don't know what one is, do you?
remark: Elena's been shut in with her samples since she got back.
gossip: The mourners took Elena's equipment for 'safety', or so they said.
Odd hobby for odd times, Jerico and his pigeons by the wall.
Elena wants to test that plague herself, and the mourners said no.
starter/compliment: Hey! Thanks again for freeing me. Now, about my distillator...
starter/insult: Being kidnapped was inconvenient, so do try to avoid it yourself.
starter/remark: I can't test a single sample without that distillator.

compliment: Good on you for getting Elena's kit back off the mourners, I hear.
Some nerve, walking into the mourners' place dressed as a doctor!
insult: Child's play, putting a rotten apple in the mourners' stew like that.
plain/insult: Very holy of you, running three vials to Varrock in a priest's robe.
remark: Elena keeps saying she wishes she knew what's going on over there.
gossip: They say the west gate opens for friends of the King now.
The mourners had a stomach upset, and bad stew is what they say.
Elena's distillator is back. The mourners say nothing about it.
starter/compliment: Hey! Now I can finally run these tests, thanks to you.
starter/insult: The touch paper didn't change. Nothing. Try not to look so pleased.
starter/remark: Even without the plague, I still worry about the people over there.

compliment: The King wants a way west through the pass, and you look sure-footed.
Lathas needs the pass crossed. His best soldiers didn't manage it.
insult: Soldiers fell in that pass and it's still shut, but you've a warm pub.
sharp/insult: The King asked for a warrior. He's making do with you, citizen.
remark: Cultists in the pass now, they say. As if it weren't bad enough.
gossip: Some of the King's best men went into the pass and didn't come back.
King Tyras is gathering strength out west, the palace says.
Poor Koftik, the King's tracker, still waiting at the pass.
starter/compliment: Ah, adventurer. I assume you're here about my brother?
starter/insult: The pass has swallowed my best soldiers, but I'm sure you'll be fine.
starter/remark: My brother gathers strength in the west. A way through must be found.

compliment: Word is you did for Iban. Called himself Zamorak's son, you know.
You found the way west through the pass? The King can't stop smiling.
insult: I hear you dropped a doll down a well and called it a victory.
sharp/insult: How interesting that three paladins went in and only you came out.
remark: Koftik's himself again but can't remember a thing, they say.
gossip: Iban is dead, I'm told. The temple came down on top of him.
The King's men are building a well in the pass, a Well of Voyage.
There's a witch still in that pass, the soldiers say, with a cat.
starter/compliment: Incredible, adventurer. A true warrior. Your loyalty inspires us all.
starter/insult: Iban's gone. My brother isn't. Don't get comfortable, adventurer.
starter/remark: Once the Well is finished, we move against my brother at last.

compliment: The King wants someone with nerve for the Well road west, maybe you?
They say elves wait out west for Lathas's envoy, and that's you.
insult: The King's errand is still waiting. The Well's not going anywhere.
sharp/insult: Lord Iorwerth's expecting someone impressive, so do break it gently.
remark: Elves out west, the King says... elves!
gossip: King Tyras is west with an army, and the palace wants him gone.
An elf lord's offered King Lathas his full support, an elf lord!
They call it Tirannwn. Elf country, full of traps from what I hear.
starter/compliment: Adventurer! Through the Well. Lord Iorwerth's elves will meet you.
starter/insult: Leave me, citizen! Oh, it's you. Well, go on then and say your piece.
starter/remark: My brother... the Dark Lord... it all ends in the west.

compliment: Word is you crossed Tirannwn and lived. The traps alone, ye gods.
The King's pleased with you, so they say, and he's not easily pleased.
insult: Is blowing up a king's tent with a barrel what they call diplomacy?
sharp/insult: Killed a king because another king asked, and never checked which?
remark: King Tyras is dead, so why's the wall still up?
gossip: A flying fireball did for King Tyras, the story goes, a fireball!
The plague must remain, the palace says. Even now, after everything.
I'm told the elves out west are at war among themselves, of all folk.
starter/compliment: Well done, citizen, an excellent job, and this will do nicely.
starter/insult: I've nothing for you right now, citizen, so do stop hovering.
starter/remark: Even with my brother gone, the plague must remain... for now.

compliment: Maybe this human isn't as bad as Islwyn thinks.
Arianwyn said a human might come. Islwyn's not happy about it.
insult: You're the human that killed Tyras? Islwyn won't want to hear it.
plain/insult: Humans only take and destroy, says Islwyn, so prove him wrong.
remark: Islwyn's grandmother was Glarial. The queen herself, that was.
gossip: Arianwyn's told the forest about the one who killed Tyras.
Islwyn's bows are crystal. Far superior to human work, he says.
starter/compliment: Very well, human. There's something you must do first.
starter/insult: All you humans do is take and destroy, so why would we want your help?
starter/remark: It was humans that led to my grandmother's death, and I don't forget.

compliment: You consecrated Glarial's tomb? Even Islwyn admits he was wrong!
Crystal from Islwyn's own stock? He doesn't give that to anyone.
insult: I hear you killed a moss guardian for a seed, and the moss is furious.
plain/insult: One seed by a waterfall and the elves forgave you, which seems easy.
remark: Good that Glarial rests under the falls now, properly.
gossip: Care and compassion, Islwyn said of the human, and he said it sober.
Eluned's taking the human to Lletya, to Arianwyn himself.
Ilfeen will re-chant crystal if you find her in the forest.
starter/compliment: Ahh, good to see you back. After more crystal equipment?
starter/insult: I admit I was wrong about you. Don't make me say it twice.
starter/remark: My grandmother rests under the waterfall now, and where better?

compliment: Have you seen the delegation from Varlamore at the palace yet?
Alina in the square can't stop talking of Varlamore, so humour her.
insult: Foreign princes at the palace, and here's you, just standing about.
remark: The Shining Kingdom, they call it. Shut for hundreds of years.
gossip: A Varlamore prince at the palace, says the Herald, with knights too.
I hear Varlamore's opening up for trade over the western sea.
Noah reckons a kingdom shut for centuries sounds like a prison.
starter/compliment: The delegation from Varlamore! Do you not want to be first there?
starter/insult: Varlamore! The Shining Kingdom! And you've not even heard of it?
starter/remark: Far across the western sea, over the mountains... just think of it!
heartland/insult: Varlamore's opening up, they say. Not to the likes of you, guv.

compliment: Sharp eyes, marking out those bandits in the square like that.
Fair play to you for saving that Varlamore priest from a knife.
insult: Followed a guard round Varrock, I hear. Did he give you a sweet after?
remark: Sergeant Tobyn's been very pleased with himself lately.
gossip: Four bandits in guards' armour, arrested right there in the square!
The treaty's signed, says the Herald. Varlamore's open to anyone now.
That prince was up on the palace roof asking questions, I hear.
heartland/insult: Bandit guards fooled everyone but you, guv, and that says a lot.

compliment: Isn't it you the Prince means, asking after the outsider from Varrock?
The Tullus twins want a word with you. That's an honour, round here.
insult: The Tullus twins are waiting on you, and they don't like waiting.
plain/insult: An outsider, summoned by the Prince. The twins looked unimpressed.
remark: The Teokan of Ralos hasn't been seen since Varrock, they say.
gossip: Someone tried to kill the Teokan in Varrock, of all places!
The twins organised the whole delegation, and they'll tell you so.
The Prince is keeping his father close. Very close, the knights say.
starter/compliment: The Prince wishes to speak with you, so do not keep him waiting.
starter/insult: You don't look like much, but the Prince asked for you, so go.
starter/remark: We organised the whole delegation ourselves, as was our duty.

compliment: You're the outsider who rounded up all six knights, on your own?
You held the Teomat against the cultists? May the sun light your way.
insult: You sobered up a knight at a fountain? The stuff of legend, that.
plain/insult: Six knights rounded up, one traitor, and the Teokan still got stabbed.
remark: Metzli's gone. Ask the priests and watch them change the subject.
gossip: They say Ennius Tullus executed that knight Velam on the spot.
The Teokan was stabbed at the Teomat, but we're told he'll live.
Metzli, Teokan of Ranul, vanished the night of the attack.
starter/compliment: You've done well, outsider. The Prince will want to hear it from you.
starter/insult: What's done is done, so do not dwell on it, or on us.
starter/remark: You're in Varlamore now, and this is how we deal with traitors.

compliment: The Prince needs someone to trust with his plan, and he named you.
Servius is on his feet again. He asks after you, they say.
insult: The Prince has a plan nobody likes, and you're in it.
plain/insult: The Queen wants whoever the Prince trusts. Pity it's an outsider, eh?
remark: The Queen was here. Nobody's seen the Prince smile since.
gossip: Cultists are recruiting out in the gorge, they whisper.
The Queen came to the Teomat herself, and words were had.
Twice now someone's tried to kill the Teokan, and twice is plenty.
starter/compliment: Nilsal! I've a plan you'll like. Well, you won't like it, but hear it.
starter/insult: Nilsal. You're the only one I trust now, and you're an outsider.
starter/remark: Father will recover. His would-be killers are still out there.

compliment: Into the Emissaries' tower with the Prince? I'd not have slept a wink.
They say you fought a frost nagua alone in the ruins and walked out.
insult: Joined a cult in a robe, I hear. Did they at least feed you?
plain/insult: Went in with the Prince and came out without him, which was careless.
remark: Servius says he won't bow to a knife wound, nor to anything else.
gossip: The Prince is gone. Taken from the ruins. Metzli's work, Servius says.
Metzli leads the Emissaries. Their Augur. The Teokan of Ranul herself.
The Tullus twins are Ralos and Ranul reborn, the cult says, reborn!
Servius says they'll all burn in the light of Ralos, and he means it.

compliment: Ask the woman in that tent nicely, as she knows a way into Sophanem.
That woman in the tent is waiting for someone, and it might be you.
insult: Sophanem's shut tight. You'll not get in by staring at it.
plain/insult: Camping outside plague-ridden Sophanem? Are you bold or just daft?
remark: They say Sophanem's locked down with plagues, and more than one.
gossip: Odd timing, a new High Priest in Sophanem and plagues the same week.
There's a red-haired woman camped by the pyramid who hates cats.
Desert nights are cold. That woman in the tent has no tinderbox.
starter/compliment: Hello, adventurer. A full waterskin and a tinderbox, and we'll talk.
starter/insult: You smell of cats. Keep those filthy creatures well away from me.
starter/remark: These desert nights are very cold... I seem to have lost my tinderbox.

compliment: You put Klenter's jar back? The priests still talk of it.
Icthlarin bless you, standing against the Devourer like that.
insult: Robbed a tomb and then put it all back? Make your mind up, friend.
plain/insult: Robbed Klenter's pyramid under a spell? Convenient sort of spell.
remark: Klenter's ghost has gone quiet at last, thank Icthlarin.
That cat of yours opened a pyramid door, the clever puss, they say.
gossip: That tent by the pyramid is empty. Nobody saw the woman leave.
A priest was possessed at the ceremony, and he's recovered... mostly.
The pox is still with us. The new High Priest looks tired.

compliment: The High Priest wants someone unafraid of Menaphos, and you'd do.
Our people are stuck in Menaphos. The High Priest could use you.
insult: Menaphos won't open its gates. Can't blame them, looking at you.
plain/insult: Not caught the plague yet? Call that your great deed so far.
remark: The bank's a hole in the ground since the beetles came up.
gossip: The High Priest took a party to the Menaphos bridge and got shot at.
Pharaoh Kemesis leads Menaphos in a secular way, the priests sigh.
Things came up through the temple cellar before the plagues... things.
starter/compliment: You'd really be willing to help us again? Then come closer and listen.
starter/insult: My focus is on the dead. You're not quite there yet, so listen.
starter/remark: Those guards are our brethren, and we will not fight our own.

compliment: Blessings! You're the one who killed that giant scarab under the city?
Our people came home from Menaphos among the dead, thanks to you.
insult: Poor Jex got clubbed, and not by you, so they say... still.
plain/insult: Al Kharid's spies all over Sophanem now, and who brought the first in?
remark: The bank's back under the temple. The merchants are open again.
gossip: Kaleef is dead down there. A keris still in the beast, I'm told.
Menaphos sent over its dead, and some of ours walked out of the pile!
Trade with Al Kharid now, if you please. The High Priest's not keen.
starter/compliment: Hello again. Our city of the dead is slowly coming back to life.
starter/insult: Only this infuriating pox left. No cure in your pack, I take it.
starter/remark: Menaphos stays shut till every last plague is gone, they insist.

compliment: The pirate on the west dock says he's after company for Lunar Isle.
Brundt talks of peace with the Moon Clan. It'd take someone like you.
insult: The Moon Clan have hated us for centuries, but they've not met you.
plain/insult: Off to the Moon Clan? They do everything by magic, so you'll fit in.
remark: Lokar Searunner, half pirate, half Fremennik, and all mouth.
gossip: Lokar ran off to be a pirate. Rellekka bored him, he tells everyone.
The Moon Clan do everything by magic. Won't share a word of it.
Hundreds of years at war with the Moon Clan, and still no end.
starter/compliment: Hey, got that seal thingy off the chief loser yet, so we can sail?
starter/insult: I've no time for the likes of you. Fine, then, what is it you want?
starter/remark: Growing crops and milking cows? So boring, which is why I left.

compliment: Brundt says you dreamed with the Moon Clan and woke up again after.
Brundt says there's progress with the Moon Clan now, thanks to you.
insult: You had to fight yourself in a dream, I hear, so which of you won?
plain/insult: Made friends with the Moon Clan, did you? Keep the spells to yourself.
fremennik/insult: Back from Lunar Isle smelling of spells. Wash before the longhall.
remark: They say Baba Yaga's house walks about on its own chicken legs!
gossip: The pirates' ship sailed in circles. Jinxed by a cabin boy, no less.
Brundt reckons we can really make progress with the Moon Clan now.
The Moon Clan are spreading word about an open-minded mainlander.
starter/remark: Loserville, full of losers, and I'm the one who ferries people to it.
