compliment: Mord on the north dock's looking for you. Something about the isles.
Trolls on the northern isles, they say. You'd be useful up there.
insult: Jatizso's king needs an errand-runner, and apparently you'll do.
plain/insult: Mord's on the dock. He's a ferryman. The boat won't come to you.
remark: Jatizso and Neitiznot. Four generations of 'is so', 'is not'.
gossip: Trolls razed Neitiznot, a whole town, gone!
Jatizso's king taxes all that moves. And some things that don't.
Imagine dinner with Mord from Jatizso and his wife from Neitiznot.
starter/compliment: Mord Gunnars, humble ferryman. Would you fancy seeing Jatizso?
starter/insult: I'm surprised King Sorvott wants you, and don't expect any gratitude.
starter/remark: Nine days and nine nights the full history takes, if you ask Maria.

compliment: You took the Troll King's head? Neitiznot sings of you for that.
They say Burowgar gave you the helm off his own head!
fremennik/compliment: Slayer of the Troll King! Sit by me at the longhall, brother.
insult: I hear you collected window tax for King Sorvott, hero of the people.
plain/insult: Spied in a jester's hat for Sorvott, and he still called you a liar.
remark: Sorvott still says the Troll King lives and calls doubt preposterous.
gossip: The Ice Troll King is dead. Burowgar has the head to prove it.
Neitiznot's bridges are fixed and they're mining runite again.
A beard tax on Jatizso now, would you believe it!
Yak meat's still banned on Jatizso, by order of the King.
starter/compliment: Hail the conquering hero! Anything I can do for you?
starter/insult: Tax collector, is it? You're not going to tax me, are you?
starter/remark: Ja, it iz so. Ne, it iz not. And so it goes every single morning.

compliment: Veos on the dock has work for a mainlander, and you'd suit it.
You look well travelled, Veos needs someone to visit all five cities.
insult: Veos is looking for someone curious. He may lower his standards.
plain/insult: Fresh off the boat and already loitering. Veos will find you a job.
remark: Veos keeps on about a client from the mainland but never says who.
gossip: Who's this client of Veos's on the mainland, asking after Kourend?
No king here for twenty years, so the Council rules, such as it is.
Veos tells every soul who lands to beware the thieves in Piscarilius.
starter/compliment: Hello again! Interested in telling my client all about Kourend?
starter/insult: Hello again! Nothing for you... unless you'd walk to five cities?
starter/remark: A quill, a scroll and a client who sees all, so I never ask questions.

compliment: Thorough, touring all five cities for Veos like that.
That takes nerve, going all the way to the Dark Altar for a stranger.
insult: I hear you smashed an orb at the Dark Altar for someone you never met.
plain/insult: Very scholarly of you, burning your hand on a glowing quill.
remark: Veos went very odd for a moment and not in his own voice, they say.
gossip: Veos's client never gave a name. Knowledge can be a curse, he says.
Something was done at the Dark Altar, the Arceuus folk mutter.
Veos says his client's very pleased. Veos doesn't remember saying it.
starter/compliment: Hello again, friend! What can I do for you? Anywhere you'd like to go?
starter/insult: I haven't spoken to you since the boat, whatever you may think.
starter/remark: Knowledge can be a curse... did I say that, or did somebody else?

compliment: Tomas Lawry wants the gangs looked at, and you look the part for it.
Somebody ought to look into these gangs and their so-called queen.
insult: Tomas Lawry needs someone who looks poor. He'll be thrilled with you.
plain/insult: The Saviours recruit from the gutter, so mind how you stand.
remark: They say a new gang's swallowing the old ones, the Saviours.
gossip: The gangs have a queen now, and nobody's seen her face.
The Saviours of Kourend. Saving us from what, I'd like to know.
Robert O'Reilly would sell his mother for a stew, and we get fish.
starter/compliment: Greetings. You look poor. Perfect. I've important Council business.
starter/insult: Greetings. Important Council business, and I suppose you'll do.
starter/remark: Gangs. A nuisance, but manageable. Until this queen of theirs.

compliment: Good riddance to Councillor Hughes, and I hear that was your doing.
Bold as you like, getting into the Saviours' warren and out again.
insult: Joined a gang to catch a gang, I hear. Which one are you in now?
plain/insult: Conrad King turns up dead on the docks just as you turn up in town?
remark: Lawry's practising an acceptance speech. For a seat he hasn't got.
gossip: Councillor Hughes is in a cell at the castle, Yama cultists, no less!
Funny how the gangs' queen was never caught, isn't it?
Devan Rutter's still about. Business as usual on the docks.
starter/compliment: You've done a great service to Kourend. I'll mention you in my speech.
starter/insult: Yes, yes, very good job. Now be on your way. I've a lot of work to do.
starter/remark: Forget the thieves. Hughes and those vile Disciples of Yama...

compliment: Lord Kandur's son is missing. He'd be glad of a steady pair of hands.
Young Artur's gone off somewhere. Help the Lord find him, friend.
insult: Artur's still missing. Even the kitchen staff have looked harder.
plain/insult: The Lord's son's lost and you're stood here admiring the vines?
remark: Elena Hosidius says Artur's meant for greatness... nearly said king.
gossip: Artur's gone missing. The Lord won't say where, or can't.
Chef Olivia knows more about Artur than she lets on, I'd wager.
Artur was always off in the Arceuus Library with his old books.
starter/compliment: Hello, friend. My eldest boy Artur is missing and I need your help.
starter/insult: A shame we could not meet in better circumstances, or better company.
starter/remark: Artur is still missing, and I've asked my family and every servant.

compliment: Bless you! You're the one who brought Artur home from the caves?
Word is you found the old Accord that everyone said was lost at sea.
insult: Hosidius rejoices because you hopped some stones and killed a snake.
plain/insult: Lord Kandur thanked you. Artur found the chest and you carried it.
remark: Lord Kandur keeps that old Accord close, and says he's no need of it.
gossip: The Royal Accord of Twill's in Hosidius now, the original, no less!
Artur says it's time for another golden age, but he says it quietly.
Words cut deeper than blades, says Lord Kandur, odd for a farmer.
starter/compliment: Artur is home safe. I hear we have you to thank for that, friend.
starter/insult: I assume you're after what I promised, so here it is, until next time.
starter/remark: The Accord is a weapon, and I've no need to use it... not yet.

compliment: Perhaps you'll help Mori find her friend, since the Council won't.
Someone in Arceuus has died. Died! You look like you'd ask why.
insult: Someone's died in Arceuus. Not that you'd know what that means here.
plain/insult: The Council did nothing for Mori. You're keeping pace with them.
remark: The people of Arceuus don't get ill. That's what we always said.
gossip: A woman called Thana has died, in Arceuus, and that's not possible.
Mori went to the Council about it. They sent her away, of course.
The Dark Altar flickered, they whisper, and nobody says it aloud.
starter/compliment: You'd help? Thank you, friend. The Council wouldn't even listen.
starter/insult: The Council never do anything for the people, and nor do most folk.
starter/remark: She's... dead... Thana... but our kind are not supposed to die.

compliment: Thank you, for saving Arceuus from... whatever that was.
Few dare go to the Tasakaal under Mount Karuulm, but word is you did.
insult: You smashed a strange device by the altar? Was it even the right one?
plain/insult: You saved the immortals. Try saving someone who needed it.
remark: They say Lord Arceuus is out of his trance, and quieter than before.
gossip: Who'd dare sabotage the Dark Altar, and deliberately at that?
Lord Arceuus took immortality for his dying wife, the Tasakaal say.
Mori goes up to the church to think about Thana, so leave her be.
starter/compliment: Hello there. Thank you for helping us. A good friend to Arceuus.
starter/insult: I come here to think quietly, friend, and that was a hint.
starter/remark: It's my way of remembering Thana, a quiet place to think.

compliment: The Assembly's after someone handy. The Doors of Dinh are failing.
You look handy, and Councillor Unkar needs the Doors seen to.
insult: The Doors of Dinh are failing. You're on the wrong side of them.
plain/insult: Lady Vulcana wants you gone and a sherry brought, in that order.
remark: Lady Vulcana's on her third sherry and it's not yet noon.
gossip: The Doors of Dinh have a hole in them. The Wintertodt's noticed.
Lady Vulcana doesn't like urgency, and she said so at some length.
Undor at the camp says only Dinh's own hammer can mend those Doors.
starter/compliment: Oh, a human. Councillor Unkar has a job for you, and I need a sherry.
starter/insult: Who is this human, and why is it still here, and where's my sherry?
starter/remark: Urgency. I don't like urgency. This is quite simply not on.

compliment: So you're the one Undor keeps going on about, the hammer, was it?
Undor says the Doors can be mended now. Thanks to a human, no less.
dwarf/compliment: Dinh's own hammer, back in a dwarf's hand. By Guthix, that's proper.
insult: Thirsty work, pouring water between jugs for an hour like that.
plain/insult: Found a hammer in a tower, I hear. Undor did the actual mending.
remark: The Wintertodt grew strong while those Doors were cracked, they say.
gossip: Dinh's own hammer out of that tower after all these years, fancy!
Someone made that hole in the Doors on purpose, Undor reckons.
Lady Vulcana celebrated the Doors with a sherry... then another.
starter/compliment: Oh look, it's the human. Hello, human. Wonderful stuff, the hammer.
starter/insult: Oh. The human is still here. Councillor, why is the human still here?
starter/remark: My plans? Let me think... ah, I know! I shall have another sherry.

compliment: Old Phileas would love a visitor, with a mystery about his ancestor.
Phileas Rimor got a parcel with no name on it and could use a hand.
insult: No rush, then, with Phileas and his thousand-year-old mystery.
plain/insult: Nobody digs on Quidamortem without Lord Shayzien's say, so ask nicely.
remark: Magnus Rimor led the King's expedition and never came back, they say.
gossip: A journal turned up at Phileas's door, with no name and no sender.
King Shayzien the Seventh sent men up Quidamortem, the old story goes.
Phileas was a soldier once. Now he talks to anyone who'll stop.
starter/compliment: Hello there! Not often I get visitors. You know, there's something...
starter/insult: Hello there. Visitors! Well, a visitor. Don't rush off like the last.
starter/remark: Magnus Rimor... the mountain... who sends a parcel with no name?

compliment: You roped down under Quidamortem? I'd not have trusted the rope.
Word is you brought back proof from the mountain, lizards and all.
insult: Killed a lizard in a cave and called it history, I hear.
plain/insult: Phileas is gone and his house is wrecked. You were the last to call.
remark: Phileas's house was turned over, and nobody's seen him since.
gossip: Phileas Rimor's gone missing. Lord Shayzien's men are asking about.
The bones said lizards on the mountain and do not trust the King.
Lord Shayzien wants anything from the mountain brought to him first.

compliment: Cook's cooking for someone very important tonight, give him a hand?
insult: Cook's still short of a rotten tomato. It's not a hard thing to find.
plain/insult: Cook wants a Dirty Blast. Don't ask me what that is, ask him.
remark: Cook's got some ancient cookbook out, there's dust everywhere.
gossip: Hush-hush, but they whisper of some important meeting at the castle.
Cook's ancestor cooked a feast here a hundred years ago, he says.
Cook's after greenman's ale now, and that's a Castle Wars drink.
starter/compliment: My friend! I'm in a pickle and need someone trustworthy, like you!
starter/insult: It's a very important meeting, so do try to hurry, for once.
starter/remark: Franizzard Van Lumbcook... a job for life... and here I am, a failure.

compliment: King Arthur's after a worthy sort to free Merlin, and you'd do.
insult: Merlin's been stuck in that crystal for ages, so no hurry, clearly.
plain/insult: The knights can't free Merlin. I'd not fancy your chances either.
remark: They moved Merlin up to his tower, crystal and all.
gossip: They say Merlin's got himself trapped in a crystal, and him a wizard!
Some say a witch put Merlin in that crystal, and the knights won't.
starter/compliment: Welcome to my court! Seek knighthood? Then help me free Merlin.
starter/insult: Lancelot doubts a commoner could free Merlin, so do prove him wrong.
starter/remark: Merlin, trapped in a crystal. And he was the clever one.
kid/remark: If the wizard's really stuck in a crystal, can I go and see?

compliment: Word is you freed Merlin. Camelot's grateful, traveller.
Fair play, an honorary knight of the Round Table!
insult: I hear Merlin's free. That crystal would've made a lovely lamp, mind.
plain/insult: Honorary knight, is it? The honorary bit's doing a lot of work.
gossip: They say Excalibur itself shattered Merlin's crystal.
They say the Lady of the Lake gave Excalibur away for a loaf of bread!
starter/compliment: Ah, my good knight! Camelot owes you a great deal.
starter/insult: Lancelot still says it was luck, and I'm sure it wasn't... mostly.
rough/compliment: Blimey, good on ye for getting Merlin out of that crystal.
kid/compliment: If you're a real knight now, show me your sword!

compliment: Arthur's sending his knights after the Grail, and you're a knight.
insult: None of Arthur's knights found the Grail last time, so no pressure.
remark: Merlin's set up by the library now, so ask him about the Grail.
gossip: They say the Grail's passed into Gielinor and Arthur's thrilled.
Young Percival rode off months back and isn't home yet, they say.
starter/compliment: Aha! I'm glad you're here. I'm sending knights after the Grail!
starter/insult: The Grail is elusive, my knight, and it takes no end of patience.
starter/remark: Percival's still not back. We are getting a bit worried.
kid/remark: The Grail's a cup, isn't it? All this fuss over a cup?

compliment: Splendid, word is you brought the Holy Grail back to Camelot!
The Fisher King's lands grow green again thanks to you, they say.
insult: Found the Grail, I hear. The knights had only been looking for years.
plain/insult: Check your sacks, lads! This one found a knight in a goblin's sack.
gossip: Sir Percival's a king now, they say. Of somewhere nobody can find.
They found Percival in a goblin sack, three months a slave!
starter/compliment: My splendid knight! Camelot is in your debt.
starter/insult: Ah, the Grail-finder. My other knights are rather sulky about it.
vicar/compliment: The Holy Grail, found! Saradomin smile on you, friend.
kid/compliment: Can I drink out of the magic cup, please, just a sip?

compliment: A noble cause, that, getting old Dimintheis his family crest back.
insult: The Fitzharmon crest is still lost, not that you've looked for it.
remark: That nobleman by the fancy dress shop's lost his estate, I hear.
gossip: Dimintheis's sons went off with the crest and haven't been seen since.
They say one of the Fitzharmon boys cooks now, out past the mountain.
starter/compliment: Adventurer! I desperately need my family crest returned to me.
starter/insult: Gah, if you're begging, go and get a job, and if not, find my crest!
starter/remark: The King keeps my estate until I show him my crest, wretched rule.
toff/remark: Lost his crest, has Dimintheis. Careless, for a Fitzharmon.
guard/remark: Nobleman by the gate keeps asking after his sons, as if that's my job.

compliment: Clever work, putting the Fitzharmon crest back together like that.
You found all three Fitzharmon boys? Well done, that took some doing.
insult: How heroic, cooking fish for a chef to win a crest.
plain/insult: Mended a family crest, I hear. Shame you can't mend a family.
gossip: One Fitzharmon son lost his bit of the crest to a demon, they say.
Dimintheis has his crest back and is ever so pleased, they say.
starter/compliment: Adventurer! Words are insufficient for the gratitude I feel.
starter/insult: Lost the gauntlets again? They always find their way back to me.
kid/remark: You fought a demon for a bit of a badge... grown-ups are odd.

compliment: Would you help Caroline? She's not heard from her husband all week.
insult: Caroline's family's still out on that platform, and you're still here.
remark: No word from the fishing platform for days now, which is odd.
gossip: Not one of the platform fishermen has written home, families fret.
They say Holgart's boat is full of holes and he wants swamp paste.
starter/compliment: Is there any chance you could help me with my husband and son?
starter/insult: Kent always writes. Always. You don't look much of a sailor, mind.
starter/remark: Not a word from Kent or Kennith all week, and that isn't like them.
rough/remark: Platform lads have gone quiet. Sea's not right, I tell ye.

compliment: Word is you got young Kennith off that platform, brave thing.
You're the one who found Kent washed up on that island?
insult: I hear a slug nearly got the better of you... a slug.
gossip: They say the platform fishermen have had slugs get into their heads!
Kent's home resting, they say. Won't be fishing for a while.
starter/compliment: Brave adventurer! I could have lost them both but for you.
starter/insult: Kent's home under my feet all day now, so thank you for that.
rough/insult: Sea slugs, was it? I'd have sorted it with a boot, me.
kid/remark: Are the slugs slimy, the ones that made the fishermen go funny?

compliment: Do you fish? Those dwarves by the mountain want a fishing trophy.
insult: The dwarves still won't let anyone through, and can you blame them?
remark: Odd lot, those dwarves guarding a tunnel and talking about fishing.
gossip: The Hemenster contest's on again. Old Jack won it years running.
A pale stranger fishes at Hemenster. Can't abide garlic, they say.
starter/compliment: Call us friends? Then win us the Hemenster trophy and all its gold.
starter/insult: You can't go down there, because you can't, so that's that.
starter/remark: First prize is gold. We dwarves are big fans of gold.

compliment: Word is you won at Hemenster with the biggest carp in years!
insult: I hear you won the fishing contest with garlic stuffed in a pipe.
plain/insult: Beat a stranger at fishing by stinking out his spot, some champion.
gossip: The dwarves let a stranger through their tunnel, unheard of!
They say the stranger in black lost his spot by the pipes to garlic.
starter/compliment: Ah, our friend! Come on through. Stop in for a beer or two.
starter/insult: Can't believe a human out-fished us. Mind, we dwarves can't fish.
dwarf/compliment: The brothers let you through the tunnel? You must be all right, then.

remark: There's always been an odd crack in the wall of that smithy.
plain/insult: Are you rummaging in other folks' bookcases again?
gossip: There's an old book on a magic ore in a house by the bank, they say.
Old tales say wizards sealed a workshop near here out of fear.
kid/remark: Mum says there's a secret room under the smithy, but I can't find it.

compliment: Clever hands on you, getting that old workshop running again.
insult: Was that you banging under the smithy all hours, then?
remark: There are elementals stomping about under the smithy now, they say.
gossip: A shield of some strange ore, they say. Made right under our feet!
kid/compliment: Was it a real rock monster you fought down there, a big one?

remark: Someone's had all the helpful books off the earth sciences shelf.
plain/insult: Do put the books back when you've done rummaging in the library.
gossip: The scholars here found more on that odd elemental ore, they say.
There's a beaten old book in the library, written in some code.

compliment: Word is that odd ore made you a helmet for the mind, of all things!
You cracked the code in that old book? The scholars are impressed.
plain/insult: I hear that helmet sharpens the mind, so did it work on yours?
gossip: There's a whole lower level under that old workshop, they say.

compliment: Lord Sinclair's been murdered! The guards could use a sharp mind.
insult: Still no culprit for poor Lord Sinclair, if you fancy a look.
plain/insult: I'd wager you're as baffled by the Sinclair murder as the guards are.
remark: Study door locked from inside and an odd smell about, so they say.
gossip: Terrible business, old Lord Sinclair stabbed in his own study.
Sinclair gave his castle to those knights. His children were furious.
starter/compliment: Oh, it's terrible! Lord Sinclair's been murdered and we need help.
starter/insult: This is private property! Unless you'd like questioning yourself?
starter/remark: The Sarge says every murder leaves clues, but we're out of our depth.

compliment: Word is you solved the Sinclair murder, fingerprints and all!
insult: Dusting cups with flour, I hear. Is that detective work now?
plain/insult: Apparently you're not as stupid as you look, or so they say.
gossip: One of the Sinclairs is under house arrest, awaiting trial.
Honest of the guards, admitting they'd never have solved it alone.
starter/compliment: Excellent work on that murder! All the guards are impressed.
starter/insult: No, your work here is done. Really and truly done, so you can go.

compliment: Sir Ceril's had cultists in his house. He'd pay for help, I hear.
insult: Sir Ceril's armour's still missing, not that it'd fit you anyway.
remark: Cultists in a cave south of the city by the clock tower, they say.
gossip: Cultists broke in at the Carnilleans' five times and took one thing!
The Carnilleans' butler followed the cult once and died that night.
starter/compliment: You there, get my stolen armour back and I'll pay you... modestly.
starter/insult: That's Sir Ceril to you, impudent scamp! Now fetch my stolen armour.
starter/remark: Blooming, thieving cultists! String them all up, I say!
toff/remark: The Carnilleans and their cultists. Some families invite trouble.

compliment: Brave, that, going down among those cultists and coming back up.
insult: Fragrant work, turning valves in the sewers all day like that.
remark: Something went on at the Carnillean house and nobody's saying what.
gossip: The Carnilleans' cult trouble's gone quiet, and quiet isn't over.
starter/compliment: Hello again, adventurer! Do mind the cultists out there.
starter/insult: It's still Sir Ceril to you, but I suppose I can wish you good day.
starter/remark: Cultists in the sewers, cultists at the door, is there no end to them?

compliment: Brother Kojo's clock has stopped. He'd pay someone to fix it.
insult: Still no clock, so I've been late for everything, thanks ever so.
remark: Does anyone know the time? That clock tower's no use at all.
gossip: Kojo says the cogs are down in the cellar with strange beasts.
starter/compliment: Hello, adventurer! Do you happen to know the time, because I don't.
starter/insult: The cogs are too heavy for me. You look... well, you'll manage.
starter/remark: Oh dear. One cog on each floor, but which of them goes where?
kid/remark: The big clock's broken. So I can stay up as long as I like!

compliment: Word is you fixed the clock tower. We all know the time again!
insult: You fixed the clock, I hear. Now I've no excuse for being late.
plain/insult: Carried some cogs up a tower. The bards will be thrilled.
gossip: Somebody poisoned the rats under the clock tower, and good riddance.
starter/compliment: Well done, well done! You are clever, and it keeps perfect time now.
starter/insult: Ah, my cog-carrier! The clock's fine, before you ask.
kid/remark: The clock works again. Now I have to go to bed on time.

compliment: Councillor Halgrive needs someone brave for those plague sheep.
insult: Nobody wants to touch those sick sheep, yourself included.
remark: Some sheep of a funny colour got loose north of the city, they say.
gossip: The mourners say those loose sheep have the plague, and they'd know.
starter/compliment: Adventurer! Four diseased sheep must be dealt with, and soon.
starter/insult: I do not blame you. It is not pleasant work, but time is short.
starter/remark: Every second they're loose, the risk of contagion grows!
rough/remark: Plague in sheep? Never heard the like, though I'm no mourner.

compliment: Word is you rounded up those plague sheep, brave in that suit.
insult: Very heroic, chasing sheep about with a cattle prod like that.
plain/insult: Herded sheep in a plague suit. You'd fit in with the mourners.
gossip: They say those sick sheep went in the incinerator, every last one.
starter/compliment: Ah, adventurer! Public health thanks you, and so do I.
starter/insult: You've washed since, I trust? One can't be too careful.
kid/remark: Can I have a go at chasing the coloured sheep with the stick?

compliment: The Watchtower wizards need help, with ogres about, they say.
insult: The Watchtower's broken and ogres are coming, but don't rush.
remark: More ogres in the Feldip Hills lately. The wizards are fretting.
gossip: Did you hear the tower's power crystals have been stolen?
starter/compliment: Help? Oh, wonderful, dear traveller! Search the bushes for clues!
starter/insult: Typical, nowadays. It's left to us wizards to do all the work.
starter/remark: Darn and drat! Oh dear, whatever has become of the crystals?
guard/remark: Ogres at the walls and a broken tower make for a lovely shift.

compliment: Yanille's safe at last! Word is you got the Watchtower working.
They say you walked right into Gu'Tanoth, among the ogres!
insult: Fixed the Watchtower, I hear. The ogres send their regards.
plain/insult: Made friends with ogres, which would explain the smell, I hear.
gossip: The ogres' little grey servants pinched the crystals, they say.
starter/compliment: Greetings, friend! Yanille is safe at last, thanks to you.
starter/insult: Ho ho, a comedian to the finish! So why are you still here?
guard/remark: The tower's shield is up. Fewer ogres, more paperwork.

compliment: Bert the sandman found something nasty in his pit, so go and ask him.
insult: Bert's still in a state over his sand pit, and you walked right past.
remark: Bert never used to haul sand all hours like he does lately.
gossip: They say they found a hand in the sand pit, just the hand!
The guard captain's in the Dragon Inn again, or does he ever leave it?
starter/compliment: Will you lend us a hand? Ah, sorry, that were a poor choice o' words.
starter/insult: Tha guard captain's no help. Doubt you'll be much better.
starter/remark: Wha' shall I do? I'll most certainly lose the job...
guard/remark: A hand in the sand pit. The captain says it's not his department.

compliment: Word is you caught Sandy out. Truth serum in his coffee, no less!
insult: I hear you went round collecting body parts, which is hands-on work.
plain/insult: How charming, carrying a wizard's head about in your bag.
gossip: They say the wizards fixed it so the sand pit fills itself now.
Sandy's wanted by the guards. Bribed a wizard, then did him in.
starter/compliment: Ey up! The pit fills itself now, so there's no more work for Bert.
starter/insult: I'd shake yer hand, but I've gone right off hands, see.
barkeep/remark: The guard captain's still on about some hand, and he drank through it.

compliment: Brother Omad's not slept in a week. A child's blanket was stolen.
insult: Thieves took a baby's blanket. And still nobody's fetched it.
remark: Odd, that ring of stones in the forest west of here, isn't it?
gossip: Brother Cedric went off for wine days ago and isn't back, they say.
starter/compliment: Oh, hello... sorry, so tired. Could you find the child's blanket?
starter/insult: We are peaceful men and you look less so. Just right for the blanket.
starter/remark: Waaaah! Waaaah! All night long, and how is a man meant to sleep?
vicar/remark: Brother Omad's yawning through prayers again, the poor soul.

compliment: Word is you got the monks their party, and their wine!
insult: Busy day for you, finding a baby's blanket and a drunk monk.
gossip: Brother Cedric's back with the wine and mostly sober, they say.
The monastery threw a birthday party, monks, partying!
starter/compliment: Ah, my friend! I'm much better now I sleep, so how about a party?
starter/insult: Do keep it down, adventurer. The little one's finally asleep.
vicar/compliment: Saradomin smile on you for helping the brothers at the monastery.

compliment: Goblins wrecked the Observatory, and the professor needs help.
insult: The professor's telescope's still broken. The stars can wait, then.
remark: Goblins moved in by the Observatory. Nothing but trouble since.
gossip: The assistant says that telescope hasn't worked in ages.
starter/compliment: Welcome to the Observatory, where wonder is all around you!
starter/insult: Ignore my assistant, or don't. You'll help me either way, won't you?
starter/remark: Those pesky goblins have been tampering with my telescope, the pests!

compliment: Splendid! I hear you got the Observatory telescope working!
insult: You looked at the stars, I hear. I do that for free most nights.
gossip: The assistant says you made the lens yourself, which was wise.
The Observatory goblins made stew in the lens mould, they say.
starter/compliment: My friend! The heavens are ours again, thanks to you!
starter/insult: You again? Don't touch anything, on my assistant's orders.
kid/remark: If you saw a star, can you get me one, a little one?

compliment: Are you sneaky? Kangai Mau wants someone sneaky for a job in Ardougne.
insult: Kangai Mau wants a skilled thief, so you can keep walking.
remark: Some Ardougne lord took a totem from the Rantuki tribe, they say.
gossip: Lord Handelmort collects things. Other people's things, mostly.
starter/compliment: Hello. I Kangai Mau of Rantuki tribe. You look brave and sneaky.
starter/insult: I told I find thieves in Brimhaven, but not you, maybe.
starter/remark: Handelmort think he have right to take our totem, and he wrong.
barkeep/remark: That tribesman's had a table all week, waiting on a thief.

compliment: Word is you got the Rantuki totem back from that Ardougne lord.
insult: Burgled a lord's private museum and all for swordfish, I hear.
gossip: They say someone got into Handelmort's house by teleport.
starter/compliment: You! Totem home now and Rantuki tribe grateful, so have swordfish.
starter/insult: You again. I hope you not steal from me now.
pirate/compliment: Arr, I like that ye burgled a lord for a tribesman.

compliment: Would you help Lady Servil? Khazard's men took her whole family.
insult: Lady Servil's still waiting by her broken cart... still.
remark: Khazard's mercenaries run this whole area and nobody stops them.
gossip: Khazard's men make folk fight in that arena for sport!
They say the authorities take Khazard's coin and look away.
starter/compliment: Adventurer, please... bring my family back from that arena.
starter/insult: The cart? That's the least of my problems, unless you can fight?
starter/remark: Justin... Sammy... I've got to find my family.

compliment: Bravo! Word is you freed the Servils from Khazard's arena.
Blimey! You're the one who killed Khazard's hellhound?
plain/insult: Fought in Khazard's arena, I hear. Did you take a bow after?
gossip: They say Khazard's still raging over that dog of his, Bouncer.
Good news from the Servils. They say the family's home and recovering.
starter/compliment: My husband and son are safe at home, thanks to you!
starter/insult: Do mind Khazard's men. They hold grudges, you know.
kid/remark: Was the hellhound big, and did it have spikes on?

compliment: Otto by the falls teaches the old barbarian ways, and you'd suit it.
insult: Otto says you've barbarian blood. He's very generous, Otto.
remark: Otto fishes without a harpoon, sharks and all, they say.
gossip: They say Otto talks with the spirits of dead barbarians.
starter/compliment: Good day! You seem a hearty warrior. Barbarian blood, perhaps?
starter/insult: Your scepticism will be your loss, civilised one.
starter/remark: May the spirits be with you. And with your arm, near sharks.

compliment: Word is Otto's taught you the old ways. Fire without a tinderbox!
insult: Catching fish with your bare arm now? Hard on the sleeves, that.
plain/insult: Planting saplings with your fist now? You're a gardener's nightmare.
gossip: They say there's a cavern under Otto's lake, full of dragons.
starter/compliment: Good day, hearty warrior! The ancestors are proud of you.
starter/insult: You still hold back too much. Spoken as a friend, mind.
kid/compliment: Teach me to catch a fish with just my hands, like you did!

compliment: Only the elite get into the Legends' Guild, and you just might.
insult: They don't call it the Legends' Guild for nothing, you know.
remark: The guild wants the Kharazi Jungle mapped, and nobody's managed yet.
gossip: Nobody's mapped the south of Karamja, or so they say, too thick.
starter/compliment: Good day, adventurer! No doubt you're keen to join the guild?
starter/insult: You'll need to be a legendary citizen, so best of luck with that.
starter/remark: Grand Vizier Erkle is a very busy man, so do be brief.

compliment: Word is you mapped the Kharazi Jungle, a true legend, then!
That totem in the main hall? They say you brought it back.
insult: I hear you mapped a jungle, so did you get lost, even a bit?
plain/insult: A member of the Legends' Guild. They're letting anyone in now.
gossip: A demon had a Kharazi shaman, but not any more it hasn't, they say.
The Kharazi tribe call the guild friends now, they say.
starter/compliment: Welcome, legend. Your totem has pride of place in the hall.
starter/insult: Ah, our newest legend. Do wipe the jungle off your boots.

compliment: A stranger at the Flying Horse wants a hero and says he pays well.
insult: The limping stranger's still looking for a hero... still looking.
remark: That fellow with the limp in the Flying Horse gives me the chills.
gossip: He's after something in the old Temple of Ikov, they say.
starter/compliment: I seek a hero for an important mission, might you be one?
starter/insult: Call yourself a hero? My daughter is more of a hero than you!
starter/remark: My patience grows thin. The Staff of Armadyl, hero!
barkeep/remark: That limping one wants a hero. I just want him to order something.

compliment: Word is you went into the Temple of Ikov and came back out.
Ice arrows, for the fire warrior in Ikov? Now that's clever thinking.
insult: Did you scare off that limping stranger? He hasn't been back since.
gossip: Some say that limping stranger was Lucien! A Mahjarrat, in our town!
kid/remark: Were the spiders in the temple ice ones, and did they bite?

compliment: Ask the Guildmaster, the Hunter Guild could use a sharp-eyed tracker.
plain/insult: The guild wants trackers. You'd lose your own footprints.
remark: Hunters come and go from this guild... some just go, mind.
gossip: Fox left the guild without a word to anyone, and Verity's fretting.
Wolf sent Fox off on some errand, and nobody's seen him since.
kid/remark: They call the guild cat a hunter and he just sleeps all day!
starter/compliment: A little birdy tells me Verity could use a hand, hunter.
starter/insult: Can't find the Burrow? Then maybe you're not cut out for this guild.
starter/remark: Politics and paperwork. I was a hunter once, you know.

compliment: You found Fox out on the savannah and patched him up, I hear.
They say the guild gives you the hard rumours now, and that's trust.
insult: Mended a cat's bed for the Hunter Guild? The bards have been told.
plain/insult: Tracked down Fox while he was lying flat on the ground, didn't you?
gossip: Something knocked Fox out cold on the savannah, and he never saw what.
Kiko's got a proper fur bed again. The whole guild can relax.
kid/compliment: You found Fox and he's just a man! I thought he'd be a real fox.
starter/compliment: Nilsal, hunter. Fox is back on his feet, thanks to you.
starter/insult: Don't let it go to your head, hunter. Kiko did most of the work.

compliment: Marcellus needs someone calm to talk to the frogs, and you'd do.
plain/insult: Frogs on strike, and you're the best the oasis could find?
remark: Don't mention frogs near Marcellus. He's had a trying time of it.
gossip: Have you heard? The frogs at the oasis have gone on strike.
Marcellus keeps saying the frogs want to enslave us all.
kid/remark: If the frogs can go on strike, can I go on strike too?
starter/compliment: You're no frog, are you? Good. I need someone I can trust.
starter/insult: You! I bet you're in with them, with the frogs!
starter/remark: The frogs are out to get us, every last one of us!

compliment: You made peace between Marcellus and the frogs, of all things?
The oasis frogs are back eating the flies, thanks to you, I hear.
insult: Settling a dispute between a farmer and some frogs is grand work.
plain/insult: Brokered peace with frogs. They'll be carving your statue, no doubt.
gossip: They say the frogs held an election, hopping about on lily pads.
Marcellus pays the frogs in oranges now, strange times we live in.
There's a frog calling himself Lord of Dread and nobody's worried.
kid/insult: You fought a frog? Was it a big frog? It was a small one, wasn't it.
starter/compliment: Hello again, friend. My patch is yours, and the flies won't win.
starter/insult: Back again? Keep your voice down, because the flies are listening.

compliment: The villa's after smart staff for the party, and you'd scrub up well.
plain/insult: A fancy party at the villa. They'd make you use the back door.
remark: That actor by the villa gate is still waiting for his big break.
gossip: A party at Villa Lucens tonight, they say. Aldarin's finest, invited.
There's a new play opening at the villa's theatre, up on the cliffs.
starter/compliment: Good day! Could I trouble you for the briefest of moments?
starter/insult: On second thoughts, you may not be cut out for this job.
starter/remark: One day they'll call me Patzi the Grand, you'll see.

compliment: Well done! You're the one who solved the death at Villa Lucens?
Sharp work, clearing your own name of murder like that.
insult: You accused the bag carrier first? Well she was a thief, at least.
plain/insult: Stole the show at the villa with a prop sword, didn't you?
gossip: The show went on at Villa Lucens, death or no, the host insisted.
One of the cast tripped him, they say. Too much wine, and a long fall.
Somebody was after the Principum Red in the villa cellar, I hear.
toff/compliment: A butler who solves murders. Constantinius should hire more.
starter/compliment: Ah, my butler! I'll be a star yet, you mark my words.
starter/insult: You upstaged me! I hired you to make me look better!

compliment: Emelio's after an easterner for some venture, and that's you, friend.
plain/insult: Emelio needs an easterner's help. He'll take you, apparently.
remark: Emelio was Varlaless once, you know. Couldn't abide outsiders.
gossip: Emelio's got a new business idea, something from the east...
The Colosseum's still cleaning up after Emelio's last idea, I hear.
starter/compliment: Kuani! You're one of them easterners, and I could use one of those.
starter/insult: You don't know the kabit? But how could you not know?
starter/remark: Meat, spices and salad, all wrapped up in bread, pure genius!

compliment: Kebabs in Varlamore! You had a hand in that, they say.
Ate a kebab and fought a minotaur in the Colosseum, what a showman!
insult: Glamorous work, fighting a minotaur for an advert.
plain/insult: A minotaur fight to sell kebabs. I hope they paid you well.
gossip: Emelio's opened a kebab shop. Buffalo, with Kharidian spice.
The minotaur thought you'd eaten minotaur meat, but it was buffalo.
kid/compliment: You're the kebab one! Can I have a kebab, please, please?
starter/compliment: Nilsal, friend! A special price for you, as always.
starter/insult: Sorry, friend. The next customers come first, even before you.

compliment: The curator could use a sharp pair of eyes at the museum.
plain/insult: The curator wanted a detective and he's got you instead.
remark: An empty case at the museum. Folk queue up to look at nothing.
gossip: Xerna's Diadem was stolen right off display at the Grand Museum!
I hear the guards are looking into the museum theft, slowly.
guard/remark: The museum theft is under investigation, so move along.
starter/compliment: Perhaps you'd have better luck finding it than the guards.
starter/insult: I'm no detective. Forgive me, but I'm not sure you are either.
starter/remark: Xerna's Diadem, gone. And nothing else even out of place.

compliment: Xerna's Diadem is back at the museum and you found it, I hear.
Well done, following that diadem's trail right across the sea.
insult: Found the diadem but won't say where? How very mysterious of you.
plain/insult: Found the diadem and won't say where? That smells fishy to me, friend.
gossip: The diadem's back on display. Where it went, nobody's saying.
A grey-haired man with a monocle was asking about boats, they say.
guard/remark: The diadem's back and the case is closed, so don't ask me how.
starter/compliment: Thank you again, iknami. The diadem has never looked finer.
starter/insult: One day you'll tell me where that piece came from, and I can wait.

compliment: Folk keep vanishing round here. We could use someone brave.
plain/insult: Folk vanishing, and you're after a pint? Read the board first, friend.
remark: Some say the missing got lost in the mountains and others say Fortis.
Francis swears the ents walked a different path that night.
gossip: More missing folk on the board at the pub, it never ends.
Old Ictus says the night people took them, but nobody listens to him.
starter/compliment: Please. If you truly care, help us find our sons.
starter/insult: Turn around. Walk out. Nobody's looking into anything.
starter/remark: One moment they were playing upstairs, and the next... gone.

compliment: You brought Shas and Etz home? Their parents can sleep again.
Brave, going into that den and bringing Antos out alive.
insult: Ictus says he told you so. Mind, he tells everyone so.
plain/insult: Turns out the madman by the sea was right, and you took your time.
gossip: Ictus was right all along. Something did come in the night.
Not everyone came back from that cave. Only the boys and Antos did.
I hear the captain's guards have new willow bows at last.
kid/remark: Shas says there were real monsters in the cave, real ones!
starter/compliment: Our boys are home because of you, and we'll never forget it.
starter/insult: You again? Oh, it's you. Come in then, and mind the new wall.

compliment: Kind of you to visit, since that tourist at the temple wants a guest.
plain/insult: You'd get on with that man and his egg up at the temple.
remark: Somebody ought to tell that tourist the temple isn't a house.
gossip: There's a tourist living in Tal Teok temple, with an egg.
That tourist talks to his egg. Calls it his best friend.
kid/remark: There's an egg sat on the temple wall and the man talks to it!
starter/compliment: You found me! Do stay for a feast, Humpy Plumpy insists.
starter/insult: Could I really trust you with Humpy Plumpy, delicate as he is?
starter/remark: I've come to quite like it here. Best friend I ever had, this egg.

compliment: That takes patience, putting an egg back together piece by piece.
insult: I hear you lost one egg and broke three more with those steady hands.
plain/insult: Smashing a chicken egg, a dragon egg and a jaguar egg is thorough.
remark: Gravity's been very busy up at the temple, they say.
gossip: Poor Alan the tourist had a great fall up at Tal Teok, so they say.
King lent all her men out to mend an egg, and I'm not making that up.
barkeep/remark: King's men sent up the hill for an egg, strangest order going.
kid/compliment: Can you fix my egg as well? I dropped it on the step.

compliment: You've a kind face. That scholar could use help with the ents.
plain/insult: The funny man's after help with the ents, so you'll fit right in.
remark: Ents, totems, spirits. All one cycle out here, the old folk say.
gossip: That scholar keeps staring at the ents, lost in thought as always.
Some out-of-towner's been asking what the totems are for.
kid/remark: I've been watching the funny man get confused by the ents!
starter/compliment: Oh! You gave me quite the start. Do you know anything of ents?
starter/insult: The locals told me nothing useful. I doubt you'll do better.
starter/remark: Why would these totems matter so much to the ents?

compliment: The ents will remember you rebuilding their totem.
An offering from the ents is an honour, and you had one, I hear.
insult: Stood and watched the scholar break a totem, then fixed it for him?
plain/insult: Carving animals on a pole to cheer up trees, proud day for you, that.
gossip: A little girl showed that scholar how to carve a totem, they say.
The ents are happy again. The totem's back up, carvings and all.
kid/compliment: You fixed the totem! The ents aren't sad any more!
starter/compliment: Ah, my fellow ent watcher! The totems are doing splendidly.
starter/insult: You again? I've written you into my notes, as a footnote.

compliment: Fancy the sea? Those salvagers on the dock are after a captain.
plain/insult: Those two want a captain and they'll take anyone, even you.
remark: Salvage work, they call it. Fishing up old wrecks for coin.
gossip: Two salvagers hiring on the dock, and far too keen for my liking.
Will and Anne are starting a salvage business, looking for hands.
starter/compliment: Ah, look what we have here! Someone who needs a good job!
starter/insult: This one's clearly never worked an honest day in their life!
starter/remark: You waive all rights in the event of horrific death, splendid!

compliment: Fair play, washed up on the Pandemonium and came back a sailor.
insult: Got your first job and went straight overboard, I hear.
plain/insult: Thrown overboard on your first day. Most of us last a bit longer.
remark: Boats everywhere these days. Everyone's a sailor now, it seems.
gossip: Those salvagers sailed off with some old medallion, not seen since.
Word is those salvagers shoved their new hand overboard, the charmers.
pirate/compliment: Arr, ye've found yer sea legs. The Pandemonium's a fine start.
rough/insult: Did ye float all the way to the Pandemonium like driftwood?
kid/compliment: Is your raft a real boat, and can I steer it?

compliment: Steve's after a sailor for some looty, and you look the part.
pirate/insult: Steve wants a rough and tough piratical type, so keep lookin', Steve.
remark: Steve's got a crate behind the bar nobody can get open.
gossip: Steve's on about pirate looty again. In a crate at Port Sarim.
Steve says the looty's disguised as ordinary cargo, which is cunning.
starter/compliment: Hoist your mast, sailor! There's pirate looty begging to be found!
starter/insult: I'm after a rough, tough, piratical type, and it isn't you!
starter/remark: Precious plundered pirate looty, and nothing normal about it, oh no!

compliment: I hear it took a proper sailor to get Steve's crate open.
insult: All that sailing for a crate of crowbars, worth it, was it?
plain/insult: Think on this. You needed a crowbar to open a crate of crowbars.
gossip: Steve's precious looty was a crate of crowbars, locked shut.
Someone drank a bottle of old stout and a troll jumped out, they say.
A dwarf near Sarim helped make the key and got paid in pie, they say.
starter/compliment: Yarr! My first mate returns! Still using that raft, are you?
starter/insult: Blistering barnacles! Did I forget to mention the troll?

compliment: Brave of you to offer Arhein a hand with the council.
plain/insult: I'd sell tickets to see you against Councillor Catherine.
remark: Catherby runs on forms, and here's another from the council office.
gossip: Arhein's got a bird he swears can read the sea currents.
The councillor's banned non-human workers, Arhein's bird included.
starter/compliment: Hello again! Fancy helping me test a little theory?
starter/insult: You can try Catherine yourself. It'll be an uphill struggle.
starter/remark: A bird that tracks currents. If only the council would let me.

compliment: A hero, beating Councillor Catherine at her own forms!
Good work, charting the currents for Arhein like that.
insult: I hear you filled in the council's form twice with the same answers.
plain/insult: Fished a mayor out of a tank. Democracy, Catherby style.
gossip: Catherby's new mayor is the same as the old ones, down to the scales.
Councillor Catherine still hasn't noticed the mayor's a fish.
kid/remark: The mayor's a fish! Everyone knows except the councillor!
starter/compliment: Hello again! Thanks to you, those currents are charted.
starter/insult: Hello again! Are you keeping the mayor nice and wet for me?

compliment: There's a hurt tortugan on that island, if you're the kind sort.
remark: Keep your head down, with gryphons seen out over the islands.
gossip: They say there's a hurt tortugan out there that won't let anyone near.
starter/compliment: Bandages... I was trying to make bandages. Seaweed and a leaf...
starter/insult: No... no help. I'll fix it myself...
starter/remark: I'm fine... I'm fine. Please... leave me alone...

compliment: You brought Floopa home. Elder Korel says she'd not have survived.
You saved the Little Pearl from the gryphon, so the eggs are safe.
insult: Elder Korel let you stay as a tourist. Don't let it go to your head.
plain/insult: Whatever next, a land walker mending tortugan roofs?
gossip: A ship with red sails was seen leaving the Little Pearl, they say.
Floopa's wound will never fully heal, Elder Korel says.
Elder Korel can't fathom how a gryphon got out to the Little Pearl.
starter/compliment: Thank you for saving my life. I mean it. I'm just bad at saying so.
starter/insult: I'd have managed. Probably. I read a book once, you know.

compliment: Elder Raley trusts you. Few tourists can say that.
plain/insult: The elders think well of you, but I'll wait and see.
remark: That ship with the red sails. Nobody here has forgotten it.
gossip: Elder Raley's looking for Floopa. She should be resting, he says.
Floopa's been seen heading off alone, flipper or no flipper.
starter/compliment: Welcome back. You haven't seen Floopa, have you?
starter/insult: You found Floopa once. Surely you can manage it twice?
starter/remark: She can't have gone far, not with that flipper of hers.

compliment: Brave, that, looking into the red-sailed traders for Floopa.
A rare honour, the elders giving you the camphor in the Sacred Grove.
insult: So you worked for the Red Reef company... for a while.
plain/insult: Fought pirates for the very traders who hurt Floopa, did you?
gossip: Spencer Brentwood wants the red coral by the Little Pearl, they say.
Floopa says Spencer stabbed her with her own spear, then said sorry.
The elders are making plans against the Red Reef company.
starter/compliment: You've been a good friend to us, and it means everything.
starter/insult: A plan of our own! Do try to stay out of trouble meanwhile.

compliment: The mayor's asking for help finding Keenan, and brave of you to stay.
plain/insult: Another outsider, and we don't need help, not from your sort.
remark: Outsiders aren't welcome on Wyrmscraig, and most of us mean it.
gossip: Keenan's gone missing. Muriel's in no state for visitors.
The lad was always sat staring at the sunstone in the mine.
starter/compliment: If you're feelin' brave, would you help us look for Keenan?
starter/insult: Not often we get one like you 'round these parts.
starter/remark: My job is to keep things calm, which isn't easy these days.

compliment: You went into Ardeaglais and came back. None of us would have dared.
You found out what became of Keenan, and hard news is still news.
insult: You're still an outsider, mind, just a useful one.
plain/insult: Saved the island from its own angel, but don't go expecting a statue.
gossip: Keenan's gone, and poor Muriel at least knows now.
The Mad Angel's left for good, they say. Left a golem to guard us.
Cormac thought the Angel was just a tale. He knows better these days.
starter/compliment: All the best, friend. Good to see you stickin' around.
starter/insult: Still here? Folk might start thinkin' you live on Wyrmscraig.

compliment: Gillie Groats could use help with that bull, and you look sturdy.
plain/insult: Cassius wants a partner for his milk scheme, and he's not fussy.
remark: Gillie says a bull's been upsetting her cows something rotten.
gossip: There's a bad-tempered bull in the Groats' cow pen, but whose?
Some fellow by the pond wants to build an empire... of milk.
kid/remark: The man by the pond keeps asking people if they like milk!
starter/compliment: You! Yes, you! Do you like making money? And... milk?
starter/insult: Fair enough. If your passion for milk changes, you know where I am.
starter/remark: An empire. Of milk. It's a perfect plan!

compliment: You sorted out that bull for the Groats. Their cows are happy again.
insult: Took on a bull over a jug of milk? Lumbridge's finest hour, that was.
plain/insult: Was it brave or daft, grabbing a bull by the horns over bad milk?
gossip: That bull in the Groats' field was Cassius's, the rogue, they say.
I hear Cassius was stealing milk from the Groats, and sour stuff too.
kid/compliment: You beat the big bull! It was bigger than a cow, wasn't it!
starter/insult: You should leave. I can't even look at you.
starter/remark: Ruined it! The unique flavour was what I was trying to sell!

compliment: You'd do, Talia's shelter needs someone worldly to find strays.
plain/insult: Talia wants someone worldly to fetch strays, so you'll have to do.
remark: Strays all over and an empty shelter, somebody ought to help, eh?
gossip: There's a dog shelter by the monastery with not many dogs in it yet.
The monks gave Talia and Chase that land. They believe in the cause.
vicar/compliment: Talia's shelter needs a kind soul, and might that be you, traveller?
starter/compliment: Welcome to our dog shelter! We need someone worldly, like you.
starter/insult: It takes hours to coax a puppy out of hiding, and you'd take days.
starter/remark: Kennels to clean, dogs to feed and fences to mend, but not one stray.

compliment: Bless you for bringing those puppies home to the shelter.
The shelter's open for business now, thanks to you, they say.
insult: Rescued puppies from goblins and outlaws? Fierce things, puppies are.
gossip: The goblins wanted puppies for guard dogs. Got a stuffed one instead.
Outlaws had one of the puppies, but not any more, they say.
vicar/compliment: The shelter thrives. Saradomin smile on you, friend.
kid/compliment: Can I have one of the puppies you found if I call it Biscuit?
starter/compliment: Welcome back! The kennels are full, and it's thanks to you.
starter/insult: Oh, you're here. The kennels need cleaning, since you ask.

gossip: The Professor's new assistant up at the manor has a sharp tongue.
The young scientist at the manor can't sleep and says the bed's vile.
remark: Someone's living behind a bookcase in that manor now, honestly.
plain/insult: Ava wants undead chickens fetched. You look the gullible sort.
starter/compliment: You there! I need a couple of undead chickens, for science.
starter/insult: You'd fetch anything for a reward, so fetch me some undead chickens.
starter/remark: This bed is vile. And the Professor upstairs is no help at all.

compliment: Clever of you to help that scientist build her contraption.
Ava's made you a gadget that fetches your arrows back, I hear.
insult: Brave work, fetching chickens, a magnet and some buttons for a lady.
plain/insult: Chopped a haunted tree for Ava, I hear. The tree's still sulking.
gossip: Ava's got an undead chicken in her bed now, for science, apparently.
starter/compliment: Ah, my gullible helper. Of course the device works, since I built it.
starter/insult: Lost your arrows again? I did build you something for that.
kid/remark: Is it true the lady at the manor sleeps on a dead chicken?

gossip: The students at the dig keep losing things, a teddy of all things.
You can't dig up there without passing the Earth Sciences exams.
remark: They say the Varrock museum pays for the whole dig, lucky them.
starter/compliment: Hello, dear! Fancy sitting the Earth Sciences exam, serious as it is?
starter/insult: An exam? You? Well, get the Curator to stamp your letter first.
starter/remark: Gloves and boots at all times! Why does nobody ever listen?

compliment: Passed all three exams, they say, then found an altar under it all.
Word is you found a Zarosian altar down the shafts, fancy that.
gossip: Saradominists buried an old altar under the dig, they reckon.
insult: You blew up a wall down the dig, I hear. For archaeology, apparently.
plain/insult: Carried nitroglycerin round the dig in your pack, I hear!
starter/compliment: Ah, my star pupil! Still handling bones very carefully, I hope?
starter/insult: Oh, it's you, dear. Every single answer wrong the first time round.

gossip: Some folk went to a house party on an island past the swamp.
There's a boat by the fishing spots. Nobody'll say who left it.
remark: Someone was screaming down by the swamp, and I didn't go and look.
starter/compliment: Help! Help! We were attacked on the island and I beg you, please!
starter/insult: You? Fine. Anyone! Just stop that killer before it's too late.
starter/remark: That psycho is still out there. They can't get away with this.

gossip: That party on the island ended in murder, and more than one, they say.
I hear the killer was one of the guests all along, which is shocking.
compliment: Good for you, catching that island killer.
plain/insult: Caught the killer, I hear. After how many of the guests, exactly?
remark: Mandy lived through it, they say. Her heart's on the wrong side!
kid/remark: If the murderer was in a wardrobe, has anyone looked in mine?

gossip: A fellow in the Jolly Boar swore he saw zombies marching in ranks.
remark: Zombies marching in ranks? Tell me they don't do that.
insult: Zombies forming ranks up north, and here's you sightseeing.
barkeep/remark: Some chap was raving about zombies in here, so I cut him off.
starter/compliment: Ah, an adventurer. I could use some help following a trail.
starter/insult: Kind of you to offer. I'd hoped for someone better read, but still.
starter/remark: Zombies forming ranks... someone must be organising them.

compliment: Varrock thanks you for holding the palace when the dead came.
Word is you found the one man who could wake Arrav's shield.
gossip: Zombies at the palace! And Arrav himself leading them, poor soul.
Dimintheis raised the shield and the zombies fell, they say.
insult: Saved the palace, I hear. Shame about the state of the furniture.
plain/insult: The necromancer got away, I hear. Took Arrav with him, too.
toff/compliment: They say Fitzharmon blood saved the city, as one always knew.
guard/remark: Zombies at the palace. Nobody tell me they'll be back.
kid/compliment: Did you see the zombies? Mum made me hide under the bed!

gossip: Arrav's still in that necromancer's grip, the poor soul, they say.
That explorer from the Jolly Boar's gone south to the desert, I hear.
remark: Zemouregal's still out there somewhere, him and his zombies.

gossip: They say someone stole Arrav's heart back from the necromancer!
compliment: Ye gods! You took Arrav's heart from Zemouregal's own vault?
You faced Arrav himself and walked away, brave soul, I hear.
insult: Robbed a necromancer's vault, I hear. Do mind he doesn't visit.
plain/insult: I hear you got Arrav's heart back, so is the rest of him home yet?
toff/remark: Arrav the hero of Avarrocka kept like a puppet, how disgraceful.
guard/remark: Robbing Mahjarrat now, is it? Don't bring him back here.
kid/remark: Was the heart still beating when it was in your bag?

gossip: Outlaws ransacked a trader's cart on this road and took his papers.
remark: That trader by the crossroads is actually called Rat, the poor man.
insult: Rat's still waiting on his papers. Outlaws don't post things back.
starter/compliment: Hello there! I'm Rat. No, Rat's my name, and could you help me?
starter/insult: Look, do you want to help me or not? Those outlaws took my papers!
starter/remark: Five pages. Those outlaws have no idea what they took.

compliment: Rat says you're a credit to... er, trading. Trading was the word, yes.
gossip: Funny how nothing at all happened in the palace library, isn't it?
Odd, that scholar Surok never leaving the palace library now.
plain/insult: Fought the King, so I hear. Don't worry, nobody believes it.
guard/remark: Move along, because nothing happened at the palace, nothing at all.
starter/compliment: Ah! You did us a fine service. Er, did me a service, a humble trader.
starter/insult: A bit more muscle and some training, private, and then we'll see.
starter/remark: Things seem pretty quiet. Which is just how we like it.

gossip: The Zamorakians in that chaos temple craft their own runes, I hear.
remark: Shifty sort, that mage selling runes out of the chaos temple.
starter/compliment: You know of the essence mine? Then perhaps we can do business.
starter/insult: A mercenary with no allegiance isn't my type, but you'll do.
starter/remark: Those Saradominist fools in the Order, inept, the lot of them.

gossip: The Zamorak lot found a way into the wizards' essence mine, I hear.
insult: Helped the wizards and then their rivals, very even-handed of you.
compliment: They say you can cross the Abyss now. Rather you than me, friend.
vicar/insult: Helped the Zamorakians, did you? I shall pray for you, friend.
guard/remark: Zamorakians by the rune shop again, and I've got my eye on them.
starter/compliment: Ah. Our mercenary. The institute remembers its friends.
starter/insult: Still running errands for the Order of Wizards, I suppose?

gossip: Part of the castle cellar wall fell in. The Duke says earthquake.
Someone swears they saw a goblin with huge eyes in the cellar.
remark: Have you heard, a goblin with a light on its head, in Lumbridge?
barkeep/remark: Rock dust all over my ingredients, earthquake, my foot.
starter/compliment: I'm sure monsters damaged the cellar. Would you ask around for me?
starter/insult: The Duke says earthquake. You look like you'd believe him.
starter/remark: An earthquake, says the Duke, when it was plainly monsters!

compliment: Well done! You made peace with the goblins under the castle?
They say Lumbridge's treaty with the cave goblins is your doing.
gossip: They say Sigmund was a HAM man all along, and who'd have thought it?
insult: Very dignified, doing a goblin bow to make friends.
plain/insult: Peace with goblins, is it? I'll still lock my cellar, thanks.
toff/remark: Goblins! One has signed a treaty with goblins, how the times change.
kid/compliment: Can I meet one of the goblins under the castle, a small one?

gossip: The Council wants to send one of us up to the surface, if anyone will.
The Council fears the HAM folk are plotting against us again.
remark: Is it the daylight keeping the Dorgeshuun below since the treaty?
starter/compliment: It is good to see you again! The Council would like a favour.
starter/insult: The Council insists a surface-dweller leads, and well, here you are.
starter/remark: We are curious about the surface. And worried about its dangers.

compliment: They say you stopped them flooding our caves, so thank you.
gossip: HAM wanted to flood the caves with a drilling machine, a machine!
Zanik died on the surface and came back. Her mark glowed, they say.
plain/insult: Zanik came back dead from seeing the surface with you, if briefly.
starter/compliment: Hello again! The Council has not forgotten what you did.
starter/insult: Ah, you. Next time, perhaps keep our agent alive throughout?

gossip: The dwarves are building a train line from Keldagrim to here!
Work on the line's stopped. They dug up old goblin things.
dwarf/remark: Our tunnel's held up by goblin relics. Somebody fetch an expert.
starter/compliment: Do you have any experience with archaeology, because we need help?
starter/insult: Hurry the dig and it's a crime against knowledge, so go slowly.
starter/remark: A train link to Keldagrim. For trade, and for goodwill.

gossip: The train runs to Keldagrim now, and there's dwarves everywhere!
They say Sigmund tried to kill Zanik on the tracks to start a war.
compliment: Thank you for stopping that war between us and the dwarves.
insult: Busy day, going digging for old pots and coming back with a prophecy.
dwarf/compliment: The line's open, and no war. By Guthix, that's good work.
starter/compliment: All the Dorgeshuun owe you our lives once again, my friend.
starter/remark: There's quite a craze for surface foods at the market now.

gossip: A surface goblin's at the gate again, begging to see Zanik.
Surface goblins aren't allowed in the city, by the Council's rules.
remark: That little goblin outside keeps on about a dream, every single day.
starter/compliment: You help me get into Dorgesh-city? I want talk to Chosen Commander!
starter/insult: Big human not help Grubfoot either? Nobody ever help Grubfoot.
starter/remark: I have dream. Land of Goblins. Chosen Commander lead us there!

gossip: Zanik vanished in Yu'biusk. Oldak can't get his machine going.
Yu'biusk's a wasteland, they say. Torn apart by the war god himself.
compliment: Some nerve, walking into the goblin temple dressed as a goblin!
plain/insult: Went all that way for a land of goblins, and lost Zanik there.
remark: Grubfoot says she'll come back one day, and Grubfoot's sure of it.
kid/remark: Turn into a goblin again and do it right now!

gossip: There's a wizard sat by the Lumbridge gate. Says she's from the Tower.
That wizard bought an old amulet the smith thought was junk, they say.
remark: A wizard in Al Kharid? She says I should expect the unexpected.
starter/compliment: Mia Persten, teleportation magic, and do you fancy a mystery?
starter/insult: You've honestly never heard of me, the creator of Home Teleport?
starter/remark: Why hold our arms out to teleport? Nobody knows, which is brilliant!

gossip: Nobody's seen that wizard by the gate in ages, and nobody knows where.
compliment: Word is you found a whole temple under the sea, of all places!
Good of you, helping the wizards close that rift, if it's true.
insult: Closed a rift into the Abyss, I hear. Right after it was opened.
trader/remark: You found a temple with a junk amulet? Then I'm in the wrong trade.

gossip: The old man by the limestone mine collects bones for a museum.
remark: The old man's sack talks. I've heard it myself, with these ears.
starter/compliment: Errr... I'm an archaeologist, and I need bones, fresh ones.
starter/insult: Bones, boiled in vinegar. Can you manage that? Errr... can you?
starter/remark: Goblin, bear, frog and ram... errr, what was next after the ram, sack?

compliment: You found every one of the old man's bones, patient soul that you are.
insult: Boiled bones in vinegar for a man with a talking sack, very sensible.
starter/compliment: Ah, my bone collector! Always on the lookout for fresh ones.
starter/insult: Errr... the museum thanks you, and sack, stop sniggering.
kid/remark: Yuck! Did you really boil bones for the creepy old man?

gossip: The old man wants more bones now. From Morytania to the desert.
starter/compliment: There are still a few bits and pieces I wouldn't mind, you know.
starter/insult: More bones for the displays, errr, unless you're squeamish?
starter/remark: Mumblemumble... yes, sack. I'm asking for more bones now.

compliment: They say you fetched every last bone that old man wanted!
gossip: Heard the old man laughing up there. Went on for ages, it did.
insult: Finished his collection, I hear. Everyone will enjoy it, he says.
starter/compliment: My best collector! Everyone will enjoy my work now, everyone.
starter/insult: Sack says you missed a spot on that last bone, but sack's fussy.
kid/remark: Is the old man poorly? He laughed for ages after you left.

gossip: Gertrude's lost her cat Fluffs. Poor woman's beside herself.
Gertrude's boys saw the cat last. They're up to no good, those two.
kid/insult: If you're after a cat, ask Wilough, and bring lots of money.
starter/compliment: Have you seen my poor Fluffs? Please, could you look for her?
starter/insult: You'll look for Fluffs? You? Well, I suppose somebody must.
starter/remark: Fluffs, poor Fluffs. She never hurt anyone.

compliment: Brought Gertrude's cat home, didn't you? Kitten and all, apparently.
insult: They saw you coming, those two children you paid to find a cat.
gossip: Gertrude's Fluffs had a kitten up at the lumber yard, fancy that.
nan/compliment: Gertrude's cat's home safe. You're a good sort, dear.
kid/insult: Wilough says you paid him to find a cat, and I can find cats too.
starter/compliment: Hello again! Fluffs is purring by my side, all thanks to you.
starter/insult: Is that kitten I gave you being fed and brushed, dear?

gossip: Sarah from the farm's put up a bounty. Some monster took her cart.
Something hulking came out of the trees by the crossroads, they say.
remark: Have you seen the notice board? There's a bounty on a monster.
rough/remark: Something's been at the crops up Falador way, and it's not foxes.

compliment: Sarah's ever so pleased, if you're the one who saw off her monster.
gossip: They say it was a sourhog that spits acid, and somebody made it!
A woman in a hood was asking after that bounty too, Sarah says.
insult: I hear you fought a big pig. Did it spit at you, by any chance?
plain/insult: Got paid for a pig's foot, I hear. I'm in the wrong line of work.
kid/remark: Did the giant pig spit at you, and did you keep the foot?

gossip: They say Kolodion changes shape when he duels, but into what?
remark: Top wizards come from all over Gielinor to fight here, they say.
starter/compliment: I am the great Kolodion, master of battle magic, care to duel?
starter/insult: Hah, a wizard of your level wants to duel me, don't be absurd!
starter/remark: Many wizards fall in my arena, never to rise again.

compliment: Blimey! You beat Kolodion in every shape, even the demon?
insult: Bested Kolodion and then went for a dip in a pool, very mystical.
gossip: Another mage has chosen a god at the statues, they say.
starter/compliment: Ah, my battle mage! How are you, and are you enjoying the bloodshed?
starter/insult: You beat me once, traveller. Don't let it go to your head.

gossip: Kolodion says three strange powers are loose in the Wilderness.
They say a general of Zamorak walks the deep Wilderness now.
starter/compliment: Three beings with power beyond even mine, and I want their remains.
starter/insult: You've potential, but what chance has a wizard of your level?

compliment: Ye gods! You killed a Zamorakian general and a justiciar?
gossip: Servants of three gods fell in the Wilderness, and one mage did it.
plain/insult: Killed champions of three gods for a better cape, worth it, was it?
shady/insult: You cut down Porazdir? Zamorak forgets nothing, meddler.
vicar/remark: A justiciar of Saradomin slain for a cloak, so they say, dear me.
starter/compliment: Your cape carries the power of three gods now, so use it well.
starter/insult: Even my power has limits. Yours, I suspect, has many more.

gossip: That woman by the mountain calls herself an archaeologist, never digs.
There's an old door under the rocks by Ice Mountain, she reckons.
dwarf/remark: Why, by Guthix, does that human lass guard a pile of rocks all day?
starter/compliment: You there, fancy some ancient ruins with untold riches inside?
starter/insult: You'll do. I can't leave. Some other archaeologist might pinch it.
starter/remark: Untold riches in there! Er, I mean untold history, of course.

compliment: Opened the old ruins under Ice Mountain and found a dwarf, I hear!
gossip: That archaeologist was a grave robber all along, and she ran off!
insult: Very heroic of you, fetching a sandwich for a thief.
plain/insult: Who won, when you played rock paper scissors with that drunk dwarf?
dwarf/compliment: By Guthix, an Imcando dwarf alive under the mountain!
kid/compliment: Show me the flex the barbarian taught you, go on!

starter/compliment: Nilsal, traveller. Could you spare some cooked fish or meat?
starter/insult: No food? Never mind. I shall just sit here and starve, quietly.
starter/remark: I ran from the spiders. Further in. It seemed wise at the time.

starter/compliment: Nilsal, friend! Logosia will be thrilled with those tomes.
starter/insult: Thank you again for the food. Some salt next time, perhaps?
starter/remark: Ralos and Ranul, sun and moon. Our order began here, I'm sure.

gossip: The museum's sending a barge to some island north of Morytania!
Nine barges they've built for that island, and not one got there.
remark: Imagine building a barge for the museum that doesn't float.
plain/insult: The museum wants someone brave for its cursed barge, so not you, then.
starter/compliment: You have the qualifications! Just the person for our voyage.
starter/insult: You have the qualifications, but I'm not sure you're ready.
starter/remark: An island north of Morytania. Easily the most interesting thing.

compliment: You got the museum's barge to that island! First one ever, they say.
gossip: Barge crew passed out on a sealegs potion, so someone else steered!
They say the seventh barge is still lost, and nobody's gone looking.
insult: Steered the barge while the crew lay out cold, like a proper sailor.
guard/remark: The museum sending folk to sea is not my department.
starter/compliment: Welcome to the museum! And thank you again for that voyage.
starter/insult: Ah, our navigator, and the barge is still in one piece, remarkably.

gossip: King Lathas wants that old outpost torn down for an alchemists' lab.
remark: The fellow at the outpost keeps shouting 'All is lost!' at people.
starter/compliment: Wait a minute. You could help me! This building has history!
starter/insult: Don't bother, you're not experienced enough to help me!
starter/remark: All is lost! This great building will soon be in ruin.

compliment: You saved the old outpost, didn't you? It's a museum now, apparently.
gossip: The King's let the outpost be. A letter did it, they say.
insult: Got quizzed on a warrior's breakfast for a bit of history, I hear.
gnome/compliment: The outpost stands, human, and we gnomes do like old things.
starter/compliment: Hurrah! My saviour! Do look round the new museum room.
starter/insult: Back again? Touch nothing, because that's all history, that is.

gossip: Sir Tiffy sits in the park all day. Recruiting, someone said.
Sir Tiffy's lot only take the clever ones, brains first, I hear.
remark: That Sir Tiffy says 'what?' after everything... everything, what?
sharp/insult: Temple Knights want the clever sort. Ah. Well, best of luck with that.
guard/gossip: Word from the castle: Sir Amik's sending another one to the park.
starter/compliment: Hello, friend! I may already have put your name forward for something.
starter/insult: Sir Tiffy tests for wits, friend, and I did say you had some.
starter/remark: Sir Tiffy's in the park. I really ought to have told you more.

compliment: So you passed Sir Tiffy's tests? You're the clever sort, then.
An initiate of the Temple Knights, and you kept that quiet?
insult: Word is the Temple Knights tested you with a fox and a chicken.
plain/insult: Bold choice, sitting Sir Tiffy's test without a stitch on.
gossip: Another initiate for Sir Tiffy with gold trim and all, they say.
toff/compliment: One hears you've been made an initiate, which is jolly good of them.
kid/insult: You did puzzles to be a knight? I'd have just hit someone.
starter/compliment: Hello, friend! Sir Tiffy tells me you did splendidly.
starter/insult: Ah, the initiate. Do try not to embarrass my letter.

gossip: They say Solus Dellagar's loose again, the murder-mage himself.
Some clerk muddled an initiate's papers, and heads will roll for it.
remark: Lock your doors tonight. There's a mad mage on the loose.
sharp/insult: Sir Tiffy wants Solus caught. By someone competent, ideally.
guard/gossip: Word from the castle is watch for a mage, wanted for murder.
starter/compliment: Ah, old bean! Bit of a muddle with your papers, what?
starter/insult: Five years a squire, dontchaknow. Unless there's a crisis, what?
starter/remark: Solus Dellagar loose again, jolly bad show, what?

compliment: Well done, running Solus Dellagar to ground like that.
A White Knight now, I hear. Sir Amik must be chuffed.
insult: Some trophy, bringing back a mage's hat as proof.
plain/insult: I hear you had help catching that mage. Quite a fair bit of help.
gossip: They say Solus Dellagar's been dealt with, so we can sleep easy.
guard/compliment: A White Knight, are you? Then you know where the armoury is.
kid/compliment: You caught the murder-mage? Did he turn you into anything?
starter/compliment: Spiffing work with Solus, old bean, absolutely first class!
starter/insult: Haw haw! You had a bit of help with Solus though, eh, old bean?

gossip: Witchaven folk are acting oddly and the mayor looks ill, I hear.
Witchaven's mayor is restoring some old shrine, odd hobby for a mayor.
remark: Nobody goes to Witchaven now. Not since that platform went up.
starter/compliment: Ah, old bean! Fancy a jaunt to Witchaven, all hush-hush and secret?
starter/insult: Witchaven needs looking into. Do try not to get lost, what?
starter/remark: Odd business in Witchaven, jolly odd, dontchaknow.

compliment: Well done, word is you saved Witchaven from something nasty.
Rather you than me, facing that giant slug under Witchaven.
insult: Is that Witchaven slime on your boots again?
plain/insult: Opened a sealed door for a sickly mayor, wasn't that clever, I hear.
gossip: They say there's something far worse than slugs off Witchaven.
kid/insult: You fought slugs? I squash those with my boot.
starter/compliment: Splendid show at Witchaven, old bean! Savant speaks highly of you.
starter/insult: I hear you let the slugs in yourself? Something of a gaffe, old bean.

gossip: The Sinclairs have upped and left the mansion, just like that.
Nobody's seen King Arthur or his knights for ages, odd, that.
Anna Sinclair's up for trial in Seers' for her own father, they say!
remark: Quiet at the mansion lately. Too quiet, if you ask me.
starter/compliment: Oh, it's you! You didn't hear it from me, but the Sinclairs left!
starter/insult: Any interesting news? No? Then what are you standing around for?
starter/remark: The King gone, the Sinclairs gone. Quite a coincidence, I say.

compliment: Word is you brought King Arthur home, and Camelot owes you for it.
You freed Merlin and the knights from Morgan Le Faye, they say!
insult: I hear you defended Anna Sinclair in court, of all people.
gossip: Merlin's threatened to make rabbits of the Sinclairs, they say.
remark: The Sinclairs never leave the mansion now, can't think why.
toff/remark: Arthur's back at the Round Table, one hears, so do try to keep up.
kid/compliment: You saved the King? Did Merlin really make frogs?
starter/compliment: Oh, it's you! Everyone's talking about Camelot, but I said it first.
starter/insult: You might have told me first, since I'm the gossip round here.

gossip: Trolls on Death Plateau again, and they come down at night.
Harold lost the storeroom combination. He's been in the pub since.
remark: They say the Prince loves a puzzle, and the guards can't stand them.
