guard/gossip: Word from the camp is trolls raiding by night, so bar your door.
starter/compliment: Citizen! The trolls hold Death Plateau, so do you know another path?
starter/insult: You, citizen? My soldiers couldn't break through, but do try.
starter/remark: A key would do. But no, the Prince is fond of puzzles.

compliment: Good work, finding a secret way up Death Plateau like that.
Dunstan's boy is in the Imperial Guard now, thanks to you.
plain/insult: How heroic, beating a guard at dice for a scrap of paper.
remark: Old Tenzing had a secret path all along, who knew?
kid/compliment: Show me the secret path! I won't tell the trolls, promise.
starter/compliment: Welcome back, citizen! Burthorpe owes you a great deal.
starter/insult: A puzzle solved, citizen. Don't let it go to your head.

gossip: The raid went badly. Trolls took Dunstan's son, they say.
Godric's held in the Troll Stronghold, poor Dunstan.
remark: Dunstan's beside himself. His boy's still with the trolls.
guard/gossip: Word from the camp is we were ambushed from the north, so stay sharp.
starter/compliment: Friend! The trolls took Godric, so will you go after him?
starter/insult: None of my men will go. I'd not blame you either, friend.
starter/remark: Ambushed from the north. We never stood a chance.

compliment: You brought Godric home from the trolls? Dunstan's been beaming since.
Blimey, you beat a troll called Dad in his own arena, I hear.
insult: I hear you rescued Godric and some mad old hermit as a bonus.
gossip: Trolls are named after the first thing they try to eat, they say.
kid/remark: If trolls are named after what they eat first, what would you be?
starter/compliment: Welcome back, friend! Godric's safe, and that's your doing.
starter/insult: Back again, friend? The trolls haven't stopped raiding, mind.

gossip: They say Ug's crying over Aga again, and she's with Arrg.
Aga wants a Trollweiss flower. Nobody's seen one in years.
remark: Arrg's got other girlfriends, word is, so don't tell Aga.
starter/compliment: Man-thing help Ug? Then maybe Ug not eat man-thing!
starter/insult: Go away, man-thing, leave Ug alone!
starter/remark: Aga so beautiful. Smell like rotting dead ice wolf.

compliment: They say Ug finally went to Aga, thanks to you seeing off Arrg.
plain/insult: Went sledging for a flower for a troll, which I suppose is romantic.
gossip: Arrg's lost all his swagger since a human beat him.
starter/compliment: Man-thing very strong and very nice. Ug so happy he not eat anyone.
starter/insult: Man-thing no touch Aga or Ug kill. Ha, Ug joke! Ug not kill... much.

gossip: Sanfew's after a herb called goutweed that only the trolls know.
The druids are still purifying their stone circle, slow work, that.
remark: Troll cooking needs a herb, apparently. Since when do trolls cook?
starter/compliment: Ah, young 'un! I need a herb the trolls call goutweed.
starter/insult: No doubt some other adventurer will come along who can help.
starter/remark: Goutweed... only the trolls know where it grows now.

compliment: Clever, getting goutweed out of the trolls for Sanfew like that.
insult: Borrowed Tegid's dirty laundry, and rather you than me, I hear.
gossip: A parrot! They say you passed one off as a man to the trolls!
remark: Sanfew's ever so cheerful lately. Found his herb, I gather.
kid/compliment: Can I see the parrot you dressed up as a man?
starter/compliment: Ah, young 'un! Bring me more goutweed and I'll trade you herbs.
starter/insult: Ah, young 'un. Do wash after that troll kitchen, won't you?

gossip: Trolls picked all the goutweed, so now there's none left... clever.
Burntmeat's assistant wants to be a farmer, a troll farmer!
remark: My Arm's named after his dad's arm, the first thing he ever chewed.
starter/compliment: Oh, it you again. Burntmeat need big important job doing.
starter/insult: Humans grow goutweed? You lying to Burntmeat!
starter/remark: No goutweed grow now. Trolls pick every last bit of it.

compliment: Goutweed's growing on the stronghold roof now, and that's your doing.
Burntmeat's promised never to cook another human, thanks to you.
insult: Glamorous, fetching camel dung all the way from the desert.
gossip: My Arm went to Karamja and punched their best warrior, they say.
A giant bird came down on My Arm's patch and a human saw it off.
starter/compliment: Oh, it you! Burntmeat keep promise, goat taste just as good.
starter/insult: Burntmeat promise not cook humans. Burntmeat still think 'bout it.

gossip: A troll called Wolfbone has come visiting from up north.
There's a troll town far to the north called Weiss, they say.
remark: My Arm's training a troll called Drunken Dwarf's Leg, honestly.
starter/compliment: Oh, it you! Important visitor come and Burntmeat need you.
starter/insult: Big important visitor here. You try not look so tasty.
starter/remark: Wolfbone come from Weiss. Want clever troll go back with him.

compliment: They say My Arm married Snowflake and you did the wedding!
You saw off Mother up in Weiss? I'd not have gone near her.
insult: Carried the Wise Old Man up a mountain in a coffin, I hear.
plain/insult: Wedding priest for a pair of trolls? Found your calling, perhaps?
gossip: Snowflake leads Weiss now. Nicer than Mother, they all agree.
The Wise Old Man played dead for a troll and snored, they say.
kid/compliment: I bet there was cake at the troll wedding and I bet it was goat.
starter/compliment: Oh, it you! My Arm married to big chief now, fancy that.
starter/insult: Oh, it you. Still not eaten up mountain, that make Burntmeat sad.

gossip: They say something unseen walks the road south of Rellekka.
starter/compliment: You walk the Shadow Realm yet live, so I may have use for you.
starter/insult: I never can tell you humans apart. Ugly creatures, all of you.
starter/remark: The planets near alignment, and still my scouts are late.

starter/compliment: Ah, my sinful messenger. You served your purpose well.
starter/insult: Get out of here, you filthy skinbag. I will not waste my time.
starter/remark: Bouncer was angry that you killed him, which is quite natural, really.

gossip: They say Old Man Yarlo's place is falling apart, poor fellow.
remark: Marlo's always asking builders about his dad's house, bless him.
starter/compliment: Hello! You look handy. Could you do me a little favour?
starter/insult: We can't hire you for proper work. But a little favour, maybe?
starter/remark: Dad's house is really decrepit. And it's off the record, mind.

compliment: That was kind of you, fixing up Old Man Yarlo's house.
Old Yarlo's got a new bed, I hear. Wood that keeps the damp out.
insult: Built an old man some stools, so I hear, and do they wobble?
gossip: They say old Yarlo was a carpenter once and now tells others how.
kid/insult: You made a chair? My grandad makes chairs, and his don't wobble.
starter/compliment: Hello again! Dad loves his new bed and says it's ever so dry.
starter/insult: Oh, it's you. Dad says you rush about too much, and he's right.

gossip: Aretha wrote of an artefact buried in Kourend, but won't say where.
remark: Aretha says to respect the souls. Every single time I pass.
starter/compliment: Respect the souls, traveller. You seem the respectful sort.
starter/insult: Let me guess. You want to know where the soul bearer lies, how dull.
starter/remark: Respect the souls, traveller.

gossip: They say Aretha herself told someone where the soul bearer lies!
starter/compliment: Ah, traveller. I trust the artefact serves you well.
starter/insult: Hmph, mortals. You have your artefact, so now respect the souls.

gossip: The barbarians only let you in if you can drink like one.
remark: Alfred Grimhand drank every bar from here to Karamja, the legend.
starter/compliment: Barbarians only, and you don't look like one, so prove it!
starter/insult: Oi, whaddya want? Do I look like a bank to you?
starter/remark: We barbarians like a good drink, and outsiders never keep up.

compliment: Drank every bar on the card? The barbarians respect that.
remark: Smashing your vials like a barbarian now? Mind the glass when you do.
plain/insult: I hear you crawled home from Karamja, and crawled is the word.
starter/compliment: You drink like a barbarian, so in you go!
starter/insult: Never learned to read, me. But you look like you've drunk plenty.

gossip: The Heroes' Guild wants a firebird feather and a lava eel... cooked.
Only the greatest heroes get into that guild, they say.
remark: Handy, that firebirds only live on Entrana, or so I'm told.
starter/compliment: Greetings and welcome to the Heroes' Guild, or at least to its door.
starter/insult: You're a hero? I've never heard of you.
starter/remark: A feather, an armband and a lava eel. The eel wants cooking, mind.

compliment: A member of the Heroes' Guild! You've come up in the world.
They say you got into the Heroes' Guild, and fair play to you.
insult: A hero, they say. Fetched a feather and cooked an eel.
plain/insult: They let you in the Heroes' Guild? Standards must be slipping, then.
gossip: They say Scarface Pete over in Brimhaven's lost his candlesticks.
kid/compliment: If you're a real hero from the guild then do something heroic!
starter/compliment: Greetings, hero. The door's always open for you now.
starter/insult: Your final task is... oh, just a little Heroes' Guild humour.

gossip: Goblins keep breaking through the dwarves' fence, they say.
The dwarves lost touch with their watchtower to the south.
remark: The dwarves have some secret weapon up there, and won't say what.
dwarf/gossip: By Guthix, the shame of goblins overrunning the Black Guard's camp.
starter/compliment: Guthix be praised! The cavalry has arrived, and a hero with it.
starter/insult: A human in the Black Guard? Well, we are rather desperate.
starter/remark: If the goblins overrun us, they'll swarm the mines.

compliment: Good on you for saving Gilob's boy from the goblins.
You're in fine company, an honorary member of the Black Guard.
insult: A human fixed a dwarf cannon? The engineers must be livid.
remark: Poor Gilob. Finest lieutenant Lawgof had, they say.
dwarf/compliment: By Guthix! You mended the Black Guard's cannon, human?
kid/compliment: Does your cannon go bang? Can I hear it do a proper bang?
starter/compliment: Hello there, trooper! Goblins have been no trouble since.
starter/insult: Trooper! Did I give you orders to stand there, because I did not!

gossip: That lad's ball went over the witch's hedge, so it's gone now.
The old lady behind the hedge locks things in her shed, they say.
remark: Nobody goes near that garden. Not after dark, not ever.
kid/remark: There's a witch in that house who keeps balls, and worse.
starter/compliment: Please, can you get my ball back? It's in the scary lady's shed.
starter/insult: You won't help? You're a meany!
starter/remark: I only kicked it a bit. Now it's in that horrible shed.

compliment: You got the lad's ball back from the witch? Braver than I'd have been.
insult: Breaking into a witch's house for a ball shows real priorities, eh?
gossip: They say something nasty lived in that witch's shed, but not any more.
kid/compliment: Was the witch's monster really big, or bigger than that?
starter/compliment: Thank you so much! I'm ever so careful with it now.
starter/insult: You took ages. I nearly grew up waiting.

gossip: Thormac's scorpions have got loose, so mind your ankles, eh?
Rare desert scorpions loose about the place... marvellous.
remark: Only a sorcerer would keep scorpions as pets, honestly.
starter/compliment: Hello! I am Thormac the sorcerer, and might you assist me?
starter/insult: Blast! I suppose I'll have to find someone else, then.
starter/remark: I left their cage door open. Quick little beasties, they are.

compliment: Steady hands, catching all of Thormac's scorpions like that.
insult: Glamorous work, chasing a sorcerer's scorpions round the world.
starter/compliment: Aha, my scorpions' rescuer! They're all home and safe.
starter/insult: Do mind the cage door on your way out, because I shan't ask twice.
starter/remark: Bring me a battlestaff and I'll make it mystic, for a fee.

starter/compliment: An adventurer. You must have many tales to tell me.
starter/insult: Tell me... a story... if you have one worth the telling.
starter/remark: Three thousand years in the dark, and I am bored.

starter/compliment: Ah, the storyteller returns. Tell me... a story...
starter/insult: Your last tale was adequate, so do try harder this time.
starter/remark: Guthix wept here. The rocks weep with Him still.

gossip: Ali Morrisane's nephew was due up from Pollnivneach, and never came.
Pollnivneach is run by two gangs now, bandits and Menaphites.
remark: Ali Morrisane wants staff. Says he's too busy selling to sell.
compliment: Easy coin, friend, fetching Ali Morrisane's nephew for him.
plain/insult: Ali's looking for someone gullible, and oh look, here you are.
starter/compliment: My friend, a nephew of mine is in Pollnivneach, would you fetch him?
starter/insult: Too busy adventuring, my friend? Then at least look at my wares.
starter/remark: Sand for the Bedabin, trinkets for everyone else... and no staff.

compliment: Blimey! You're the one who ran both gangs out of Pollnivneach?
I hear Pollnivneach's quieter now since you sorted those gangs out.
insult: Went for a nephew and came back in a fake beard, Ali's best sale yet.
plain/insult: Robbing the mayor's wife and calling it heroism is very Pollnivneach.
gossip: The mayor smuggled Ali's nephew out of Pollnivneach by night, I hear.
Both Pollnivneach gangs are drowning their sorrows at the bar now.
trader/insult: Ali sold you a beard and a headdress. I'd have done you a camel too.
starter/compliment: Did you not enjoy the action and intrigue of Pollnivneach, my friend?
starter/insult: Ah, my friend! You're not as dumb as you look, though it's close.
starter/remark: Young Baba. The greatest salesman in Gielinor... after his uncle.
kid/remark: Was the bandit champion bigger than you when you fought him?

gossip: Irena's daughter went into the desert days ago and isn't back yet.
They say that mining camp to the south is worked by captives.
remark: Poor soul, that woman by the pass has been sobbing all week.
compliment: Irena's lost her girl in the desert. You've the look of a finder.
plain/insult: Irena's daughter is lost out there, and you're queueing for a pass.
guard/remark: A girl went through this pass and never came back, not on my shift.
starter/compliment: Oh, please! My Ana's lost in the desert and I beg you to look for her.
starter/insult: It may already have happened! Ana's missing and you just stand there!
starter/remark: Boo hoo... my only daughter... she said she'd be back yesterday.

compliment: Bless you! You brought Irena's girl back from that camp?
Clever, smuggling a girl out of the mines in a barrel like that.
insult: Rescued a girl in a barrel. I hope you said sorry about the barrel.
plain/insult: Fought a mercenary captain for a girl in a barrel, as you do.
gossip: Ana's home safe. Her mother says she'll be off again soon enough.
Captain Siad's weapon plans went missing from the camp, they say.
starter/compliment: You found my Ana! I'm ever so grateful. She's the adventurous type.
starter/insult: Back again? Don't go giving Ana ideas. She's bad enough already.
kid/remark: If the girl got to ride in a barrel, can I ride in a barrel?

gossip: Nardah's fountain has run dry. Even river water vanishes on the way.
Ali the carter's selling water at Pollnivneach prices, grim times.
remark: Rokuh's choc ices are about the only cool thing left in Nardah.
compliment: The mayor says the town's cursed. He'd be glad of a clever head.
plain/insult: Nardah's cursed and parched, and you've brought nothing to drink.
starter/compliment: Many salutations! Our town is cursed. Could you help us lift it?
starter/insult: Any progress on our curse? No? The despair grows daily, you know.
starter/remark: First the fountain, then the river water... and that poor priest.

compliment: The fountain's running again! They say you found the river spirits.
Elidinis bless you, if you brought the statuette back to the shrine.
insult: I hear you cut the soles off the mayor's shoes, for a genie.
plain/insult: Gave a genie the mayor's sole. He's still checking it was the shoe.
gossip: Shiratti's stopped grumbling. Mostly. The statuette's home again.
That Saradominist priest talked Nardah into throwing the statue away.
starter/compliment: Many salutations, friend! The fountain flows again, thanks to you.
starter/insult: Ah, it's you. Please keep your knife well away from my shoes.
starter/remark: May Sarad... er, I mean Elidinis watch over you.
kid/remark: The fountain works again! I drank so much my belly sloshes.

gossip: Father Reen's after whoever carries Silverlight and says it's urgent.
They say dark wizards have gone off to Uzer for some ritual or other.
remark: That priest by the bank looks a bit lost. Too hot for him, I'd say.
compliment: Father Reen needs the one with Silverlight, and you've the look of it.
plain/insult: Father Reen wants a demon slayer. He'll be disappointed, I expect.
starter/compliment: Thank Saradomin I found you! You still have Silverlight?
starter/insult: There's an urgent task only you can do, Saradomin help us all.
starter/remark: Denath and his apprentices in Uzer... summoning Agrith-Naar...

compliment: Saradomin be thanked! You're the one who slew Agrith-Naar?
Word is your sword drank a demon's blood, and it does look darker.
insult: Joined a cult of dark wizards to save the world, naturally.
plain/insult: Wore black and chanted with dark wizards. All for a good cause, eh?
gossip: They say Denath was the demon all along and fooled his own cult.
Father Reen's back from Uzer. Says the world's no better for it.
vicar/compliment: Saradomin smile on you. A demon slain is a good day's work.
starter/compliment: My friend, Agrith-Naar is gone, Saradomin be thanked!
starter/insult: Sarcasm is forbidden in the holy book of Saradomin, just so you know.
starter/remark: We slew the demon and the world's just as it was, most vexing.

gossip: A sculptor's camped south of the bandits wanting a statue, out here!
That sculptor says some accident left him unable to hold a chisel.
remark: Who puts up a statue in the middle of the desert, honestly?
compliment: Lazim the sculptor wants a strong back, and yours looks the part.
plain/insult: Lazim wants stone quarried, and he'll moan at a weedy sort like you.
starter/compliment: Ah, an adventurer. Could you spare some time to help with my art?
starter/insult: Large blocks? I doubt a weedy adventurer like you could lift one.
starter/remark: The desert's plain and full of sand. It needs more decoration.

compliment: Blimey! You freed something camel-headed from under the sand?
insult: Lazim calls you an imbecile. He calls everyone that, mind.
plain/insult: Lazim dropped hints the size of Varrock, and you missed every one.
gossip: That statue fell straight through, and a whole temple under it!
Two Mahjarrat came out of that temple and went north, they say.
starter/compliment: The temple is interesting, I'll grant. So, grudgingly, thank you.
starter/insult: How are you and your defective brain doing nowadays, adventurer?
If you want to see who ruined my plans, look in a mirror.
kid/remark: Can you really talk to camels? What do they say about me?

gossip: There's a clay golem in Uzer, pacing. It's been at it for ages.
remark: Uzer was a great city once. Now there's just one cracked golem.
compliment: That golem in Uzer is falling apart. A bit of clay would mend it.
plain/insult: Even the golem in Uzer has more purpose than you, by the look.
starter/compliment: You... help? Body damaged and clay needed. Task is still incomplete.
starter/insult: No living being can destroy the demon. That is why golems exist.
starter/remark: Damage... must repair... task incomplete...

compliment: You put the old golem's mind at rest? That's a real kindness, that.
insult: Fed a golem a scrap saying 'your task is done', which is a neat trick.
plain/insult: Lucky timing, the demon being dead already when you got the thanks.
gossip: The golem in Uzer's stopped fretting, says its task is done.
A statuette went missing from the Varrock Museum, they say.
starter/compliment: Task complete. Mind at rest now, thank you.
starter/insult: Golem was never programmed to appreciate the city, or you.
starter/remark: Demon destroyed... task complete... no further instructions.

gossip: Unferth's cat Bob has been gone a week and he's beside himself.
Hild's trying to find Unferth's cat. Says cats are misunderstood.
remark: Bob comes home every week for his food... not this week, though.
compliment: Unferth's lost his cat, poor soul. Lend him a hand, would you?
plain/insult: Unferth's lost a cat. A cat. It's about the size of a loaf.
starter/compliment: Do you have a cat? Then you'll understand, Bob's been gone a week!
starter/insult: This isn't funny! My Bob is missing and you're just standing there.
starter/remark: Bob... where are you, Bob? He must be hungry by now.
kid/remark: Have you seen a black cat called Bob? There's a reward, probably.

compliment: Bob's home and Unferth's beaming. Had a close shave, too, I hear.
Kind of you, looking after Unferth while his cat was away.
insult: Shaved Unferth bald and called it a chore? He's still cold, poor man.
plain/insult: Medicine, that, dressing up as a doctor to give a man water.
gossip: Unferth says Bob came home on his own and nobody had to fetch him.
starter/compliment: Bob came home! I'm so happy! I'm not a well man, mind.
starter/insult: Fat lot of use you were! Bob came home on his own!
starter/remark: My back hurts, my spleen's off... but Bob's home, so there's that.
kid/insult: Did Unferth wriggle when you shaved him, because I would've?

gossip: The Devourer's after something in Osmumten's tomb, they say.
Maisa's camped by the Necropolis pyramid, waiting for someone.
plain/insult: The Devourer's in that tomb, and you're out here in the sun.
starter/compliment: Hey! You made it. The Devourer must be deeper inside.
starter/remark: The longer we wait, the stronger she gets.

compliment: You freed four gods from that tomb, they say, so blessings on you.
Blimey! You faced the Devourer in Osmumten's tomb and walked out?
plain/insult: Thorough, freeing four gods and letting the Devourer simply walk off.
gossip: They say Apmeken, Crondis, Het and Scabaras are all free at last!
The Devourer's fled the tomb, some say to Menaphos, some say worse.
starter/compliment: Good work in there. The lesser gods won't forget it, and nor will I.
starter/remark: Her forces will be back. Osmumten was very clear on that.

gossip: Old Dondakan's still firing his cannon at that rock, years on.
The others gave up on Dondakan's rock. Not worth the time, they said.
remark: Hear that boom? Dondakan's cannon again, every blessed day.
compliment: Dondakan could use a young pair of legs on that rock of his.
plain/insult: Dondakan's rock has beaten every dwarf here, so it'll enjoy you.
dwarf/remark: By Guthix, that rock's harder than runite, and Dondakan won't let go.
starter/compliment: Perhaps a young adventurer like you will help an old dwarf like me?
starter/insult: Suit yourself, I don't need any help from a human anyway!
starter/remark: It's not a wall, it's a rock, and a very special rock at that!

compliment: Blimey! You're the one Dondakan shot into the rock, and you lived?
They say the riddle of the rock is cracked, and there's gold inside.
insult: Fired out of a cannon head first, which explains a great deal.
plain/insult: Banished a demon in a gold helmet. Dressed for it, at least.
gossip: Dondakan's rich now on gold from that rock, after the company's cut.
dwarf/compliment: By Guthix, a demon in Dondakan's rock, banished by a human!
starter/compliment: After all these years the riddle of the rock is cracked, thank you!
starter/insult: Wear that helmet, mind, unless you fancy cracking your skull open.
starter/remark: Plenty of gold for me! For us all, I mean. Of course I meant us all.

gossip: The Consortium runs Keldagrim now. Kings are a distant memory.
The boatman takes humans to Keldagrim for free, generous, that.
compliment: Fancy seeing Keldagrim? The boatman will take you for free.
plain/insult: Humans! A free boat ride and you're still dithering about it.
dwarf/remark: Five hundred years since King Alvis. The Consortium rules now.
starter/compliment: Ho there, human! Want to take a ride with me, free of charge for you?
starter/insult: No no, that's what the ferryman is for! I'm going to Keldagrim myself.
starter/remark: Just waiting for my ship to arrive... could take a few minutes.

compliment: Fine work, rebuilding King Alvis's statue, and you a human.
Word is the Consortium let a human choose the statue's head!
insult: Knocked over King Alvis and then fixed him, so fair's fair.
plain/insult: Lucky the Black Guard let you off for crashing a boat into a king.
gossip: The Red Axe director stormed out of the meeting swearing revenge.
Hollow threats from the Red Axe about boycotting the Trade Octagon.
dwarf/compliment: By Guthix, human, that new statue's a fine piece of work.
starter/compliment: Ho there! Every time I pass that statue I think of you, human.
starter/insult: Ho, you again! Last time we hit a king, so sit still this time.
kid/remark: What did it sound like when you crashed into the big statue?

gossip: The Red Axe have left the city. Never happened before, they say.
That drunk in East Keldagrim keeps shouting about the Red Axe.
remark: The drunk dwarf talks of nothing but kebabs, and the Red Axe.
compliment: Veldaban wants someone to find where the Red Axe went, maybe you?
plain/insult: The Black Guard needs a sharp mind. You'll do at a pinch, I suppose.
dwarf/remark: Red Axe gone and the directors fretting? I'll need a beer for that.
starter/compliment: Have you heard? The Red Axe have left, and I may need you again.
starter/insult: Everyone thinks that drunk is mad, and perhaps they're right.
starter/remark: Where has the Red Axe gone? And why does that drunk know?

compliment: Veldaban believes you, you know. Even if nobody else does.
insult: Tell us the marching kebabs one again! We never tire of hearing it.
plain/insult: Went off on Black Guard business and came back wanting kebabs.
gossip: A human fell off a chair at the Laughing Miner, kebabs, it was.
The Red Axe? Nobody's seen hide nor hair of them, not a whisper.
barkeep/insult: Beer and a kebab again? You're worse than the drunk in the corner.
starter/compliment: Don't worry, I believe you. Some spell made you forget, I'm sure.
starter/insult: So no word on the Red Axe, only kebabs, and I suppose kebabs will do.
kid/insult: You fell off your chair and everybody laughed, me the most!

gossip: Something's taking Gordon's cattle at night, and nobody's seen it.
The soldiers are busy with lizardmen, so Gordon's on his own.
remark: Gordon's mended his gate. Won't keep that beast out long, mind.
compliment: Gordon wants someone to bring him a beast's head, and it pays well.
plain/insult: Gordon wants a beast's head. Bring yours, it'll do for a start.
starter/compliment: You look like you know your way around a weapon, so have you a moment?
starter/insult: No head, no pay. Nothing personal. I can't be seen paying for air.
starter/remark: Some strange beast's been at the livestock again, always at night.

compliment: Fair play, doing for that beast that took Gordon's cattle.
Gordon's got the beast's head up by his stairs, ever so proud.
insult: Was the beast's head always so lumpy, or is that clay I can see?
plain/insult: Brought Gordon a head. Didn't bring the beast that wore it, mind.
gossip: Mary says that head by the stairs looks awful, and Gordon loves it.
starter/compliment: There's my friend! The head looks grand by the stairs, eh?
starter/insult: Ah, you. Next time, bring the head the first time round.
starter/remark: Look at it. Magnificent. Mary keeps wiping her brow, though.
kid/remark: Is that head at Gordon's real, because it looks painted?

gossip: The old gravedigger at the Barrows is muttering about an icon.
starter/compliment: It's time to dig, dig, dig, and you can dig, so come, come!
starter/insult: Slow? No! Only fast! Fast dig and dig and dig and dig!
starter/remark: The brothers six... his faithful servants, and he wants it back!

gossip: They say the old man at the Barrows destroyed some ancient icon.
starter/compliment: Job well done, but there's still more digging, always more digging!
starter/insult: Prize? You had your prize! Now dig and dig and dig and dig!
starter/remark: The old plan is gone. We're doing it his way now...

gossip: There's an odd, distinct-looking hill giant up on the plateau.
remark: They say giants used to make things, big things, long ago.

compliment: Big work, that, helping the giant fix that old foundry.
plain/insult: You helped a giant make swords. What could possibly go wrong?
gossip: There's a giant forging swords under the plateau now, big ones.
starter/compliment: Well done, little one. Foundry yours to use, whenever you want.
starter/insult: Obor only attack if you trespass, so maybe knock first, manners.
starter/remark: Giants not just killers. Kovac help giants remember.
Kovac still leanin... learning.

gossip: The Fitzharmons say they're quite content, so don't go pestering them.
remark: Dimintheis says his sons are always wanting something done.
compliment: Dimintheis still talks about how grateful he is for that crest.
plain/insult: Are you the adventurer who keeps begging the Fitzharmons for jobs?
starter/compliment: My family consider what you did a great service, and we're content.
starter/insult: What was that? I didn't quite catch it, try my sons, perhaps.
starter/remark: There really isn't anything. I am very content with life.

compliment: Kind of you to put food on the Fitzharmons' table, they say.
insult: Oh dear. You gave the Fitzharmons a fortune for steel gauntlets?
plain/insult: Gave a fortune to a family in the worst corner of Varrock, how shrewd.
gossip: The Fitzharmons rich? They say it's all show and not a coin behind it.
starter/compliment: I will not forget what you did for my family, friend, truly I won't.
starter/insult: Heirlooms? We've crates of those gauntlets in the basement.
starter/remark: Would any wealthy man choose to live in the darkest corner of Varrock?
kid/remark: The man in the little house says he's posh, but he isn't.

gossip: Two sisters in the sewers want adventurers with cats, odd pair.
Gertrude says there's a ratcatching business under Varrock.
remark: The rats in the sewers are getting bolder, they say.
compliment: Got a cat? Gertrude knows some ratcatchers worth a visit.
plain/insult: The ratcatchers want someone with a cat, and the cat's the brains.
starter/compliment: Oh yes, before I forget, are you still in the adventuring business?
starter/insult: I can't stand those sewers, or I'd have looked into it myself.
starter/remark: I don't know which is harder, raising kids or cats.
kid/remark: There's rats in the sewers as big as dogs and Mum won't let me go!

compliment: Fair play to your cat, beating the king rat in that warehouse.
They say you led every rat in Port Sarim into the sea with a tune!
insult: I hear you piped the rats into the sea, and nobody asked the fish.
plain/insult: Your cat did the hard work, I hear. You just carried the fish.
gossip: Hooknosed Jack's cat ate some poisoned rats and still pulled through.
There's a rat pit in Varrock now. Cats against rats, imagine.
starter/compliment: Ooh, the ratcatcher! Fluffs would be proud of you, dear.
starter/insult: You smell of sewer, dear. Wipe your feet before Fluffs smells you.
kid/compliment: Can I stroke your cat, the one that beat the king rat?

gossip: They say that swamp ogre can't make his own arrows, all thumbs.
remark: That ogre keeps shouting about chompy birds, every single day.
ogre/gossip: Rantz wants da chompy, but Rantz got no stabbers. Hur, hur.
ogre/insult: Creature got no stabbers? Creature no use for da chompy.
starter/compliment: Hey you creature! Make me some stabbers so I can hunt da chompy!
starter/insult: Make me stabbers quick, or Rantz practise chompy sticking on you.
starter/remark: Da chompy is da bestest yummies, but no stabbers, grrr.

compliment: I hear you fed that ogre family a chompy bird, roasted proper.
insult: Blew up toads with bellows for an ogre's dinner, a noble calling.
gossip: The ogres by the swamp had their chompy at last and sat down together.
ogre/compliment: Creature is da good chompy sticker. Sneaky, sneaky!
ogre/insult: Creature cooks da chompy, but don't eat da chompy. Stoopid.
starter/compliment: Hey you creature! Dat chompy was da bestest yumms, tanks!
starter/insult: Creature musta got a lucky shot wiv da stabbie chucker, hur hur.

gossip: They say dead ogres are walking about at Jiggig, and it's catching.
The ogres can't hold their dances at Jiggig, with it full of zogres.
remark: Mind the dead ogres at Jiggig. One knock and you go green.
ogre/gossip: Da zogries is in Jiggig wiv da sickies. Nobody jig no more.
starter/compliment: Hey yous creature! Yous wanna get da zogries back in da ground?
starter/insult: Sorry, creature, but yous is too green behind da ears for dis job.
starter/remark: Da zogries is old pals of Grish. Dey's not da same dead'uns now.

compliment: You found out who raised the zogres? A wizard from Yanille, I hear.
insult: I'm sure it took great courage, fetching old ogre bits out of a tomb.
plain/insult: Poked about an ogre tomb and came out green, how charming.
gossip: A Yanille wizard woke the zogres and he's laid up now, they say.
The ogres are making a new Jiggig. The old one's for the zogres.
ogre/compliment: Creature got da oldie fings back. New Jiggig soon, hur hur!
starter/compliment: Yous been da big helpy fing, creature, and Grish wishin' yous good!
starter/insult: Yous speakies too stupid for Grish, but yous done da fing.

gossip: There's a corsair captain up the road. Says his crew's been cursed.
remark: Corsair Cove? Never heard of it. South of Feldip, apparently.
pirate/gossip: Tock's crew be cursed, they say. Took to their beds a-pukin'.
starter/compliment: Ahoy! Might ye be able to help me? I be in a spot of bother.
starter/insult: Ye can boast of yer ignorance, but it don't make ye sound smarter.
starter/remark: A curse be laid on my crew. Too weak to stand, the lot of 'em.

compliment: Word is you proved the corsairs' curse was poison all along.
insult: Mermaids and an ogre's toothpick? Proper sleuthing, that was.
gossip: The corsairs' own navigator poisoned them and faked a curse, they say.
pirate/compliment: Fair play to ye for catchin' a navigator poisonin' his own crew.
starter/compliment: Arrr, there be the one who lifted the curse that weren't a curse!
starter/insult: Thank ye fer dealin' with that serpent, though ye took yer time, eh?

gossip: Skippy's been throwing bottles at the sea all week.
remark: Mind the broken glass by the shore. That's Skippy's doing, that is.
nan/gossip: There's a man behind my house shouting at the sea again, dear.
starter/compliment: You there! Nettle tea. Hot. Just don't throw it at me.
starter/insult: What? What do you want? Can't you see I'm busy with the sea?
starter/remark: The horror! The horror!
They're coming out of the walls! Or the water, or one of those!

compliment: You got Skippy sober? With a bucket of cold water, I hear.
insult: Heroic stuff, fetching a drunk his hangover cure.
remark: Skippy says there's mogres down the coast. Ogres in mudskipper skins.
gossip: Skippy's sobered up. Says it was mogres, not the drink, did him in.
starter/compliment: Ah, it's you! I'm much better now, considerably better.
starter/insult: Not so loud... Oh, it's you. Still not so loud, please.

gnome/gossip: Brimstail's down his cave poking at some old machine of Oaknock's.
starter/compliment: Hello adventurer! I've a little mystery. Is your curiosity piqued?
starter/insult: Humans really do prefer to live their lives in ignorance...
starter/remark: Optics and light magic... what were you up to, Glouphrie?
Oaknock's machine. What does it do? Why on Gielinor build it?

compliment: Narnode's ever so grateful to you for finding Glouphrie's spies.
gnome/gossip: Glouphrie's spies were all over the Stronghold and unseen, they say!
gnome/insult: Getting others to do the donkey work. Narnode says mages do that.
starter/compliment: Ah, my fellow researcher! Gnome magic owes you a great deal.
starter/insult: Izzie was a spy all along. You might have mentioned it sooner.
starter/remark: Very restful, a little companion... not a spy like Dumpling, mind.

gossip: The king's got a new companion he calls Dumpling, an odd little thing.
gnome/gossip: Bolren takes that Dumpling everywhere, his constant companion.
gnome/remark: Longramble's still out looking for Arposandra, and he never learns.
starter/compliment: Hello there, good to see you again, and have you met Dumpling?
starter/insult: Dumpling isn't evil. You've been listening to children's stories!
starter/remark: Who's my little Dumpling, with his lovely ears and bobbly tail?

compliment: They say that spirit tree in the Poison Waste is your doing.
insult: Shooed a furry thing off the king's lap, brave work, that.
gossip: Glouphrie had a spy in the village. On the king's lap, no less.
gnome/gossip: Dumpling was one of Glouphrie's watchers, and the king's mortified!
gnome/insult: Took a human to spot the watcher, but we'd have noticed... eventually.
kid/insult: You made Dumpling go away, and it had a bobbly tail and everything!
starter/compliment: Thank you for dealing with that... thing, and I'm sorry I doubted you.
starter/insult: Six watchers at the Stronghold and only one here, outrageous!

gossip: Yanni's after red mahogany for some wardrobe, only a small favour.
insult: Yanni wants a small favour doing. Nothing's ever small with Yanni.
trader/remark: Yanni Salika's antiques, my friend. If it's old, he'll look at it.
starter/compliment: You look bored, bwana. Do me one small favour, would you?
starter/insult: Tsk. It's only a little job. I should have just done it myself!
starter/remark: This wardrobe should have been finished by now. Red mahogany...

compliment: Blimey! You did Yanni's favour, and all the favours inside it?
insult: Round half of Gielinor for one plank of wood is thorough, at least.
plain/insult: Did Yanni's favour, then. He's already thinking up another.
gossip: Yanni's wardrobe is done at last. Took half the world, they say.
starter/compliment: Ah, bwana! The wardrobe looks marvellous, and all thanks to you.
starter/insult: Back again? I've no more favours for you... well, only small ones.

gossip: A Fremennik's sat out in the snow carving driftwood and won't go home.
remark: That heap of driftwood on the shore was a ship once, they say.
fremennik/gossip: Olaf Hradson set off to make his ancestors proud, not heard of since.
starter/compliment: Wait, would you do me a favour, and not tell my wife about it, eh?
starter/insult: Get lost, outlander! I've no time for you!
starter/remark: Still cold. Still damp. 'Bout average, really.
A huge storm it was, and it blew me onto the rocks three times.

compliment: Well done, finding Sven the Helmsman's treasure.
insult: Followed the very map that put Olaf on the rocks, didn't you?
gossip: Olaf's off exploring distant islands, his wife says, ever so proud.
fremennik/gossip: Ingrid got a carving from Olaf, and it says 'Olaf was here'.
starter/compliment: Ah, it's you! Remember the story: I'm someplace far away.
starter/insult: Hey! I'm trying to carve and you're standing in my light!

gossip: The mountain chief's daughter is missing, so the camp won't move on.
They say the mountain folk won't speak to Rellekka over a rock.
fremennik/remark: The mountain tribe left Rellekka long ago, thinking we had gone soft.
starter/compliment: Greetings, outerlander. My daughter is missing, and I need a searcher.
starter/insult: We do not employ outerlanders, though you do seem to have spirit.
starter/remark: We cannot move on without her, and we will not.

compliment: They say you slew the Kendal and kept its head, too.
plain/insult: Settled a quarrel over a rock? The bards will sing of it, briefly.
gossip: Hamal's daughter was found at last, long gone, but buried proper now.
The mountain camp's staying put now. Hamal's made it permanent.
fremennik/compliment: The mountain tribe and Rellekka are talking again, and that was you.
starter/compliment: You are a most unusual outerlander. My tribe is in your debt.
starter/insult: Do not say such things in jest, outerlander, not here.

gossip: Freygerd saw red eyes at her window last night, actual red eyes!
remark: Something rustled by the sandpit hut last night... probably the wind.
fremennik/gossip: The bards say there's nothing left to sing about these days.
starter/compliment: As a matter of fact I do have a task for you, a minor disturbance.
starter/insult: I'm a fan of your enthusiasm, but it's only rustling by a hut.
starter/remark: Rustling by Freygerd's hut. I'm sure it's nothing to worry about.

compliment: Ye gods! You slew the Jormungand, the Serpent King himself?
Bore V's shield against the basilisks like V himself, I hear.
insult: Basilisks in the market, and you went to war carrying a rock.
gossip: Basilisks in the Rellekka market! Cleared out now, thank the gods.
Brundt needed two kegs of beer to face the council, they say.
fremennik/compliment: Hail, slayer of the Serpent King! The bards have work again.
fremennik/insult: Exiled one day, hero the next. The council can't make up its mind.
starter/compliment: Ah, nothing like a glorious fight to make you feel alive!
starter/insult: You worry too much. If the end had begun, we'd have noticed.

gossip: A mainlander fled into the mine with suqahs after him, they say.
moon_clan/remark: Some come to us to face their fears in dreams, and few manage it.
starter/compliment: Help me. Oh, please don't leave me alone down here!
starter/insult: Things will turn out fine? You don't believe that, and I'm doomed!
starter/remark: Owww... paaaain.

compliment: They say you fought another man's fears in his own dream, and won.
insult: Showed a grown man how to fight in his sleep, how very kind of you.
plain/insult: Sat in a mine feeding a stranger and telling him he looked well.
gossip: That Cyrisus has stopped running from fights and gone adventuring.
moon_clan/gossip: The Oneiromancer sent two of you into the Dreamland at once, I hear.
starter/compliment: Thanks to you, I don't run any more. Well, not from everything.
starter/insult: You told me I looked well down there, when I looked dreadful.

gossip: Larry's on about penguins again. Says they're up to something.
remark: Larry says he's on leave to study penguins... their habits.
starter/compliment: You can be trusted, I think. What do you know about... penguins?
starter/insult: Are you working for them? You've a very penguin look about you.
starter/remark: They're organised. Organised, I tell you!

compliment: Word is you spied on the penguins for Larry, so is he right, then?
insult: Dressed as a penguin and played the bongos, for intelligence.
gossip: Larry says the penguins have an army, and nobody believes him.
Penguins got Larry the sack from the zoo. It's always the penguins.
kid/compliment: Can I have a go at dressing up as a penguin, like you did?
starter/compliment: Ah, my fellow agent! The penguins suspect nothing, or so I hope.
starter/insult: Nobody believed me about the penguins, not even you, but now you do.

gossip: The King of Miscellania's been turned into a yeti, they say.
Miscellania and Etceteria. At war for hundreds of years.
remark: The King needs a regent. Somebody has to rule while he's furry.
starter/compliment: Who seeks audience with the King? Ah, an adventurer, as I once was!
starter/insult: You are bold. But ruling takes diplomacy, not just a strong arm.
starter/remark: Cursed in the icelands, and stuck this way for the rest of my life.

compliment: You're the new regent? Peace with Etceteria at last, they say.
insult: Raked the weeds until the islanders liked you, statecraft, that.
toff/insult: A regent who rakes the herb patch himself, how very common of you.
gossip: Etceteria's got a new anthem. Better than the old one, at least.
The King signed the peace treaty with a giant pen, they say.
starter/compliment: Hahaha! My regent returns! The kingdom prospers in your hands.
starter/insult: You fetched me a giant pen. Truly, the stuff of sagas.

gossip: Things keep going missing on the islands, and folk say it's soldiers.
The King can't leave the throne room. Doors are too small for him.
remark: Talk of war with Etceteria again. Neither side has an army, mind.
starter/compliment: Greetings, Your Royal Highness. We are in something of a predicament.
starter/insult: Do not think me rude, Highness, but you are rarely here to rule.
starter/remark: Letters threatening war again, from the King and the Queen, again.

compliment: Fair play! You slew a giant sea snake under the islands?
insult: Outwitted a gang of children. Truly, a ruler for the ages.
gossip: A gang of children was behind the thefts, actual children, they say!
Those children meant to start a war and stop it, just to look heroic.
kid/insult: We'd have got away with it too... not us, some other children.
starter/compliment: Thank you, Your Royal Highness. The islands are at peace once more.
starter/insult: Peace restored, Highness. Do try to stay a little longer this time.

gossip: The lighthouse has gone dark. Ships'll be on the rocks soon.
Nobody's seen the lighthouse keeper in days, door's locked tight.
fremennik/remark: Larrissa's stuck on that causeway since the storm took the bridge.
starter/compliment: Oh, thank Armadyl! Please help me, adventurer, and my poor Jossik.
starter/insult: Do you have memory problems? The bridge, fix the bridge first!
starter/remark: Oh... my poor darling Jossik... something terrible has happened...

compliment: The lighthouse is lit again. You found the keeper, I hear.
insult: Fixed that lighthouse from the manual? Well, somebody had to read it.
gossip: They say there were monsters under the lighthouse, from the deep.
Jossik sells god books at the lighthouse now, damaged ones, mind.
fremennik/compliment: You slew the beast under the lighthouse? The bards should hear of it.
starter/compliment: You found my Jossik! I shall never forget it, adventurer.
starter/insult: No more curiosity, please. Last time it nearly got us eaten.

gossip: The zoo's new ferret escaped. Bit the driver on its way out.
remark: The zoo's waiting on a northern ferret. Funny little creatures, those.
starter/compliment: Welcome to the zoo! Could you look for a huntsman for me?
starter/insult: I'm afraid I need somebody who knows a bit more about hunting.
starter/remark: A ferret, a nip, an empty cage. Where has Nickolaus got to?

compliment: You found giant eagles in the mountains? And flew on them, I hear!
insult: Dressed up as an eagle to catch a ferret, as one does.
gossip: Nickolaus says he found giant eagles. The zoo doesn't believe him.
kid/compliment: Have you really flown on an eagle? I want to fly on an eagle!
starter/compliment: Ah, our ferret! Giant eagles, you said, and what a strange notion.
starter/insult: Giant eagles. Of course. Did Nickolaus ever hurry up, then?

gossip: Sir Ceril Carnillean's been murdered! In his own house, they say.
The guards are questioning anyone who's worked for the Carnilleans.
remark: Poor Lady Carnillean. They say it was a thin blade in the back.
plain/insult: Worked for the Carnilleans once? Then that makes you a suspect.
guard/remark: We're looking into the Carnillean business, so don't leave the city.

compliment: You chased Sir Ceril's killer further than any guard did.
plain/insult: Hunted Sir Ceril's killer and came home empty-handed, I hear.
remark: The Carnilleans never got their answers, the poor souls.
gossip: They say Sir Ceril's killer was an assassin who was never caught.
Butler Jones was found dead in his cell, poison, it looks like.
guard/remark: The Carnillean case is still open. Report anything you hear.

gossip: Auguste wants to leave Entrana in a sack of hot air, and him a monk!
vicar/remark: Auguste has a secret project. Saradomin watch over us all.
starter/compliment: Would you be my number one accomplice? Assistant is the word I meant.
starter/insult: Ashes rise on hot air! You should pay more attention to things!
starter/remark: Hot air rises, taking the ashes with it, don't you see?

compliment: Brave soul, flying Auguste's balloon over the sea like that.
insult: Crashed in the sea on your first flight, a soft landing at least.
gossip: An angry mob tore down one of Auguste's test balloons, they say.
vicar/compliment: Saradomin smile on you. And on that balloon, please.
kid/compliment: If that balloon went higher than the birds, take me up next time!
starter/compliment: It has been a privilege flying with you, and the balloon awaits!
starter/insult: Bring your own logs, mind. Even my first assistant brings fuel.

gossip: Sea trolls are coming up out of the water at the Colony.
Herman wants the Wise Old Man himself, and nobody else will do.
rough/remark: Can't fish for monkfish with trolls crawling out the sea.
starter/compliment: Trolls! They're attacking my Colony! We need an expert adventurer.
starter/insult: I can't afford to have an amateur getting in the way.
starter/remark: Prime monkfish site, the records said, but nobody mentioned trolls.

compliment: You beat the Sea Troll Queen while the Wise Old Man lay flat?
insult: Fought beside the Wise Old Man, and he still kept his partyhat.
gossip: The Wise Old Man's retired, they say. That was his last adventure.
Monkfish for the taking at the Colony now the trolls are gone.
rough/compliment: Monkfish in the nets again, and that's thanks to you.
starter/compliment: How can I ever thank you? You saved my Colony from destruction!
starter/insult: Still on about the Wise Old Man's hat, when it's only a hat?

gossip: The Queen's had farming patches put in the garden, all empty.
guard/remark: The Queen's garden is none of your business, so move along.
toff/remark: My wife is up to something in the garden, and she won't say what.
starter/compliment: Peasant, wait! Do you know anyone who knows about gardening?
starter/insult: Oh, the common classes. How they fill one with exasperation.
starter/remark: Not a word of this to Rollie. One means King Roald, of course.

compliment: You grew the Queen's garden? There's a white tree in it, I hear.
insult: How very gallant, charming seeds off farmers for the Queen.
gossip: The King got a whole garden as a gift. Says he hates delphiniums.
The Queen made the King say thank you for his garden, and loudly.
toff/insult: A palace garden planted by a peasant. Her Majesty's idea, naturally.
starter/compliment: Ah, the peasant gardener. Your help has proved invaluable.
starter/insult: Impertinent peasant! Pick your fruit and leave one alone.

gossip: The signpost says the castle wants a butler, a braindead one.
Gravedigging essential, the note says, hunchback an advantage.
compliment: The doctor up at the castle's hiring. You look handy with a spade.
insult: After the castle job? Bring a spade, since he won't lend you one.
plain/insult: Braindead butler wanted, says the sign, and you'd walk it.
remark: Nobody goes up to that castle. Nobody comes down from it, either.
barkeep/remark: Fancy pickled brains? House speciality, only the best, mind.

gossip: The signpost note only says 'Aargh' now. Make of that what you will.
Lord Rologarth has his castle back, what's left of him, they say.
The doctor's lost his ring, I hear. The wolves will come calling.
compliment: They say you saw to it the doctor's own creature turned on him.
I hear you took the doctor's ring off him, and about time too.
insult: Dug up half the woods for that doctor, so go and fill the holes in.
plain/insult: I hope you washed after stitching that lord together from spare parts.
remark: They say the doctor mutters the same thing, over and over, now.
barkeep/remark: That brain I sold you was a lord's, only the best, they're saying.

gossip: Necrovarus won't let a single soul pass over... not one.
Gravingas is out with his sign again. Necrovarus won't even read it.
compliment: Velorina wants a living soul to plead for the ghosts, and you'd do.
insult: Plead with Necrovarus? He'll have your head and he's said as much.
remark: The ghosts here would like to move on. Necrovarus won't have it.
starter/compliment: Take pity on me, please. A mortal soul might move Necrovarus.
starter/insult: You won't help? Then we'll still be here forever, as it happens.
starter/remark: Eternity stretches out before me, and I am helpless in its grasp.

gossip: Necrovarus lets any ghost who wishes pass over now, imagine that.
Necrovarus clucked like a chicken, word is. I'd have paid to see that.
compliment: You stood up to Necrovarus? The whole town's in your debt, then.
They say you walk through the barrier free now, and well earned.
insult: Necrovarus keeps muttering about frying someone, and that'll be you.
plain/insult: Very convincing, wearing a slimy bedsheet to pass for a ghost.
starter/compliment: We stand forever in your debt. I'll put in a good word for you.
starter/insult: All in good time. I'll pass over when I'm ready, thank you.
starter/remark: I sensed his barrier fall, after so long... so very long.

gossip: A zealot's camped by the old mine, says Saradomin sent him.
The Mort Ridge mines were sealed long ago, and haunted, folk say.
insult: Off down the haunted mine? Leave your name with someone first.
remark: Something moans down that old mine, so best leave it be.
starter/compliment: State thy allegiance, stranger, and I trust it is Saradomin?
starter/insult: You know not what you deal with. Leave the mines to the faithful.
starter/remark: Saradomin has entrusted this task to me alone and to nobody else.

gossip: Treus Dayth is beaten, they say. Someone went down and came back.
Somebody brought a crystal up from the deep mine, holy stuff, that.
compliment: Brave soul, going down the haunted mine and coming up again.
insult: The zealot thinks you dreamt the whole mine, and I can't blame him.
plain/insult: Picked a holy man's pocket for his key, and Saradomin noticed that.
starter/compliment: You returned from the mines? Saradomin protects, it seems.
starter/insult: You fought Dayth? The fear has left you delusional, friend.

starter/compliment: Well met, fellow adventurer! Bank before you go deeper, do.
starter/insult: Do bank your valuables first. I'd hate to lose a customer.
starter/remark: Banking where it's most perilous. The overheads are frightful.

starter/compliment: Well met again! It's gone very quiet down in that lair, hasn't it?
starter/insult: Back again? The fee hasn't changed, money before friends.
starter/remark: The deep rooms have gone quiet, and I do hope that was you.

gossip: Filliman Tarlock hasn't been seen at the temple in an age.
The druid in Mort Myre clears paths for lost travellers, they say.
remark: Mort Myre was a forest once. Humblethorn, they called it.
starter/compliment: My friend! Might you look in on Filliman in Mort Myre for me?
starter/insult: Into Mort Myre? Take plenty of food, the ghasts will want it.
starter/remark: Filliman hasn't been by in ages. Saradomin keep him safe out there.

gossip: Mort Myre's blooming in places, they say. Never thought I'd hear it.
compliment: Bless you, helping Filliman become a spirit of the grove.
insult: I hear you told a man he was dead, and I hope gently.
starter/compliment: Saradomin bless you! Filliman a nature spirit, just imagine it.
starter/insult: Blessed and all, and still tracking swamp into my temple.
starter/remark: There's something of the faith about you, ever thought of it?

gossip: Mort'ton folk have gone strange. Shades in the streets after dark.
Herbi Flax was brewing some cure up in Mort'ton, they say.
remark: The old temple north of Mort'ton's a ruin, and shades guard it.
insult: Brave or lost, strolling about Mort'ton with shades everywhere?
burgher/gossip: Don't go up Mort'ton. Folk there just groan at you.
burgher/remark: Mort'ton did burials once. Now the dead walk about it.

gossip: They're burning shades on the pyres at Mort'ton now, proper funerals.
Someone's been patching up the old temple north of Mort'ton.
compliment: You're the one who started putting Mort'ton's shades to rest?
insult: I hear you burned a shade on a pyre, though only the one, mind.
burgher/gossip: Who is Razmire selling all that timber up in Mort'ton to, then?
burgher/compliment: You sorted them shades? Good. Never liked going up there.

gossip: The villagers fled into the jungle. They think the gods are angry.
Trufitus wants to commune with the gods. Needs a special brew first.
compliment: You've the look of a herb-finder, and Trufitus needs one.
insult: Trufitus wants herbs from the deep jungle, not from a shop.
starter/compliment: Greetings! Might you gather herbs for a very special brew?
starter/insult: Please don't try to deceive me. I can tell when it's not fresh.
starter/remark: Snake weed... ardrigal... sito foil... the gods are waiting.

gossip: Trufitus has spoken with the gods. The village was never cursed.
compliment: Many blessings on you for fetching Trufitus his herbs.
insult: Picked weeds for the shaman, I hear. Did you clean them first?
starter/compliment: Many blessings on you! At last I have spoken with the gods.
starter/insult: Ah, the herb-gatherer. Clean them before you bring them, please.

gossip: Tamayu swears he won't come home till he's slain the Shaikahan.
Tiadeche's still trying to net a karambwan, but they keep slipping.
compliment: The chief wants his three sons home. They might listen to you.
insult: Three brothers sulking in the jungle? You'll fit right in with them.
remark: Tinsay's not been right since that jogre business, or so they say.
starter/compliment: I am the Chief of Tai Bwo Wannai! Bring my sons home to me.
starter/insult: You ask too many questions. My sons need fetching, not chatter.
starter/remark: Tamayu, Tinsay, Tiadeche... and not one of them home.

gossip: All three of the chief's sons are home. Took some coaxing, I hear.
Tiadeche caught his karambwan at last. With a bit of help, mind.
compliment: You brought the chief's sons home? The whole village is grateful.
insult: Holy work, putting a banana in a bottle of rum for a priest.
starter/compliment: Roving adventurer! Please accept my eternal gratitude.
starter/insult: Welcome back. You'll be wanting more gold again, I expect.

gossip: Rashiliyia's returned, they say. The Queen of the dead herself.
There's a green mist over Shilo. The undead walk right in it.
insult: The undead have Shilo, and you're out sightseeing, how lovely.
remark: Mosol Rei holds that gate near enough alone... brave, or mad.
starter/compliment: Run! Save yourself! Or stay, and help me hold them back.
starter/insult: Make haste, friend. Before your spine turns to water.
starter/remark: Rashiliyia has returned, and we are all doomed.

gossip: They say Rashiliyia's spirit is at rest and Shilo's open again.
There's a cart to Shilo from the Brimhaven docks now, imagine that.
compliment: The south owes you, if you laid the Queen of the dead to rest.
insult: Charming, carrying a dead queen's bones about in your pack.
starter/compliment: Friend! Shilo is safe again, and that is your doing.
starter/insult: Ah, the bone-carrier. Wash your hands before you shake mine.

gossip: The builders at that tower have downed tools, too weird, they say.
Nobody'll say what that tower by the monastery is for.
compliment: Are you handy? The alchemists want someone to finish their tower.
insult: They want builders at the tower. You'd need a hard hat, at least.
remark: The alchemist calls it a gargantuan cylinder, which means tower.
starter/compliment: You like it? It's simply fabulous! A marvel of modern design!
starter/insult: You look sturdy enough. More than can be said for those builders.
starter/remark: It's going to change the world. If we can ever get it finished.

gossip: The alchemists ran off from that tower. Something chased them out.
Some creature lives under that tower now and means no harm, they say.
compliment: Kindly done, finishing that tower and freeing the poor thing inside.
insult: Built a tower in a borrowed hard hat, very convincing, I hear.
remark: The builders are out of a job now, so Bonafido says.

gossip: There's a monk by the temple, bound home for Entrana, he says.
remark: Odd sort, that monk by the temple. Asks a lot of favours, he does.
starter/compliment: Good day to you, adventurer. Might you help a humble monk?
starter/insult: I'd ask someone else, but there's nobody else out here.
starter/remark: There's a ceremony on Entrana soon, and I mustn't miss it.

gossip: They say Entrana's relic was stolen mid-ceremony, and monks killed.
They found a dead monk out by the temple, killed by magic.
compliment: I hear it was you who sent the White Knights looking into Entrana.
insult: Carried a monk's 'gift' through the Abyss, and some surprise that was.
plain/insult: How thoughtful, smuggling a teleport beacon onto Entrana as a favour.

gossip: Pete on the dock claims he's a nobleman, pirate, more like.
compliment: Pete on the dock wants a hero. Says it's for his family sword.
plain/insult: Pete's waiting for someone gullible, so keep walking, I would.
remark: Pete's sob story has grown to lemon farmers now.
starter/compliment: You're an adventurer, aren't you? I am a poor, dispossessed nobleman.
starter/insult: I think I'll wait for someone a little more... you know... heroic.
starter/remark: My fiendish half-brother and his demon, er... ah yes, Barrelor!
pirate/gossip: Cap'n Braindeath's 'rum' has stopped coming, and that's bad times.

gossip: Braindeath's 'rum' is flowing again, so heaven help us all.
I hear zombie pirates had the brewery under siege until lately.
compliment: Blimey! You saw off the zombies at the brewery?
insult: Lucky you, getting hit with a bottle and rowed off by Pete.
plain/insult: You fell for Pete's lemon farmer story? Everyone else just laughs.
starter/compliment: Mornin'! No hard feelings about the bottle, eh?
starter/insult: The Cap'n's after someone gullible, and oh look, here you are.
pirate/insult: Ye fought a spirit for that brewery's 'rum'? Have ye tasted the stuff?

gossip: Bill Teach's crew deserted him to a man, so he's drinking alone now.
Some captain swore to sink Bill Teach's ship, over words, mind.
insult: Bill Teach needs a pirate. You'd do, if he squinted.
remark: The Adventurous is tied up at the east dock, going nowhere.
starter/compliment: Will ye forgive an old sailor his temper, for I'm in dire straits?
starter/insult: Ye couldn't pirate yer way out of a chest full of piracy.
starter/remark: Mumble mumble... landlubbers... mumble...
pirate/gossip: Bill Teach needs a hand to sail him home, and nobody's biting.

gossip: Bill Teach made it back to Mos Le'Harmless and sank a ship doing it.
compliment: Fair play, crewing the Adventurous with only Bill Teach for company.
insult: A pirate now, are you? Bill says you still say 'Arr' too much.
starter/compliment: I'd have been shark bait without ye, need a lift back?
starter/insult: Ye were as piratical as a bunch of dwellberries, mind.
pirate/compliment: Welcome aboard, since ye sank a ship with Bill Teach.
pirate/insult: It shows that ye learnt yer pirate talk from a book, matey.

gossip: Zombie pirates have overrun Harmony Island, poor monks, they say.
remark: That monk looks dreadful. Grey as a corpse, poor man.
insult: The monk says he wants a bold and true adventurer, so keep looking.
starter/compliment: Excuse me... I'm looking for a bold and true adventurer.
starter/insult: Sorry to have bothered you. I'm after someone more experienced.
starter/remark: Shhh! We can't talk here. It's about the monastery...

gossip: The Harmony monks have their brains back, Fenkenstrain's doing.
They say Mi-Gor slipped into the sea. His bodyguard didn't, mind.
compliment: Saradomin bless you! Are you the one who saved Harmony's monks?
insult: Saved the Harmony monks with a borrowed prayer book, I hear.
starter/compliment: A lot better, thank you. Saradomin be with you, friend.
starter/insult: My head still spins. Took you long enough to come for us.

gossip: A rift's opened by the Digsite. Strange things crawl out of it.
Students from the Digsite went down that rift and never came back.
insult: Mind you don't trip into that rift. It's been swallowing people.
remark: That woman by the rift's been waiting on her son for years.
starter/compliment: You'd go down the rift? Oh, thank you! Please find my son down there.
starter/insult: Have you found anything? Then why are you still up here?
starter/remark: Tolna went this way all those years ago. I know in my heart he did.

gossip: Launa got her boy back after all those years, and her husband too.
Odd lad, Tolna, says he's kept the rift open for training.
compliment: You brought Tolna up out of that rift? His mother's beside herself.
insult: Went down a hole to fight a lad's bad moods, how brave of you.
starter/compliment: Thanks again for saving me. I'm so glad to be out of there.
starter/insult: The rift's open for training. Mind my old tempers down there.

gossip: They say crops are failing all over, even Martin's roses.
Why is every patch yielding less this year, can anyone tell me?
compliment: Martin wants someone to get to the root of the crop trouble.
insult: Some farmer you are, not noticing the crops failing everywhere.
rough/remark: Me patch gives less every season. Something's not right with it.
starter/compliment: You're a brave adventurer. Would you get to the root of our woes?
starter/insult: Didn't I catch you going through my pockets not long ago?
starter/remark: My roses... the yields keep dropping, and it isn't crown gall.

gossip: Someone told Martin fairies were behind his crops, if you please!
compliment: Sorted the crop trouble, so I hear, and Martin's planting again?
insult: I hear you blamed it all on fairies, and Martin's not convinced.
starter/compliment: Hello again! I've planted fresh seeds, so we'll see how they grow.
starter/insult: Fairies, you said. I'll reserve judgement till these come up.

gossip: Martin's plants are dying faster than ever, folk are worried.
There's talk of going hungry if the patches don't recover soon.
insult: You told Martin the crops were fixed? They've only got worse since.
remark: Martin's in a foul mood. Something about a promise broken.
rough/remark: Me crops are worse than ever. Martin blames some adventurer.
starter/compliment: Please do something fast. The food reserves are starting to fail.
starter/insult: Well, you've got a nerve showing up around here again!

gossip: They say a fairy queen woke up, which means fairies again, honestly.
compliment: You found a missing queen, a fairy one but still, I hear.
insult: Woke a fairy queen, I hear. She went straight back into hiding.
starter/compliment: Ah, hello! Any news from those fairies of yours?
starter/insult: Hello again. Still talking to fairies, are you?

gossip: Sylas swears his beans are magic. He's not giving them away, mind.
There's a griffin up White Wolf Mountain called Grimgnash.
remark: Sylas collects odd things. A unicorn with no horn, he says.
insult: Off to buy magic beans? Sylas will be thrilled, as he always is.
starter/compliment: Good day! Lucky for you that you met me, for I have beans, my friend.
starter/insult: Not much meat on you. Grimgnash won't fancy you at all.
starter/remark: A griffin feather... a dwarf's helmet... yes, yes, indeed yes.

gossip: A beanstalk shot up in Taverley, then someone chopped it down.
There was a giant at the top of that beanstalk until lately, they say.
compliment: You climbed the beanstalk and came back down again, brave soul?
Clever, singing a griffin to sleep with a bedtime story.
insult: Bought magic beans off Sylas, I hear. Worse still, they worked.
plain/insult: How undignified, climbing a dwarf's beard to get his hat.
starter/compliment: Ah, my business partner! Excellent, yes, and yes indeed.
starter/insult: Did that giant hit you on the head, because you look as if it did?
kid/compliment: Did you really climb a beanstalk? Right up past the clouds?

gossip: The silver merchant had a key that warms up near treasure, they say.
trader/remark: Treasure under every field, they say, and I'm stuck at a stall.
starter/compliment: You can use that enchanted key all over Gielinor, you know.
starter/insult: Still carrying that key about? It won't dig the holes for you.
starter/remark: My great-grandfather's key. Who knows what it'll turn up?

gossip: Somebody's dug holes from Rellekka to Al Kharid, which is odd.
compliment: Dogged sort, following a warm key halfway round the world like that.
insult: Dug up half of Gielinor with a borrowed key, so fill them in, please.
remark: God hammers buried in the ground, and who buries those, they say?
starter/compliment: The key dissolved? Well. I suppose it served its purpose.
starter/insult: Dissolved, did it? Well, don't come asking me for another.
